title: NFL power rankings Week 3 see Raiders, Bengals, Vikings, Bills soar
description: NFL power rankings before Week 3 of season see Commanders, Buccaneers, Texans, Chargers, Falcons, Raiders, Bengals, Vikings, Bills among big movers.
fullText:
In our NFL power rankings after NFL Week 1, we gave our first impressions of each NFL team.

For our NFL power rankings after NFL Week 2, we are sharing our second thoughts on those initial notions.

And some NFL teams gave us plenty of reasons to have second thoughts on our original perceptions in our NFL Week 3 power rankings.

Check out how we rank every NFL team in our NFL power rankings before NFL Week 3, with the Dallas Cowboys, Denver Broncos, New Orleans Saints and Carolina Panthers among the NFL teams to change our opening ideas for the better and the Pittsburgh Steelers, Baltimore Ravens, Jacksonville Jaguars and Chicago Bears among those to change our introductory beliefs for the worse after NFL Week 2.

Where is every team in our Week 3 NFL power rankings? Previous ranking in parentheses. Return after the Rams vs. Giants game on Monday Night Football for updated rankings.

Watch NFL games on FUBO (free trial)

Malik Willis was 14-for-23 for 197 yards and one touchdown in the loss to the 49ers. The Dolphins have the Chiefs, Vikings and Bengals up next. When do they win their first game? It might be a while.

NFL Week 2: Lost to San Francisco 49ers, 35-13 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Kansas City Chiefs (Sept. 27)

The Titans almost beat the Eagles, allowing a touchdown pass with nine seconds left. We don't believe in moral victories, but sometimes a team has to take anything it can get. A real win will come for Cam Ward and Tennessee, eventually.

NFL Week 2: Lost to Philadelphia Eagles, 24-20 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At New York Giants (Sept. 27)

It's hard to judge the Falcons with Cooper Rush as their starting QB, but the results have not been good. Bijan Robinson can't do everything for Atlanta. The good news? Atlanta plays in the NFC South, which always seems wide open.

NFL Week 2: Lost to Carolina Panthers, 34-3 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At Green Bay Packers (Sept. 24)

Who had Deshaun Watson and the Browns beating the Buccaneers? A week after we said it was going to be a long season in Cleveland, the Browns evened their record at 1-1. We don't see Cleveland competing for the AFC North title, but maybe the season won't be that long.

NFL Week 2: Beat Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 23-19 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Carolina Panthers (Sept. 27)

What changed? NFL power rankings Week 2 shaken up with Bears, 49ers, Cardinals wins

Arizona looked great after Week 1 and after it tied Seattle, 7-7, at halftime, in Week 2. But it allowed 24 unanswered points and had only 151 yards of total offense against the Seahawks. That isn't going to cut it. Was Week 1 an anomaly? The schedule is tough, and the results might be difficult for Cardinals fans to see.

NFL Week 2: Lost to Seattle Seahawks, 31-7 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At San Francisco 49ers (Sept. 27)

New York came back to earth after its Week 1 win with a very Jet-like performance in Week 2. Still, this team is better than we thought it would be before the season.

NFL Week 2: Lost to Green Bay Packers in overtime, 20-17 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At Detroit Lions (Sept. 27)

We had high hopes for Washington with Jayden Daniels' return this season, but the Commanders are now 0-2 and Daniels left Week 2. Is another long season coming for Washington? It sure looks like it right now. The upcoming schedule is brutal.

NFL Week 2: Lost to Dallas Cowboys, 37-20 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Seattle Seahawks (Sept. 27)

It looks like the Buccaneers' offense misses Mike Evans. It has fewer than 400 yards passing in two games, with the scary Vikings defense up next. Is it a must-win game for Tampa Bay?

NFL Week 2: Lost to Cleveland Browns, 23-19 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Minnesota Vikings (Sept. 27)

We thought the Chargers could be a contender in the AFC this season. We are rethinking that stance after losses to the Cardinals and Raiders. It's been only two weeks, but Justin Herbert and company do not look like playoff contenders.

NFL Week 2: Lost to Las Vegas Raiders, 26-14 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At Buffalo Bills (Sept. 27)

The Colts' loss on Sunday Night Football brought the AFC South to 1-7 two weeks into the season. Ouch. The loser of the Texans vs. Jaguars game in NFL Week 3 will be 0-3, but you can't count an 0-3 team out in that division.

NFL Week 2: Lost to Kansas City Chiefs in overtime, 33-30 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Houston Texans (Sept. 27)

Aaron Rodgers was 23-for-39 for 187 yards, with an interception in Week 2. Pittsburgh has a solid defense, but it won't be able to compete in the AFC North without more on offense.

NFL Week 2: Lost to New England Patriots, 20-3 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Cincinnati Bengals (Sept. 27)

Where is Houston's running game? The Texans had 18 rushes for 60 yards in the loss to the Bengals, while C.J. Stroud threw 55 pass attempts, only completing 30. The defense doesn't look that formidable anymore, either. It's only two games, but it doesn't look good for Houston.

NFL Week 2: Lost to Cincinnati Bengals, 20-6 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At Indianapolis Colts (Sept. 27)

Maybe we were too rough on the Panthers after their Week 1 loss to the Bears. Carolina's defense went from allowing 59 points to giving up three. Bryce Young appears to have taken a big step forward. The NFC South could be there for the taking in 2026.

NFL Week 2: Beat Atlanta Falcons, 34-3 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At Cleveland Browns (Sept. 27)

The Saints are a two-point conversion attempt away from being 2-0. Tyler Shough's development has been fast, and the NFC South suddenly seems in play for New Orleans this season.

NFL Week 2: Beat Baltimore Ravens, 24-17 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Las Vegas Raiders (Sept. 27)

Who saw this coming? Kirk Cousins and the Raiders are 2-0. And this is without Brock Bowers. It helps when Tre Tucker has five catches for 119 yards and a touchdown. The schedule is about to get a lot more difficult. Will Las Vegas be brought back down to Earth?

NFL Week 2: Beat Los Angeles Chargers, 26-14 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At New Orleans Saints (Sept. 27)

This team is so close to being 0-2. But it's not. Jordan Love and company somehow won a game where they had 199 yards of total offense and went 1-for-9 on third down. That won't cut it against most opponents, but it worked against New York.

NFL Week 2: Beat New York Jets in overtime, 20-17 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Atlanta Falcons (Sept. 24)

Where was this offense in Week 1? Dak Prescott was 26-for-31 for 279 yards, with four touchdown passes. That will do. That will also make Dallas a threat in the NFC East.

NFL Week 2: Beat Washington Commanders, 37-20 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Baltimore Ravens (Sept. 27 in Rio de Janeiro)

The Giants visit the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football in NFL Week 2.

NFL Week 2: At Los Angeles Rams (Sept. 21)

NFL Week 3: Tennessee Titans (Sept. 27)

After scoring 59 points in Week 1, the Bears were held to 3 in Week 2, with Caleb Williams' injury looming large in Chicago. Can the Bears challenge for the NFC North title if he misses a lot of time?

NFL Week 2: Lost to Minnesota Vikings, 9-3 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Philadelphia Eagles (Sept. 28)

The Patriots' defense absolutely smothered Aaron Rodgers in this game. Good thing, too, because the offense just doesn't look right. The defense (16 points allowed in two games) might keep New England in the AFC East race.

NFL Week 2: Beat Pittsburgh Steelers, 20-3 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At Jacksonville Jaguars (Sept. 27)

It's hard to win at Empower Field at Mile High, as the Jaguars found out. Just how good is Jacksonville? We're about to find out with the Patriots, Bengals and Eagles up next. One positive? The Jags are in the AFC South, so they are never out of it.

NFL Week 2: Lost to Denver Broncos, 20-13 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: New England Patriots (Sept. 27)

Jaylen Waddle had eight catches for 138 yards against the Jaguars. That impresses us. So did Denver's defense bouncing back in a big way from Week 1. This Broncos team is dangerous in the AFC West and the AFC.

NFL Week 2: Beat Jacksonville Jaguars, 30-20 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Los Angeles Rams (Sept. 27)

Jared Goff and the Lions never gave up in a short week against a team opening a new stadium. We still think Detroit will have a big say in the NFC North this season.

NFL Week 2: Lost to Buffalo Bills, 41-31 (Sept. 17)

NFL Week 3: New York Jets (Sept. 27)

Saquon Barkley's status looms large over Philadelphia, but the Eagles are 2-0 and looking like the favorite in the NFC East again. It helps to have Jalen Hurts at QB.

NFL Week 2: Beat Tennessee Titans, 24-20 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At Chicago Bears (Sept. 28)

It might not matter who plays QB for the Vikings, this Minnesota defense just might give it a chance in every game. Dallas Turner has been unstoppable.

NFL Week 2: Beat Chicago Bears, 9-3 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At Tampa Bay Buccaneers (Sept. 27)

The Joe Burrow to Ja'Marr Chase connection still works, but it is Cincinnati's defense that has us thinking the Bengals could be the new favorite in the AFC North.

NFL Week 2: Beat Houston Texans, 20-6 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At Pittsburgh Steelers (Sept. 27)

The Rams host the New York Giants on Monday Night Football in NFL Week 2.

NFL Week 2: New York Giants (Sept. 21)

NFL Week 3: At Denver Broncos (Sept. 27)

The Ravens were outscored 15-0 in the fourth quarter in Week 2, with Lamar Jackson throwing a late interception to seal the loss. This team could still challenge for the AFC title, but it has work to do on defense and offense.

NFL Week 2: Lost to New Orleans Saints, 24-17 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: Dallas Cowboys (Sept. 27 in Rio de Janeiro)

It wasn't pretty, but the Chiefs moved to 2-0 with the overtime win over the Colts and now sit atop the AFC West with the 2-0 Raiders. Kansas City started 0-2 in 2025, but appears ready to contend again in 2026.

NFL Week 2: Beat Indianapolis Colts in overtime, 33-30 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At Miami Dolphins (Sept. 27)

No Sam Darnold, no problem? Drew Lock went 19-for-26 for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the win over the Cardinals. Seattle's defense allowed only 151 total yards. Yeah, this team could repeat as Super Bowl champions.

NFL Week 2: Beat Arizona Cardinals, 31-7 (Sept. 20)

NFL Week 3: At Washington Commanders (Sept. 27)

The Bills have given up 62 points this season, but Josh Allen and company have scored 77 in a 2-0 start. This team appears to be a bigger Super Bowl contender than we first thought.

NFL Week 2: Beat Detroit Lions, 41-31 (Sept. 17)

NFL Week 3: Los Angeles Chargers (Sept. 27)

This team is on the rise. The 49ers scored touchdowns on their first five possessions and look like they were underestimated in preseason Super Bowl odds and rankings. Brock Purdy and company could contend for the NFC title.

NFL Week 2: Beat Miami Dolphins, 35-13 (Sept. 20)

title: Green Bay Packers hit with nightmare injury sequence as two players leave on carts
description: The Green Bay Packers endured a nightmare opening to their Week 2 matchup with the New York Jets, losing two players to injuries on consecutive plays. Both players needed to be taken off the field in a cart after going down. Jayden Reed was the first player to leave the field, with the Packers gathering [...]
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers endured a nightmare opening to their Week 2 matchup with the New York Jets, losing two players to injuries on consecutive plays. Both players needed to be taken off the field in a cart after going down.

Jayden Reed was the first player to leave the field, with the Packers gathering around him as the cart arrived following a concerning neck injury. The Athletic's Matt Schneidman reported that Reed was taken to the locker room shortly after the incident.

The entire Packers sideline is on the field with the cart coming out for Jayden Reed pic.twitter.com/vtd3Vnh8jG

— Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) September 20, 2026

On the ensuing play, Packers offensive lineman Zach Bako-Bewele was also taken off the field on a cart, according to Schneidman. Trainers secured his leg in an air cast before bringing him back to the locker room.

The Packers quickly ruled both players out for the rest of the game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that, "The #Packers have ruled out WR Reed (neck) and RT Zach Bako-Bewele (knee)."

Reed was injured after making a four yard reception and taking a hard hit to the head from Jets linebacker Demario Davis as he was brought down.

Bako-Bewele went down on the very next snap, forcing the Packers to bring out the medical staff. Trainers placed his leg in an air cast before he was taken off the field, indicating the injury may be serious, though Green Bay will need to provide the official diagnosis.

title: Celtic Told Martin O’Neill Wants to Stay Despite Poor Run
description: Celtic have been told that Martin O’Neill still has the energy to continue as the club’s manager despite the team’s recent poor run.The Hoops are not only coming off a 1-0 defeat in the most recent derby on Sunday in the Scottish Premiership, but they also lost their opening match in the UEFA Europa League […] The post Celtic Told Martin O’Neill Wants to Stay Despite Poor Run appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Celtic have been told that Martin O'Neill still has the energy to continue as the club's manager despite the team's recent poor run.

The Hoops are not only coming off a 1-0 defeat in the most recent derby on Sunday in the Scottish Premiership, but they also lost their opening match in the UEFA Europa League against Ferencvaros, leaving a terrible impression, and suffered a resounding 0-3 defeat against Rangers in the first edition of this season's Old Firm Derby in the Scottish League Cup quarterfinals, being eliminated from the competition prematurely.

This situation has generated both strong and harsh criticism of coach O'Neill, and although the Irishman is considered a club legend, some fans would prefer he resign to stop damaging his reputation.

In any case, following Sunday's defeat against Rangers, Neil Lennon, who has always said that he considers O'Neill to be something of a father figure, has told Sky Sports (h/t Daily Record) that the Irishman still has the energy to continue in charge and that this is what he wants to happen, but that it is normal for him to be under pressure in situations like these.

He said, "Martin is clearly hurting; he's smarting about it. The break has come at a good time for him; he can recuperate, get some sun. He still feels he's got the energy to do it, but when you get a week like this, you'll come under a lot of scrutiny."

Next up for Celtic, they will have a much-needed break due to the September and first-week-of-October international break, but next month will be very busy, with six matches on the calendar starting Oct. 11, when they visit Motherwell for Matchweek 8 of the Scottish Premiership.

On Oct. 15, they will visit Benfica for another matchday of the UEFA Europa League, and just three days later, they will host Hearts at Celtic Park for Matchweek 9 of the league.

On Oct. 22, they will host Celta Vigo for Matchday 3 of the Europa League, before visiting Hibernian for Matchweek 10 of the league on Oct. 24. They will finish the month on Oct. 28, when they host Dundee United for Matchweek 11 of the Scottish Premiership.

The coming days will be key for the club's board, coaching staff, and sporting management to act on the remainder of the season. Let's see what happens.

title: Sixers 3 goals: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope needs to spark the bench unit
description: Philadelphia 76ers veteran Kentavious Caldwell-Pope needs to bring a spark to the bench unit in an effort to help the team grow.
fullText:
In this new series, Sixers Wire looks at the 16 players, per Spotrac, that comprise the Philadelphia 76ers roster — 14 under standard contracts and the two players on two-way deals — and gives each three goals for the 2026-27 season.

The new season begins on Oct. 20, and training camp is right around the corner. Now is the time to begin previewing the new season of adventure that is Sixers basketball.

Up next in this series is veteran addition Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. The Sixers signed the 13-year man, and 2-time champion, out of Georgia to a deal shortly after landing LeBron James and KCP is expected to bring a lot of experience and shooting to this bench unit. He averaged 8.4 points, 2.7 assists, and 2.5 rebounds for the Memphis Grizzlies in 2025-26.

For Caldwell-Pope, his three goals are as follows:

Caldwell-Pope has been around and seen a lot in this league. The veteran won titles with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020 and the Denver Nuggets in 2023 so he knows what it takes. He knows there will be ups and downs throughout the season, and while the Sixers have plenty of veterans they can turn to in those down moments, Caldwell-Pope has to be the one to settle down a second unit full of younger players. He is somebody who can do a number of different things whether it's a hustle play, knocking down the 3-pointer, or making plays for others. His voice and productivity will be important in the coming season.

Speaking of that 3-pointer, KCP's percentages haven't been great in his previous two seasons. After shooting 40.6% from deep for the Nuggets in 2023-24, that percentage dropped to 34.2% with the Orlando Magic in 2024-25, and then down to 31.6% for the Grizzlies in 2025-26. Granted, the situations with the Magic and Grizzlies were tough as he played for a team that didn't have the shooters and playmakers he played with in Denver, and he could find that touch again in Philadelphia when considering the talent around him now. His 3s will be essential for Philadelphia's success.

Another big aspect Caldwell-Pope brings to the table is his defensive ability. He is someone who really digs in and gets after it on that end of the floor and the Sixers could really use somebody who can step in and produce on both ends of the floor. If Philadelphia can get some legitimate 3-and-D play out of Caldwell-Pope, then the second unit becomes one of the better ones in the league. He is somebody who can adequately defend his man on the perimeter while also being able to switch onto a bigger player if needed.

title: Celtic struggling to be 'on same script' - Carter-Vickers
description: Celtic centre-half Cameron Carter-Vickers has admitted it has been difficult to get all their summer signings "on the same script" but expressed confidence in their squad despite three damaging defeats in a row that have called into question the future of manager Martin O'Neill.  The 74-year-old veteran team boss wondered if it is time "to wrap it up" as he headed into the international break pondering his position at the Scottish Premiership leaders following Sunday's 1-0 defeat by Rangers.
fullText:
Celtic centre-half Cameron Carter-Vickers has admitted it has been difficult to get all their summer signings "on the same script" but expressed confidence in their squad despite three damaging defeats in a row that have called into question the future of manager Martin O'Neill.

The 74-year-old veteran team boss wondered if it is time "to wrap it up" as he headed into the international break pondering his position at the Scottish Premiership leaders following Sunday's 1-0 defeat by Rangers.

But Carter-Vickers told Sky Sports: "I agree with the manager - I don't think there was much in the game. Neither team were particularly good. There's a lot we can improve on, but I'm confident in the group we have."

Asked why Celtic's season had taken a downturn with two losses to their city rivals either side of Europa League defeat by Ferencvaros, the United States international added: "Hard to put your finger on one thing.

"We played a bit too random. We need to get better at that, getting a script and sticking to it.

"The last two games we've played have been big pressure games. As players, you rely on having something to fall back on.

"We haven't had the time to get that. As players, we can do better for sure. It's something we can improve on.

"There's a lot of new players at the club. It's about getting everyone on the same script. The group are together like we've always been. We need to find consistency."

title: What is Yankees’ Aaron Judge facing? Surgeon weighs in on possible return, calf re-injury risk
description: A sports surgeon details when Yankees captain Aaron Judge might be able to return from a calf strain.
fullText:
NEW YORK — The Yankees surely were in a somber mood during Sunday night's cross-country flight from Phoenix to New York. The AL East race is all but over and Aaron Judge is hurt again, this time potentially for the season.

The Diamondbacks prevailed 5-3 on Saturday night and 8-4 on Sunday afternoon, costing the Yankees two more games in the standings and leaving them six games behind with seven games remaining in the regular season.

Following Monday's off day, the first-place Rays will be in the Bronx for four games in three days at Yankee Stadium, which will probably lead to champagne corks popping in the visiting clubhouse. The Rays need just one win to clinch the AL East.

At this point, the Yankees will inevitably face the Red Sox a week from Tuesday in Game 1 of a Wild Card Series.

The mystery is whether Judge will be back for this best-of-three.

1. The three-time MVP is back on the injured list with a right calf strain less than two weeks after returning from a fractured rib that sidelined him for 88 games.

2. The strain is in the soleus muscle.

3. He's eligible to be activated for next Sunday's regular-season finale, game 162.

How bad is it? What did the MRI reveal?

As usual, the Yankees and Judge have remained guarded/secretive about revealing his injury and rehab details.

"It doesn't matter what the grade is," manager Aaron Boone said last Friday in Phoenix. "We're going to get him back or we're not. That's what we're going to work to do and we'll see.''

Judge basically said the same thing to Yankees media on Saturday, while adding, "I'd like to be back for the playoffs. That's definitely the plan."

What can we unpack from what little we know?

NJ.com consulted with an NYU Langone Health sports orthopedic surgeon to provide a clearer picture of what Judge is facing without knowing if the strain is a Grade 1 (mild), Grade 2 (moderate partial tear) or Grade 3 (severe complete rupture).

"If it's a Grade 1, in two weeks you could see Judge doing baseball activities again and then three weeks back playing," Dr. Spencer Stein said. "It's a calf muscle strain and they're annoying injuries."

Judge was injured during last Wednesday's game in Minnesota, so three weeks would be Oct. 7. If the Yankees win their Wild Card Series, that would be Game 3 of their best-of-five Division Series with the Rays.

"But that's really best-case scenario," Dr. Stein said. "That would be the fastest."

Yankees designated hitter Giancarlo Stanton went on the IL in April with a Grade 1 calf strain and still hasn't returned. He had a setback in June, and then while rehabbing, he strained his other calf in August.

If Judge rushes back, he'd also be risking a setback, the doctor warned.

"I've seen studies there's up to 50% chance of re-injury in these muscular injuries — hamstring injuries, calf muscle injuries," Dr. Stein said. "There's a high rate of retear, so it's definitely a balance of not going back too quickly on them."

Rushing back might be why Judge is hurt again. When he was out with his rib injury, he was shut down from baseball activities from June 1 until Aug. 19. Less than three weeks later, Judge was back from the IL and playing right field for the Yankees with no rehab games and a few live batting-practice at-bats packed into a workout the day before his first game back.

"Well, I would say that there should always be a stepwise return to sports where you build things up and that takes time," Dr. Stein said. "When you're under a time constraint because it's end of season and the playoffs are around the corner, sometimes you have to take a risk and go a little faster. But with a risk, you can end up with another injury."

The location of his calf strain is problematic.

"The gastrocnemius, plantaris and soleus muscles comprise the calf, and the soleus muscle is a push-off muscle and part of the Achilles tendon," Dr. Stein said. "There's just a lot of force in that area, a lot of strain and stress, especially when you're swinging a baseball bat."

If Judge returns, he'd be much better off DHing instead of playing right field, Dr. Stein added.

"No question," he said. "The soleus muscle constantly is engaged during simple standing and walking."

That's another risk the Yankees would have to take.

Judge would have to play right field rather than be the designated hitter. Ben Rice, who has 39 home runs and 95 RBI, is entrenched at DH, while Luis Garcia Jr. and Paul Goldschmidt form a potent first base first-base platoon

Here is Dr. Stein's advice for Judge:

"Follow the instructions and take it day-by-day. Work with the therapists and trainers. Make sure your strength is there. You don't want to rush it too much. You don't want a long-term injury that keeps happening.

"You want to be able to come back, and we get that, but you do want to meet the criteria: Good strength with a good amount of flexibility in the knee and ankle area."

title: Iowa vs Michigan | Odds, injuries, predictions, storylines
description: Everything you need to know for Iowa football vs. Michigan game, including time, TV channel, injury updates, betting odds, predictions and storylines.
fullText:
Iowa football and Michigan will face off Saturday, Sept. 26 at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor.

The Hawkeyes won their first three games of the season, all at home, against Northern Illinois, Iowa State and Northern Iowa. Michigan is 3-0 after beating Western Michigan, Oklahoma and UTEP.

Kickoff for Iowa vs. Michigan is set for 2:30 p.m. CT in Week 4 of the college football season.

Whether you're looking for kickoff information, injury updates, betting odds or score predictions, this guide has everything you need to know before the Hawkeyes and Wolverines take the field.

We'll update this story throughout the week with the latest injury news, coach comments, line movement and game-day developments leading up to kickoff.

Location: Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor

Spread: Michigan -4.5 (DraftKings odds as of Sunday night)

Over/Under: 37.5 (DraftKings odds as of Sunday night)

The Hawkeyes and Wolverines are scheduled to kick off at 2:30 p.m. CT on Saturday, Sept. 26 at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor.

CBS will televise the Hawkeyes-Wolverines matchup. The game can be streamed via Fubo.

Michigan is favored by 4.5 points

Money line: Michigan -198, Iowa +164

Iowa football tight end DJ Vonnahme missed the Hawkeyes' Sept. 19 home game vs. UNI due to an injury, but head coach Kirk Ferentz was optimistic that he would return for the Michigan game.

Bryce Hawthorne was banged up on an illegal block vs. UNI but Ferentz said he seemed fine after the game.

Running backs Kamari Moulton missed the UNI game but is expected back for Michigan. Running back LJ Phillips also might be available.

Iowa is 3-0 but two of those games were against overmatched non-Power 4 opponents. The No. 17 Hawkeyes barely got past an Iowa State team that was picked to finish last in the Big 12.

No. 18 Michigan escaped against Western Michigan 13-12 in a controversial finish before notching a quality win against Oklahoma.

We'll learn a lot about the Hawkeyes and Wolverines on Saturday.

The 17th-ranked Hawkeyes begin a grueling stretch (at Michigan, vs. Ohio State, at Washington) with an impressive victory at the Big House to move to 4-0. Iowa 21, Michigan 14

title: Big 12 football rushing yardage leaders after Week 3

fullText:
Iowa State's Aiden Flora had the best game of the week among Big 12 running backs with 194 rushing yards and two touchdowns on just 12 carries, averaging over 16 yards per carry. His electric performance moved him into a tie with BYU's LJ Martin for the top rushers in the Big 12.

West Virginia also has an elite running back duo. Quarterback Avery Johnson with Kansas State also had himself quite a day in the Wildcats' win over Tulane. Johnson was their leading rusher with 12 carries for 152 yards and two touchdowns after barely having 100 rushing yards in their first two games combined.

title: Antoine Semenyo surprised by Man City plan to use him as Erling Haaland back-up
description: Semenyo scored twice in Manchester City’s 5-3 win over Sunderland – and is ready to play striker if needed
fullText:
Antoine Semenyo has said he is happy to be Manchester City's Plan B as a centre-forward this season – even though he suggested they are yet to tell him about it.

After Omar Marmoush joined Tottenham, City are aiming to use the Ghanaian as a striker when Erling Haaland is not on the pitch.

The versatile Semenyo has operated as both a left winger and a right winger since arriving from Bournemouth and showed his finishing ability by scoring his first goals of the season with a brace in Sunday's 5-3 win over Sunderland.

And he said: "I've heard about his back-up striker thing. I don't know where it's come from, but if I need to, then I'll do it. I've no problem in doing that."

With Semenyo and Haaland rested, teenager Floyd Samba played as the centre-forward in Thursday's 5-0 victory over Norwich in the Carabao Cup.

Semenyo believes new manager Enzo Maresca's style of football suits wingers like him as he savoured the start to a new era.

"I've enjoyed it," he added. "I think for wide players, we're high and wide, and we get a lot of one-v-one situations, and he backs us to win our duels, even if you lose them, just keep going. But collectively, it's quite similar to last year and we just need to keep improving."

City have made a 100 per cent start to the Premier League season and have won their last seven games in all competitions.

And Semenyo said: "Everyone feels good. It's where we want to be. We're not going to get too complacent, too relaxed. We know that there's a lot more games to go. And we just want to continue winning."

title: Chiefs DL Chris Jones defends teammate Harrison Butker against critics
description: During his press conference, Kansas City Chiefs defensive lineman Chris Jones defended teammate Harrison Butker against critics | @EdEastonJr
fullText:
Kansas City Chiefs defensive lineman Chris Jones spoke with reporters after the Week 2 overtime victory over the Indianapolis Colts. He defended teammate Harrison Butker against his critics.

"Listen, they talk about my kicker y'all as a whole down my kicker last year, and I just got two middle fingers to y'all," said Jones. "I love Butt (Harrison Butker), and I trust in Butt, and I think Butt is the best kicker in the league. And I'm gonna continue to support my kicker."

Butker converted four of five field goal attempts in the victory, including two in overtime.

"Listen, nobody is perfect. Even though we want Butt to make them all, sometimes you're not, and it's just the cycle of life, and that's where adversity comes in," said Jones. "That's why I support Butt: he stands tall every time, faces it like a man, and (I) give two middle fingers to anybody who doubts my kicker."

Butker faced criticism last season for early inconsistency but remains one of the most clutch kickers in NFL history.

This article originally appeared on Chiefs Wire: Chiefs DL Chris Jones defends teammate Harrison Butker against critics

title: Leeds 0-0 Crystal Palace - the fans' verdict
description: Ian: Leeds battled hard and could have easily lost.  On another day, we may have had a first-half penalty, but Palace turned up and gave better than we did.  Leeds will be top half and perhaps challenging for Europe with a little luck.
fullText:
We asked for your thoughts after Sunday's Premier League game between Leeds United and Crystal Palace.

Here are some of your comments:

Ian: Leeds battled hard and could have easily lost. Lots of mistakes all over the pitch and nobody really stood out. Substitutes added nothing. Thought there should have been a straight red in the first few minutes when Ampadu was kicked in the head. On another day, we may have had a first-half penalty, but Palace turned up and gave better than we did.

Thomas: Very tight game, with Palace creating more chances, but I think Dominic Calvert-Lewin will be disappointed with missing the fantastic opportunity he had to settle the match. Didn't really create much so a draw was a fair result

Hillsy: Sometimes it's more difficult when you're expected to win against a side lower on quality but possessing great grit, so it's important to be defensively resilient. Leeds will be top half and perhaps challenging for Europe with a little luck.

Richard: Lacklustre at best against a team supposedly tired from European adventures. Never mind - three weeks at least in the top five and most Leeds fans would have given an arm and a leg for that back in August.

James: The Eagles' best league performance to date. Quality starting to show. Important that Sarr gets a start soon to sharpen attack. Defence looking solid. Wharton not quite there yet but not far off.

Hughie: The positivity generated on Thursday carried through. Defensively, we needed that clean sheet and there was a better balance in midfield with more targets for Wharton to pass forward to. A very encouraging performance against a very competitive Leeds side. I'm happy with the point.

Steve: Palace are certainly showing signs of improvement with some delightful one-touch patterns of play. The defence restricted a dangerous Leeds attack to very few opportunities, which was great to see. With more clinical finishing, the much-improved second-half display deserved all three points. The future is definitely looking brighter with every game.

Gary: A greatly improved defensive performance and I'm loving the way we are attacking. We always look dangerous and are creating chances. Two clean sheets is very much a positive and, if we can improve further after the international break, I have high hopes for the rest of the season.

title: Tennessee Titans' Robert Saleh: 'There's no moral victories'
description: Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh says there are no moral victories after a narrow loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
fullText:
The Tennessee Titans played a strong game against the Philadelphia Eagles but fell 24-20 in Week 2. While Tennessee played better this week and had a lot more positives than negatives, it still wasn't enough.

The Titans still have issues in their secondary and too often gave up chunk plays on critical money downs, which again led to a time-of-possession disparity. Cam Ward and the offense were better, but came up short.

Following the game, head coach Robert Saleh gave an honest assessment of the afternoon.

#Titans HC Robert Saleh on his message to the team following the loss #TitanUp pic.twitter.com/jJYmg6Apt3

"There's no moral victories. There's going to be things that we've got to improve on. Like I told our team, we're going to be sick when we watch this tape, because we should be 1-1 right now. But we're not, and that's credit to Philly. They executed. It sucks. Whether you lose by 100 or in the last second, it doesn't matter; they all suck."

He's absolutely right; the Eagles executed, and Tennessee has a lot to work on heading into Week 3. While there were some good things, their inability to get off the field on third down should be a major focus heading into their matchup with the New York Giants, and who knows, maybe they can pull off their first win of 2026.

title: Notre Dame football: Three ways to fix the running game
description: Notre Dame football still has some issues with its run game, and here are three ways that the Irish can fix it going forward.
fullText:
Notre Dame football: Three ways to fix the running game

The biggest glaring weakness in Notre Dame football's 2026 offense, is the rushing attack, and while there was a 100-yard performance against Michigan State, it has still left plenty to be desired.

Collectively as a team, taking out quarterback CJ Carr's five rushes, the backs have gained 387 yards on 102 carries for a 3.79 average rush. That's not great, as Nolan James leads the team with 169 yards, most of them coming this past weekend.

While it seemed like head coach Marcus Freeman was fairly happy with the backs performance against the Spartans, they certainly left meat on the bone. After have some time to think about how to fix this issue for the Irish, here are three ways Notre Dame can get the run game clicking.

There's plenty of reasons to go with Nolan James Jr. as RB 1. This is one of them. Not sure Aneyas Williams gets beyond the LOS after the missed James Flanigan block. James somehow gets five yards. pic.twitter.com/CJ6BUzljuW

As noted earlier, he's had the best season so far, and been the most effective. The explosive plays just aren't there like we've seen in years past, with his long being just 17 yards. James and Aneyas Williams both have virtually the same amount of touches, and he's been better than the first three games starter. It's time to move Williams to the backup role, although he should still get plenty of action. James has earned the starting job with his play, and it makes sense to ride the hot hand.

FULL STEAM AHEAD! An amazing catch by Micah Gilbert! 🤩

📺: Notre Dame Football: Michigan State @ Notre Dame on NBC + Peacock pic.twitter.com/QjodGYh7vN

You have to play to your strengths, and Carr is that for the Irish. With the struggles the backs have had so far this year, it makes sense to unleash the star quarterback. Carr didn't really push the envelope against Michigan State, but when he did he was finding Micah Gilbert. It's no coincidence that the run game started working once a few big pass plays were made. Keeping the safeties back to play the pass opens up running lanes, and at this point, playing backwards makes perfect sense.

Offensive snap counts for #NotreDame vs. Michigan State, per @PFF_College (68 max):
QB/
Carr 68

OL/
68-Black, Knapp, Craig, Absher, Lambert

The first two games it was trial by fire for the Irish offensive line, but against MSU, it was Will Black, Anthonie Knapp, Ashton Craig, Sullivan Absher and Guerby Lambert. The five took all 68 snaps, and by the end of the game started to find a groove. They surely wore down the Spartans defensive line, but that's part of game plan. It's hard to mix-and-match lineman during a game, as it's hard to find a semblance of cohesion with a group. It looks like Notre Dame now has that, and with more time, this unit will be much better.

title: One fatal flaw on each MLB contender that could derail long playoff run
description: From the Rays' bottom of the order to the Dodgers' shaky bullpen, every playoff contender is carrying one weakness that could end its October early.
fullText:
Entering the last week of the Major League Baseball season, 13 teams are still alive for October, and not one of them would be considered a totally complete team.

The Milwaukee Brewers have the best record in baseball but just one starter behind its ace it can actually trust. The Tampa Bay Rays are on the verge of clinching the top seed in the American League but have a lineup that goes cold at the bottom of the order almost every night. And a few teams, like the New York Yankees, are staring down injuries that can make or break their October.

Last season proved how a fatal flaw can come back and bite a team in October.

The Brewers had the best record in baseball in 2025 then scored one run a game and hit .128 in a four-game National League Championship Series sweep by the Dodgers. It was the lowest batting average in a postseason series of at least three games in MLB history. Their power outage was not a fluke. Milwaukee finished the year in the bottom third of the majors in home runs, covering for it all season with contact and speed. The flaw was there, buried under 97 wins, and it was exploited once the bright lights came on.

Here's the one fatal flaw that could end each contender's season:

MLB POSTSEASON FIELD: Who has clinched berths and who's on the verge?

The Rays have the best record in the American League (95-60, through Sept. 20) and need only a win or a New Yankees loss to clinch the AL East and home field advantage through the ALCS. Their flaw is buried at the bottom of the order. The seventh, eighth and ninth spots in the lineup rank 24th in the majors in OPS. Taylor Walls is hitting .219 with a .609 OPS in 52 games. Jorge Mateo has a .397 OPS in 23 games since Tampa Bay acquired him. The Rays have been burned by this flaw before. In 2023,the bottom of their lineup went 3-for-17 with no runs scored in a two-game sweep by Texas in the Wild Card Series, part of a 33-inning postseason scoreless streak.

The Yankees lead the majors with a 3.08 bullpen ERA, but Aaron Boone trusts exactly three relievers with a game on the line: closer David Bednar and setup men Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn. Every reinforcement behind them has left doubt in Boone's mind. New York traded a struggling Camilo Doval away at the deadline instead of adding to the pen, then lost Fernando Cruz to a partial UCL tear in late August. Ryan Weathers, the next man up, hasn't pitched since Aug. 23. Blackburn and Headrick had already thrown 79 and 73 innings heading into Sunday's game, more than typical setup men carry into a pennant race, let alone October. History carries a warning for the Yankees here. Cleveland's bullpen led the majors in the second half of 2016, but manager Terry Francona rode just two trusted arms hard, Andrew Miller and Cody Allen, through October. Both were spent by Game 7, and Cleveland ended up blowing a 3-1 World Series lead. One bad week from the bullpen and the Yankees are heading to the golf course instead of the World Series.

Boston clinched a playoff berth Sunday, Sept. 20 depite losing and hold the second AL wild card at 84-72, but its bullpen depth beyond three arms is the real question. Justin Slaten is done for the season, a degenerative elbow injury discovered too late to fix with anything but rest. Tyron Guerrero has been out since Sept. 1 with shoulder inflammation. Closer Aroldis Chapman, 34 saves and a 1.95 ERA, is nursing lat tightness, which already forced Garrett Whitlock, an ERA near 1.80 himself, into save situations he's never handled before. Boston gave up infield prospect Marcelo Mayer in August just to get reliever Erik Miller. That's how thin the bullpen was even before the injuries hit.

A thin bullpen is a real weakness in October, as the Orioles showed in 2023. Felix Bautista suffered a season-ending elbow injury just weeks before the playoffs and Baltimore went on to be swept in the American League Division Series.

The White Sox lost their lead in the AL Central, and part of the reason is a red flag for the playoffs. If they get in, the worry is that their rotation can't get through a lineup twice. Sean Burke went six innings against Detroit on Sept. 19, the first White Sox starter to complete six innings since Aug. 21. That's nearly a month of bullpen games in disguise. Trade deadline pickup Luis Castillo got pulled from the rotation entirely and moved to relief after his outings collapsed. His replacement, rookie David Sandlin, has an ERA near 7. Anthony Kay has been yanked early in four straight starts. Sean Newcomb, who carried the bullpen for months, has allowed runs in five of his last six outings. Chicago fell out of first place in the AL Central for the first time since early July, and it wasn't the offense that let go.

Cleveland's bullpen has no safety net. Closer Cade Smith has carried the group all year, but Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz, the two relievers who were supposed to set up in front of him, haven't thrown a competitive pitch all season. Both are on unpaid leave while awaiting a federal trial on pitch-rigging charges – now pushed to November – which puts them out for the postseason, too. The relievers brought in to cover that gap keep breaking down. Colin Holderman aggravated a wrist injury on a rehab outing Sept. 17. Shawn Armstrong, out since July 25 with a calf strain, isn't eligible to be back until Sept. 23. Cleveland is leaning on arms with no October track record to hold leads under the most pressure of the year

Houston's bridge to Josh Hader has collapsed. The Astros trail Texas by one game in the AL West with six left, and the two setup relievers who were supposed to get games to him are both hurt. Steven Okert, their best setup arm, hasn't pitched since Sept. 1 with a hamstring strain and won't be back before the postseason ... if there is one. Enyel De Los Santos joined him on the injured list Sept. 19. That leaves Bennett Sousa, who has a 5.27 ERA and control problems, and Bryan Abreu, who blew a save the same day in a loss that knocked Houston out of a playoff spot. That's two hurt setup arms and a shaky one left standing. That is not a formula for October.

The Rangers lead the AL West by one game over Houston, but the bullpen behind Jacob Latz wasn't built for this. Texas lost two relievers for the season – Carter Baumler and Jalen Beeks – and designated veteran Chris Martin for assignment in August after a 7.00 ERA. That left Latz, a converted starter, as closer by default. He converted nine consecutive saves before blowing one against Boston on Sept. 18. Days later, Skip Schumaker had nobody left in the pen and had to use starter Nathan Eovaldi for relief innings, then Jordan Montgomery for more two days after that.

A starter coming out of the bullpen isn't that crazy in the playoffs, but a bullpen held together by starters filling in is a screaming warning siren.

Spencer Schwellenbach and Hurston Waldrep both had season-ending elbow surgery in late August – Schwellenbach's second in under a year. Bryce Elder had knee surgery in September. Reynaldo López has been on and off the injured list twice, most recently Sept. 15. That is four rotation arms gone and leaves Chris Sale, 14-9 with a 2.18 ERA, and Tyler Mahle, sharp since he arrived from San Francisco, as the only settled postseason starters Atlanta has. The Braves have tried this before. In 2013 they lost Tim Hudson and Brandon Beachy to injuries, went into October with only Kris Medlen and Mike Minor as trusted starters and rode 37-year-old Freddy Garcia to a Game 4 exit in a 3-1 NLDS loss.

The Phillies traded for Jhoan Duran for just this time of year, and he hasn't disappointed. The problem for Philadelphia is getting to him. Orion Kerkering, their setup man for most of the year, got optioned to Triple-A on Sept. 19 after an ERA above 8.00 since the All-Star break. Jonathan Bowlan, who took over the eighth inning, is playing through a groin strain. What's left is rookie Alex McFarlane and September call-up Max Lazar in the highest-leverage innings of the year. Philadelphia holds the last NL wild card spot at 86-70, a game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres, with no margin for what comes next.

Milwaukee may have the best record in baseball – 98-58 through Sunday – but they run out of starters really fast. Jacob Misiorowski is a bona fide ace and the likely NL Cy Young winner, and Logan Henderson has quietly gone 10-3 with an ERA near 2.50 behind him. After that, it's question marks. The Brewers traded Freddy Peralta in January then lost Brandon Woodruff and Quinn Priester to season-ending surgery. Kyle Harrison was supposed to be the answer behind Misiorowski. He had a 2.57 ERA before the All-Star break. Since then, it's over 7.00, including four earned runs in one and two-thirds innings against Pittsburgh on Sept. 17. Deadline pickup Dustin May is an unproven fourth option with little margin for error. The best record in baseball still needs pitching to win a series.

The Cubs will take the best offense in baseball into October – 835 runs scored through Sept. 20, the most in the majors – and pair it with the pitching staff most likely to give a game away. Chicago's pitchers have allowed 227 home runs, also a league high. Cade Horton needed Tommy John surgery in April and won't pitch again this year. Ben Brown was shut down for good in September with a neck injury. Justin Steele hasn't started a big league game since April 2025. Deadline addition Kevin Gausman has a 5.04 ERA in eight starts as a Cub. Clay Holmes had a 1.55 ERA in his first five Cubs starts then allowed eight earned runs in 4⅓ innings against Miami on Sept. 6, leaving Craig Counsell still deciding whether he trusts him in October. It's happened to a loaded lineup before. The Dodgers scored 906 runs in 2023 – the second most in baseball that season – then watched Lance Lynn set a playoff record allowing four home runs in one inning as Arizona swept them out of the NLDS. Even the best offense in baseball can't outscore its own pitchers giving up home runs like this.

The Dodgers' bullpen problem is bigger than one bad closer. Edwin Diaz posted an 11.85 ERA before a neck injury, then came back Sept. 18 after a rehab stint so bad he retired two of eight batters in one outing. Dave Roberts didn't give him the ninth inning back. His replacement, Tanner Scott, isn't clean either. He blew a save against Miami on Sept. 13, his fourth in 26 chances. Setup man Edgardo Henriquez, who has a 2.85 ERA, went down with a back strain Sept. 14 and won't pitch again this season. A bullpen implosion has cost the Dodgers before. The 106-win 2019 team kept turning to Joe Kelly until he finally served up a series-ending grand slam. Los Angeles clinched its fifth consecutive NL West title with a bullpen nobody trusts yet.

Luis Rengifo was hitting .291 with a .784 OPS when he tore his ACL on Aug. 29. He is done for the year, and so is the San Diego bench really. Gavin Sheets has been out with a foot injury since late August. Ramón Laureano's absence has stretched deep into September. The Padres are tied with the Cubs and one game ahead of the Phillies for wild card positioning but sitting on the wrong side of the tiebreakers to both teams. They are filling in with September call-ups instead of players they built the roster around, and there isn't much season left to figure out if that holds up. The 2012 Yankees tried that when they lost Derek Jeter to a broken ankle in the ALCS opener; they got nothing much from the bench options and were swept by Detroit hitting .157 as a team.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: One fatal flaw on each MLB contender that could derail long playoff run

title: Man City 5-3 Sunderland - the fans' verdict
description: What a perfect performance by the lads and what a magnificent way to capitalise on Arsenal's loss yesterday and secure ourselves at the top of the table.  Sunderland were a credit and gave us a real test.  Brian Brobbey will be a very good player in the near future.
fullText:
We asked for your thoughts after Sunday's Premier League game between Manchester City and Sunderland

Here are some of your comments:

Youssef: We fought, we battled, we won. What a perfect performance by the lads and what a magnificent way to capitalise on Arsenal's loss yesterday and secure ourselves at the top of the table.

Owain: Brilliant going forward but suspect at the back. Sunderland were a credit and gave us a real test. Brian Brobbey will be a very good player in the near future. Thought we were pressurised and our passes went astray too often. We now have three good wide options. I like Enzo Fernandez, and I hope the Semenyo-distracted will leave him alone. Looked very impressive and deserved his player of the match.

Robert: Absolute credit to Sunderland who came to the Etihad to play football and not put 10-men behind the ball. They made this game what it was, very entertaining and worth watching.

Phil: Didn't want to sign Enzo, but what a player. Him and Elliott Anderson were outstanding.

Stuart: Although our defending was poor, the way we went toe-to-toe with City and caused them so many problems makes me proud. I think a lot of neutrals will enjoy watching Sunderland this season.

Mason: A swashbuckling approach that took City by surprise. Individual defensive errors cost Sunderland but overall it was a performance which showed they could go toe-to-toe with the best. Cut out those mistakes and it will soon click.

Mark: Another incredibly spirited display - my goodness, this team has character. The results will come.

David: Can't believe Sunderland have only four points - not many teams will come to the Etihad and score three! They have got the verve, commitment and fire-power to have a really good season. Keep trying, Mackems!

Iowa State football and Utah meet Saturday, Sept. 26 at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City for the Cyclones' Big 12 opener. Kickoff is set for 2:30 p.m. CT.

Iowa State is 2-1 with wins over Southeast Missouri and Bowling Green and a loss to Iowa. Utah is 3-0 after beating Idaho, Arkansas and Utah State.

Whether you're looking for kickoff information, injury updates, betting odds or score predictions, this guide has everything you need to know before the Cyclones take the field against the Utes.

We'll update this story throughout the week with the latest injury news, coach comments, line movement and game-day developments leading up to kickoff.

Location: Rice-Eccles Stadium, Salt Lake City

Spread: Utah -10.5 (DraftKings as of Sunday night)

Over/Under: 49.5 (DraftKings as of Sunday night)

The Cyclones and Utes are scheduled to kick off at 2:30 p.m. CT on Saturday, Sept. 26 at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City.

The game will be televised nationally on FOX.

Money line: Iowa State +360, Utah -470

Iowa State defenders Beni Ngoyi and Drew Surges did not play against Bowling Green but might be available vs. Utah. Cyclone cornerback Jaheim Singletary was hospitalized after a scary collision in the Bowling Green game. He was released from the hospital Saturday but his status is unknown.

The Cyclones were picked to finish last in the Big 12, but they are a confident bunch and believe they're much better than that. We'll start to find out if they're right when they face a tough Utah team on Saturday.

The Cyclones' defense keeps them in the game and Iowa State gives the Utes a good battle on the road. The Cyclones build more positive momentum heading into an Oct. 3 home game against West Virginia. Utah 21, Iowa State 17

title: Fulham 1-1 Man Utd - the fans' verdict
description: Joachim Andersen is causing us issues, after a great few years.  Let the youngsters loose with Bernd Leno and Alex Iwobi.  If we had taken Josh King off but replaced him with Emile Smith Rowe, we might have kept them more at bay and held on for the win.
fullText:
We asked for your thoughts after Sunday's Premier League game between Fulham and Manchester United.

Here are some of your comments:

Jeremy: A young team learning their trade. So close to a memorable win. Calvin Bassey/David Affengruber are building a great pairing. Joachim Andersen is causing us issues, after a great few years. Let the youngsters loose with Bernd Leno and Alex Iwobi.

Gordon: We played really well. Once we made the last substitutions, we set up to defend and that was our mistake. If we had taken Josh King off but replaced him with Emile Smith Rowe, we might have kept them more at bay and held on for the win. Hindsight is a wonderful thing. The team and manager should be proud of the performance but keep chins up and make sure our next game is as good. Keep the faith.

Keith: Have been a Fulham fan since 1974 with all the ups and downs. Can any Fulham fan please tell me why it seems we cannot defend a lead and concede so many late goals? Surely it must frustrate many Fulham fans and not just me.

Hillary: Just bad luck for the London boys. They were resilient and put pressure on the Red Devils - a draw wasn't bad, though.

Nigel: That was difficult to watch. Slow, laboured build-up with too many square and back passes. Once United reached the final third, the forward momentum halted and the ball inevitably went back or square. None of the forwards are producing the goods. It is clear to me that the starting eleven are a collection of individuals not yet gelling as a team. Michael Carrick must find a solution to that over the international break.

Peter: We learned that this team is not tactically good enough to do what we expect. Is it the players? Or the management team? Is it the owners? Is it all three? Whatever it is, this must be resolved sooner rather than later. With the Champions League looming, this could be embarrassing!

Mohammad: This team is disjointed with no leadership on the field. A bits-and-pieces team with lack of effort and lack of teamwork. You cannot score goals with nobody in the penalty area. Trying to do too much meaningless passing with every position, not performing to Premier League standards, whether it's the goalkeeper, defenders, midfielders, or nothing going forward.

Mike: How have Manchester United gone from beating Manchester City, Arsenal and getting into top four after a rough start last season... to this mess again? They don't look like they have the desire. Same man in charge but a completely different looking team?

title: Nothing to report about contract - Van Dijk
description: The 35-year-old's deal expires at the end of this season and it remains to be seen whether the centre-back, who joined Liverpool from Southampton in January 2018, will be offered an extension or he will choose to move on.  Van Dijk has played every minute of Liverpool's Premier League campaign so farand said his side have "not had a bad start" under new boss Andoni Iraola.  The Reds are unbeaten in seven games this season and go into the international break sixth in the table after two wins and three draws in the league.
fullText:
Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk insists he is "focusing on the "present" and there is "nothing to report" when it comes to his Anfield contract.

The 35-year-old's deal expires at the end of this season and it remains to be seen whether the centre-back, who joined Liverpool from Southampton in January 2018, will be offered an extension or he will choose to move on.

Van Dijk has played every minute of Liverpool's Premier League campaign so farand said his side have "not had a bad start" under new boss Andoni Iraola.

The Reds are unbeaten in seven games this season and go into the international break sixth in the table after two wins and three draws in the league.

Speaking after Sunday's 1-0 win at Bournemouth, Van Dijk said: "Any manager that comes to a new environment and a new club needs a bit of time, and the same goes with players.

"We work a lot, almost every day, and hopefully it works sooner rather than later. It is down to us to get results. At a club like Liverpool, you don't have a lot of time to get results so you have to get the points on the board.

"We've not had a bad start - we could have done better in a couple of games, but we are where we are. On to the next."

Van Dijk will now head off on international duty after holding positive talks about his Netherlands future with new manager Xavi, who was at Anfield to watch Liverpool's Champions League opener against Atletico Madrid earlier this month.

The Reds host Manchester City after the three-week hiatus (16:30 BST on 11 October).

title: The Optimist: Do it again, Bryce
description: The Panthers are a really fun team to watch. Now we get to ask if they can be more than that. Can they be competitive?
fullText:
They were the best of teams. They were the worst of teams. Then we reflected on the fact that the Carolina Panthers 34-3 win over the Atlanta Falcons was, pending the results of Monday Night Football, the largest margin of victory in the NFL in Week 2 by a mile and a half and we determined that the Panthers are, at the very least, not the worst of teams. In fact, the 1-1 Panthers have a positive score differential through two weeks in spite of giving up a franchise record number of points in Week 1. That is true because they played an incredibly inept Falcons offense without a quarterback to speak of and because the offense has largely started out strong in the 2026 season.

That strong start has been keyed by none other than the very much maligned Bryce Young. We'll detail his rise more later on, but suffice it to say that he is passing the eye test at a level many of us had long since given up on. We're not ready to crown him as a franchise quarterback, but we will be if he keeps up this pace through the season. Kudos are also due to the management of the team and the defense as a whole. Let's get into it.

Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke have transformed this defense from last season. The unit as a whole has a lot of the same problems that it did last season, largely thanks to injuries undoing some of the gains they made through free agency, but one weakness is well on its way out the door. These guys are heads up players who are only going to get more comfortable playing in this scheme and with their new teammates as the season goes on.

Both of them had incredible interceptions that were largely due to their ability to pay attention to the football and make the play in front of them. Lloyd and Okereke shared the team lead with nine tackles on the day. For Lloyd that included one sack, two additional tackles for loss, one additional quarterback hit, three passes deflected, and two interceptions. He returned the second pick 16 yards for a touchdown.

Yes, they did this against Cooper Rush so well that they also got the opportunity to do it against Jack Strand in the same game. Yes, they were picked apart by the same Caleb Williams last week who only managed three points against the Minnesota Vikings in most of four quarters before suffering a severe looking hamstring injury. Like I said, they are only going to get better the more time they have to gel with their new team. This week isn't their floor so much as a glimpse of a possible ceiling.

It's a ceiling worthy of the history of Carolina Panthers linebackers. All they have to do is reach it.

This is what we wanted to see this year. Tetairoa McMillan had a 100-yard day, Jalen Coker was a reliable, productive target, and Xavier Legette made a positive impact. Sprinkle in a couple targets to running backs and tight ends in appropriate situations, add some broth and a potato and the Panthers look like they got a stew going.

Unlike their offense, the Falcons defense is a real unit made up of professional football players. This was what they did against real competition and it was great. Neither the Falcons nor the Bears are likely to be near the top ten of defenses by the end of the season, but neither unit is laughably bad, either. These were great games to ramp up into the rest of the season.

Question marks abound around Young, Legette, Jonathon Brooks, and the meaning of life, but right now the Panthers have an honest to goodness strength in their wide receiver room and that's fantastic to see.

No player is going to be beloved by their team's fans when they are acquired via a trade that involves sending away a first overall pick, other high future picks, and a fan favorite wide receiver. Young's path was further inhibited by awful coaching as a rookie, comparisons to Williams, and his own awful, awful play in the first three years of his career.

The bright side for him has been the coaching and encouragement he has received from head coach Dave Canales and offensive coordinator Brad Idzik. Both of those mentors are young in their own rights and are growing into their current roles at about the same rate that Young is. That is to say that it equally unsurprising that it took a minute to for them to find success together as it was frustrating to watch them struggle along the way.

These past two weeks to open the season have qualified as success for Young and Idzik. Over two games, Young has averaged 324 passing yards, three touchdowns, 0.5 interceptions, a 63% completion rating, and 8.86 yards per attempt. In his career prior to this season, he average 180 passing yards, one touchdown, 0.65 interceptions, and 6 Y/A per game. This season has provided a small sample size so far, but we can only judge off of what he has shown so far.

So far he is throwing the ball further down field, keeping drives alive for longer, getting in scoring position more, and turning the ball over less. Outside of the box score, his pocket presence, movement, vision, general demeanor, and touch have all dramatically improved. Bear with me for one of the biggest "ifs" in the history of the Carolina Panthers.

IF Young can keep this up, IF Young can keep playing at this level then he will be who the Panthers drafted him to be. He will have absolutely spoiled his rookie contract window. From a team building perspective, that's like shooting yourself in the foot to make sure you can walk in a few years. But compared to where the Panthers were for the six years prior to drafting Young, that seems like fine logic to me.

That all depends on Young. Two games are hardly a trend. Thus we cannot say definitively that Young, Canales, and Idzik have "Arrived". We can say, however, that so far they are passing the eye test. The little things are adding up in their favor. Play calls are in and Bryce Young is at the line of scrimmage with time to spare. Penalties, like the many we saw in the first quarter of yesterday's game, aren't complete drive killers. These are great things that we have now witnessed twice against pretty poor defenses. If we see them again against better defenses, like the Browns and the Lions before the bye-week, then we'll probably be in for a fun season.

The Panthers offense that showed up the last two weeks at least makes a game out of their next two contests. The Panthers defense that we saw yesterday won't show up again, but it may look closer to that than who they were against the Bears. Time will tell.

For now, I'm focusing on Young's statistical improvements to buoy my optimism through the week. Forgive me if this is a little pie in the sky. It's been a minutes since we got to start the season talking about nice things. so I'm just going to do that until the nice things go away and we have to spend weeks on end cursing the Kellen Moore/Tyler Shough Saints.

Let's go back to what we were talking about after the preseason. The Carolina Panthers were traditionally a team to start the season slowly under Bryce Young and Dave Canales. By all accounts, that's not what we've seen so far. Let's look at Young's average first two games of the season:

153 more yards per game. Two more touchdowns per game. A 5% improvement isn't exactly world changing, but the nature of his passes have changed. 4.23 more yards gained per pass attempt show a more aggressive passer. Combine that with a higher completion percentage and we have an offense that is moving the ball.

We've cautioned all the way that we don't know if this Bryce is a real boy or just an early season figment of our collective optimism. That is true. But there is another question lingering in this data that I'm going to ask just for fun:

What if Young's season trajectory hasn't changed? Right now Bryce Young is a top five passer, statistically speaking, in the NFL. What if this is his slow start to 2026?

title: Bengals vs. Steelers odds: Opening lines for Week 3 matchup
description: The Bengals are opening as 3.5-point favorites in Pittsburgh.
fullText:
The Cincinnati Bengals have started the 2026 season 2-0 with two pretty solid wins —the Buccaneers at home in Week 1 and the Texans in Houston in Week 2, the latter by a score of 20-6.

The Bengals' defense put on a show in Houston, keeping the Texans out of the end zone for the entire game. Houston converted just 5/17 third-down attempts and was completely stonewalled on fourth down, going 0/4.

Even though Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for nearly 200 receiving yards and two touchdowns—both scored by Chase—the defense won the day. Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, Boye Mafe and the rest of Al Golden's rebuilt unit were outstanding, and the Bengals now sit alone atop the AFC North heading into Week 3.

Next up, the Bengals head to Pittsburgh to open division play against the 1-1 Steelers. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, Cincinnati opened as a 3.5-point favorite, with the over/under set at 43.5 points.

The Steelers defeated the Falcons 20-13 in Week 1 before traveling to Foxborough and losing to the Patriots 20-3 in Week 2.

Now, Aaron Rodgers, DK Metcalf, and the Steelers' offense will have to find a way to keep pace with Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and the rest of Cincinnati's offense—all while dealing with Dexter Lawrence and a Bengals defensive front that just made life miserable for the Texans.
