title: Openda calls out one Juventus teammate for being a reason he struggled
description: Lois Openda is currently on loan at Lyon from Juventus after spending just one season on the books of the Bianconeri, and the striker appears to view Dusan Vlahovic as one of the reasons he struggled ...
fullText:
Lois Openda is currently on loan at Lyon from Juventus after spending just one season on the books of the Bianconeri, and the striker appears to view Dusan Vlahovic as one of the reasons he struggled in Turin.

Juventus were confident they had signed a top player when Openda joined them on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent last season. He had been superb at RB Leipzig, where he established himself as one of the best attackers in Germany and attracted interest from several top clubs.

Juventus won the race for his signature and brought him to Turin to share the goalscoring responsibilities with Vlahovic and Jonathan David. Openda and David appeared to have a good relationship both on and off the pitch, and had they been given enough time to play together, they might have achieved more.

However, that opportunity never really came, with Luciano Spalletti preferring to use the Serbian despite knowing that Vlahovic had not signed a new contract. Vlahovic was a superb striker and suited the manager's style, but Openda felt there were difficulties when it came to combining with the other attackers.

Openda has now identified this as one of the reasons he struggled in Turin. Tuttojuve quoted him as saying: "With Jonathan, we could play together, but there were tactical issues because I play a lot with depth, and Juve weren't capable of expressing themselves that way. On top of that, Vlahovic rarely gave up the ball. I had a few chances, but as time went by, I was given less and less space, and in the end, I realized that if I wanted to play, I had to leave."

(Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

The comments suggest Openda felt that Juventus' tactical approach limited his opportunities to demonstrate his qualities. His preference for making runs in behind did not always fit the way the team played, while the limited opportunities alongside David also affected his chances of establishing himself.

Openda ultimately decided that leaving was necessary if he wanted to play regularly. His loan move to Lyon now gives him another opportunity to regain his confidence and show the qualities that made him such a highly regarded attacker at RB Leipzig.

His experience at Juventus appears to have left him with a clear understanding of what he needs from his next club. For Openda, regular opportunities and a tactical system that suits his strengths could be important as he looks to rediscover his best form.

title: Barcelona scout 19-year-old Brazilian defensive talent – report
description: Barcelona will be heading into the international break with the best start to a season in quite time now, with the team having won all their matches in all competitions.However, the ecstasy of that su...
fullText:
Barcelona will be heading into the international break with the best start to a season in quite time now, with the team having won all their matches in all competitions.

However, the ecstasy of that success was slightly muted after Andreas Christensen's injury against Sevilla.

The Dane could be out for up to six weeks by rough estimates, leaving Barcelona without a key defensive options as we enter a tricky part of the campaign.

Given Christensen's injury, it is only natural to expect Barcelona to step up their efforts when it comes to eyeing defensive reinforcements.

According to UmDois Deportes (h/t SPORT), the club have already kickstarted their preparations, as they are keeping close tabs on Arthur Dias.

Dias dueling with former Barcelona star Memphis Depay. (Photo by Heuler Andrey/Getty Images)

A left-footed centre-back by trade, Dias currently plies hits trade for Athletico PR and has been recently called up by Carlo Ancelotti to the Brazilian national team.

The report suggests Barcelona scout Joao Amaral was in Curitiba this weekend to witness Dias in action against Bahia.

Barcelona, though, could face stiff competition for Dias, with Tottenham Hotspur along with Como, Newcastle United and Benfica also interested in his services. Athletico PR had already rejected a bid from Tottenham in the summer.

It is clear that Barcelona are in the running to sign Arthur Dias despite increasing competition. And given the player's profile, it is easy to wonder why.

Does Dias have what it takes to thrive at Barcelona? (Photo by Heuler Andrey/Getty Images)

Aged just 19, Dias is an ambidextrous centre-back, who has shown a high level of physicality and maturity for his age. He already has 50 competitive appearances to his name for Athletico PR.

Other than his physicality and a 1.88m frame, the young Brazilian is also known for his ball-playing ability. He is adept at both short passes or passes in between the line, making him a natural fit for Barcelona's style of play.

Joao Amaral's presence in Curitiba, therefore, is certainly exciting news for fans as Barcelona look for potential defensive reinforcements in the upcoming January transfer window.

title: Richard Hughes left Liverpool a massive problem that will haunt them, 'immense' star proves it
description: Liverpool had a rather interesting summer transfer window.They replaced many of their first-team squad and, with Andoni Iraola coming in to take over from Arne Slot, their whole identity changed.Durin...
fullText:
Liverpool had a rather interesting summer transfer window.

They replaced many of their first-team squad and, with Andoni Iraola coming in to take over from Arne Slot, their whole identity changed.

During pre-season, it felt like Liverpool were going to completely transform and potentially even get back to the top of the Premier League table.

However, they've massively underdelivered and, even though there have been glimpses of improvement, it's unclear whether Iraola's appointment was a good or bad thing yet.

They spent over £150 million again this summer with Bradley Barcola being their marquee signing.

But, by the end of the window, Richard Hughes left his post and, although he may feel like he did a good job, there's one massive problem that he's left the Reds to deal with that looks likely to come and haunt them.

Mohamed Salah's Liverpool exit this summer was definitely the highest profile departure from L4.

The Egyptian King still had a year left on his deal but, instead of seeing that out, the winger and the club chose to mutually terminate his contract.

This made fans believe that signing a new right-winger would be one of the main things on Liverpool's priority list.

And, while they did bring two new wingers in over the summer, naturally, they both play on the left so, when used on the right, they're not likely to perform to the best of their ability.

Indeed, some players such as Ismaila Sarr and Yankuba Minteh were eyed as potential options to replace the 34-year-old but, after Brighton and Crystal Palace were demanding stupidly high fees for both players, those deals never really went anywhere.

This left Liverpool lacking depth up front and, since Salah contributed to 22 goals across all competitions last season, it gave them a massive gap to plug.

And, after his recent performance, it's now clear that the Egyptian's exit is likely to come back and haunt them.

Before Salah exited L4, the attacker was easily one of Liverpool's most important players.

The attacker was their main source of goals and was the reason why they won the Premier League title again in the 2024-25 season.

No matter what season, how old or how fit he was, the Egyptian always managed to find a way to get the ball into the back of the net or at least set one of his teammates up.

The same thing happened on Saturday with Trabzonspor.

The Turkish Super Lig outfit pummelled league leaders Galatasaray 4-0 with Salah bagging himself a hattrick and assisting his teammate for the fourth.

Of course, Salah wasn't himself last term but, even then, he still contributed to 22-goals across all competitions which certainly isn't a number to be frowned upon.

If Liverpool weren't going to replace the Egyptian, they should have definitely kept Salah around longer.

Because, even though teams obviously need to move on from their golden era, without replacing their star men, they're going to fall further behind.

Here's hoping that Liverpool find someone to replace him soon, otherwise, some serious questions will need to be asked.

title: Luke McCowan not suited to start in Celtic’s bigger games
description: It’s glaringly obvious to the Celtic support that Luke McCowan isn’t suited to start in our big games, so why does he continue to get selected?Luke McCowan of Celtic arrives prior to the Scottish ...
fullText:
Luke McCowan of Celtic arrives prior to the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Falkirk at Celtic Park on August 29, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Luke McCowan is in the firing line once again due to a lacklustre and wasteful display in his 45 minute appearance in the 1-0 loss to the Rangers at Celtic Park. During that first 45 minutes the former Dundee captain continually gave the ball away with misplaced passes or was caught in possession, much to the frustration of the 60,000 Celtic supporters watching from the stands.

Last month McCowan was unfairly singled out for his part in the 5-1 capitulation in Linz, and yet again his shortcomings were exposed in the latest Glasgow Derby defeat.

Cameron Carter-Vickers of Celtic and Luke McCowan of Celtic. LASK v Celtic, UEFA Champions League, Play Off Round, Second Leg, Football, Raiffeisen Arena, Linz, Austria – 25 Aug 2026Linz Raiffeisen Arena: Photo Michael Zemanek/Shutterstock

Like many supporters, I was dismayed when Luke's name was read out in the starting XI, and not because I have any sort of vendetta against him. Frankly, he's been a liability in these games as past experience more than proves.

Luke is a reliable squad player to call upon in the run-of-the-mill domestic fixtures, but in the more demanding fixtures, he seems to falter as he duly proved once again on Sunday afternoon where he put in an inept and uninspiring display in a torrid first half, and looked very much like this sort of occasion is to much for him to handle.

Attila Osvath of Ferencvaros is challenged by Luke McCowan of Celtic during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Celtic FC and Ferencvarosi TC at Celtic Park on September 17, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Luke who was handed an extension on his current deal only a short few months ago was selected to give us an extra body in a midfield that's been badly exposed in recent weeks, but he didn't add anything to the battle, and was it was no surprise when he was hauled off at the interval.

If anyone in the coaching staff thought that Luke could provide the physicality that has been missing since Arne Engels was sold, then they got their answer in that first half yesterday afternoon.

Luke is approaching his 29th birthday, and is a vastly experienced professional, and being a Celtic supporter, as well as being at the club for long enough to know the importance of yesterday's fixture, it beggars belief that he looked like a rookie being thrown into the mix.

Martin O'Neill arrives at the stadium. Celtic v Rangers. Scottish Premiership. 20 September 2026. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

This isn't the first time that the former Dundee man has went missing in this fixture, and begs the question, why does he keep getting selected for fixtures of such importance when he such a liability? Martin O'Neill said afterwards that Luke merited the start. How? What have we missed?

As a squad player and as a useful substitute, Luke can do a decent job in his time at Celtic. But he's shown that is as much as can be realistically expect of him.

title: Born in Bihar, a master’s degree from IIT Kanpur, but with cricket still in his heart, Abhishek Anand has taken his passion to Japan
description: Abhishek Anand, proud IIT Kanpur graduate, who represent Japan's national cricket team, capturing widespread social media interest with his incredible story from Bihar to this unexpected opportunity.
fullText:
From IIT Kanpur to Japan's national cricket team, Abhishek Anand's journey has taken an unexpected turn and now, a viral video has put the Bihar-born cricketer in the spotlight ahead of Japan's historic T20I against India.

The 28-year-old, who hails from Bihar's Rohtas district, moved to Japan for employment after completing his Chemistry degree at IIT Kanpur. He continued pursuing cricket alongside his professional career, eventually earning a place in Japan's national team.

However, despite the buzz surrounding his story, Abhishek's participation in the September 22 fixture is not confirmed. Japan have announced a 15-member squad for the match, and Abhishek is not among the selected players.

During his college years in IIT Kanpur, he remained connected to cricket and captained the institute's team. After graduating, he relocated to Tokyo for work. Rather than giving up the sport, he began playing club cricket in Japan, balancing his professional commitments with his passion for the game.

His performances in the local cricket circuit helped him earn a call-up to Japan's national setup. Abhishek made his T20I debut against the Cook Islands on May 9, 2025. He has since played 18 T20Is, scoring 275 runs, including a highest score of 55, and taking one wicket, according to figures cited in recent reports.

Abhishek's journey has attracted attention on social media ahead of the India-Japan fixture, with a video fea turing the cricketer going viral. In the clip, he is asked about being a Bihari representing Japan. His response and a message directed at the Indian team have sparked interest among cricket fans, with the phrase "Bihari kahan nahi hai bhai" drawing particular attention.

India and Japan are scheduled to meet in a historic one-off men's T20I on September 22 at the Sano International Cricket Ground in Tochigi, Japan. The match will be the first men's international cricket meeting between the two countries and is being held under the Suzuki Cup banner to commemorate 75 years of India-Japan diplomatic relations. It will also serve as preparation for the Asian Games, where the cricket competition begins two days later.

title: Eagles snap counts vs. Titans: Breakdown, analysis from 24-20 win
description: Breaking down the Eagles’ snap counts and playing-time percentages from their 24-20 Week 2 victory over the Titans
fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles used extensive rotations at several positions in their 24-20 Week 2 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Jalen Hurts and the starting offensive line played all 76 offensive snaps. Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen and Lane Johnson joined Hurts in going the distance.

DeVonta Smith led the skill-position players with 67 snaps, accounting for 88% of Philadelphia's offensive plays. Tight end Johnny Mundt was next with 49 snaps, while rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon played 48. Dontayvion Wicks logged 47 snaps. The backfield distribution was among the biggest surprises. Will Shipley led the group with 39 snaps, followed by Tank Bigsby with 26. Saquon Barkley played only 12 offensive snaps, or 16%. Darius Cooper played 31 snaps and caught the winning 3-yard touchdown from Hurts with nine seconds remaining. Dallas Goedert played only 19 snaps, while Hollywood Brown played 17.

Philadelphia had five defenders play all 53 snaps: Zack Baun, Cooper DeJean, Andrew Mukuba, Quinyon Mitchell and Riqq Woolen. Second-year linebacker Jihaad Campbell played 47 defensive snaps, giving him an 89% share. Moro Ojomo led the defensive line with 43 snaps, followed by Jalyx Hunt with 42. Jalen Carter and Nolan Smith Jr. each played 41.

Jordan Davis played 23 snaps, while Azeez Ojulari Ebiketie logged 15. Byron Young played 13, and A.J. Epenesa received eight.

Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Kelee Ringo led the special-teams units with 19 snaps apiece. Trotter did not receive a defensive snap after playing a prominent role in the season opener, making his Week 2 usage one of the most notable changes in Philadelphia's rotation.

title: Aaron Glenn on Jets taking the ball in OT: I wanted to control the clock
description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn faced questions about a number of his decisions after Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers.
fullText:
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn faced questions about a number of his decisions after Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers.

Glenn chose not to use his final timeouts before the end of regulation, which was questioned by many because the Jets had a chance to get the ball back and end the contest without needing to go into extra time. After the game went into overtime, Glenn made another decision that came up for further inspection.

The Jets won the toss and opted to receive the kickoff. Quarterback Geno Smith was sacked on the first two plays and the Jets never got the ball back after punting because the Packers drove for a game-winning field goal. After the game, Glenn said he was hoping to leave the Packers with as little time on offense as possible.

"Usually, if you can get yourself in a situation like that and you can really control the clock, you can control exactly how they're going to play offense once you go and score," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "So, we control the clock, we go run it down; say we run it seven minutes, which we've done before, we've run a number of time off the clock, it only gives them so much time to try to rebuttal. We didn't do a good job in that situation. And plus, to me, once you get the ball and you go down and score, you put the pressure on the other team that has to go ahead and score. But that didn't happen for us the way I planned."

Having Smith drop back to pass is a curious way to control the clock, although the Jets had struggled to find momentum running the ball all afternoon. They had held the Packers' offense in check, however, and Green Bay ended the afternoon with 199 total yards, but Glenn went with his offense and that turned out to be the wrong choice.

title: KV Mechelen will not part ways with Fred Vanderbiest yet despite winless start to the season
description: KV Mechelen have had a terrible start to the Belgian Pro League season. Last season, the side qualified for the top six play offs for the first time and were hoping to build on that this season. Howev...
fullText:
KV Mechelen have had a terrible start to the Belgian Pro League season. Last season, the side qualified for the top six play offs for the first time and were hoping to build on that this season. However, after seven games, the side sit rock bottom with just three points and no wins. However, Fred Vanderbiest will remain, for now at least, in charge of KV Mechelen. As reported by Sporza, there is currently no panic at KV Mechelen who remain confident that Vanderbiest can turn things around.

This may well be an acknowledgement on the part of the board that recruitment has, so far, not been great. Very few of the players signed in the summer have been able to make much of an impact on the side, who still remain reliant on Myron van Brederode for inspiration. The 23-year-old Dutch winger is the sides top scorer with three goals, building on his strong season last year where he managed 10 goals and five assists in 36 games for the club.

Outside of van Brederode, the side have only scored two other goals. That is a real concern, with 14 shipped at the other end in seven games. What is equally concerning for KV Mechelen fans is that the midfield duo of Denis Praet and Frederik Hammar has yet to come to fruition. Last season, Hammer was fantastic in the midfield, and there was hope that Praet would add an extra level of quality to the central midfield. This has yet to happen.

The side could also do with finding a way to get either Bouke Boersma or Benito Raman scoring. Boersma joined midway through last season to replace Lion Lauberbach, who joined Venezia. Boersma had scored 11 goals in 23 games for De Graafschap in the Dutch second tier, and had a decent start to his KV Mechelen career with three goals and three assists in 17 games. He has struggled so far this season. Raman has struggled to make an impact under Vanderbiest. Prior to the coach taking over, Raman had scored 15 goals in 34 games for KV Mechelen. Under Vanderbiest last season he managed only three goals in 31 games. So far this season he is scoreless in six. It does feel that Raman is not the sort of striker Vanderbiest wants up top, as the likes of Lauberbach were much more suited to his style of play with his physicality, even if he was not technically that great.

Vanderbiest now has a long international break to try and work things out at KV Mechelen. One would imagine that the next four games are crucial for him to remain head coach of KV Mechelen. If the side fail to beat Kortrijk or OH Leuven in their next four matches, its hard to imagine Vanderbiest being able to remain as the sides head coach.

title: British player receives surprise Laver Cup call-up for London event
description: The last edition at The O2 in 2022 saw three-time Grand Slam champion Andy Murray compete for Team Europe
fullText:
British No 1 Arthur Fery has been called up as a Team Europe alternate for this weekend's Laver Cup in London.

Fery, who reached the semi-finals of Wimbledon in July and led the British side that defeated Ecuador in the Davis Cup at the Copper Box Arena over the weekend, will serve as a back-up to Yannick Noah's six-strong team at The O2 this weekend.

The 24-year-old will practice with the team – which consists of Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Flavio Cobolli, Rafael Jodar, Jakub Mensik and Casper Ruud – and will fill in should there be an injury or withdrawal.

"It's an honour to be part of Team Europe at Laver Cup, especially here at home in London," said Fery. "I grew up going to The O2, so to come back as part of Team Europe in front of the British fans is something I'm really proud of and am looking forward to.

"It's going to be great to be around some of the best players in the world and learn from them. I'll be ready to do whatever is required of me to support my teammates from the bench."

At the last Laver Cup held in London in 2022, memorable for Roger Federer's final professional match, three-time Grand Slam finalist Andy Murray featured for Team Europe.

Team World have also named Peruvian player Ignacio Buse, the world No 35, as an alternate to back up Alex de Minaur, Taylor Fritz, Brandon Nakashima, Alexander Bublik, Learner Tien and Francisco Cerundolo. Nakashima replaced Ben Shelton in the visiting team's line-up after the US Open finalist withdrew last week.

"Laver Cup is a historic event and I'm very excited to be part of it," said Buse. "It's an incredible opportunity to be surrounded by so many great players and icons of the sport and to have someone with Andre Agassi's experience as a coach.

"I'm going to enjoy it, learn as much as I can and make the most of the experience."

This week's event in London will be the ninth Laver Cup in total, after the tournament debuted in Prague in 2017.

Team World have won three of the last four events, after Team Europe won the first four editions.

title: Milwaukee Brewers: Jackson Chourio made MLB history in 3-0 win over Baltimore Orioles
description: The Milwaukee Brewers set a franchise record last year by going 97-65. Not only did they finish with the best record in baseball, but they also had more wins than any other team in the history of the organization. Now, a year later, they are even better. With their 3-0 win over the Baltimore Orioles [...]
fullText:
The Milwaukee Brewers set a franchise record last year by going 97-65. Not only did they finish with the best record in baseball, but they also had more wins than any other team in the history of the organization.

Now, a year later, they are even better.

With their 3-0 win over the Baltimore Orioles on Sunday night, Milwaukee improved to 98-58 on the season. Obviously, this breaks their franchise record from last season, and also marks the first time in franchise history that they are 40 games over .500.

Oh, and Jackson Chourio made history, too.

Heading into the game, Chourio had 24 home runs and 19 stolen bases on the season. He swiped two bags in the 3-0 victory, giving him his third consecutive 20-20 season to start his Major League career.

This milestone is notable for two reasons. First, he joins Julio Rodriguez and Bobby Witt Jr. as the only three players in baseball history to start their careers with three straight 20-20 seasons.

But what is even more impressive is that Chourio, who is still just 22 years old, is the first player in history to have three consecutive 20-20 seasons before the age of 23:

Jackson Chourio swipes his 20th bag of the season

He is the first player with 3 seasons of 20+ stolen bases and 20+ home runs before turning 23 years old! pic.twitter.com/3PwbpjxM3a

— MLB (@MLB) September 21, 2026

What makes the achievement all the more impressive this year is the fact that Chourio missed the first month of the season with a fracture in his left hand. Had he been healthy in March/April, he likely would have accomplished this milestone weeks ago, and perhaps would have a 30-30 season by now.

For the 2026 season, the Brewers' star left-fielder is hitting .285/.344/.481 with 24 home runs, 70 RBI, and 21 stolen bases.

Oh, and he leads all MLB left fielders in defensive runs saved, making him a serious candidate for a Gold Glove award.

title: Juventus condemns fans who interrupted a minute’s silence for Inter and Italy star Sandro Mazzola
description: Juventus has strongly criticized its own supporters who disturbed a minute’s silence in honor of former Italy and Inter Milan star Sandro Mazzola.  The tribute was being held at all Serie A matches over the weekend after Mazzola, widely considered one of Italy’s greatest ever players, died on Friday.  The minute’s silence was interrupted in Turin, ahead of Sunday’s match against Atalanta, as a section of Juventus fans turned their backs on the field and chanted songs about their own club legends instead.
fullText:
TURIN, Italy (AP) — Juventus has strongly criticized its own supporters who disturbed a minute's silence in honor of former Italy and Inter Milan star Sandro Mazzola.

The tribute was being held at all Serie A matches over the weekend after Mazzola, widely considered one of Italy's greatest ever players, died on Friday. He was 83.

The minute's silence was interrupted in Turin, ahead of Sunday's match against Atalanta, as a section of Juventus fans turned their backs on the field and chanted songs about their own club legends instead. Inter and Juventus are fierce rivals.

The chants were drowned out by applause from other supporters in the stadium — both home and away fans.

"No rivalry can justify a lack of respect during a minute's silence," Juventus said in a statement.

"Honoring the memory of those being remembered and coming together in remembrance during moments of commemoration is a shared responsibility that transcends allegiances and colors."

Juventus could risk a fine or even having the Curva Sud — the sector where the ultras sit and where the disturbance happened — closed for a match. A decision by Italy's sporting justice system is expected early this week.

After a stunning qualifying lap landed him pole position, McLaren's Lando Norris was unable to hold on to the lead because of losing out during a virtual safety car period. He managed to recover to third.

title: Tiatia in talks over new Dragons deal
description: Dragons aim to secure new contract with head coach Filo Tiatia as he prepares for a second full season in charge at Rodney Parade.
fullText:
Dragons are in advanced talks with head coach Filo Tiatia about a contract extension.

The former All Blacks forward joined the Rodney Parade club in the summer of 2024 as defence coach.

He was promoted as interim boss after the departure of Dai Flanagan the following November and was appointed on a permanent basis in February 2025.

Tiatia's deal expires at the end of the 2026-27 campaign and Dragons are keen to retain his services.

"We'd love to lock Filo in and back him for a long-term future at the Dragons," said chief executive Rhys Blumberg.

"He has definitely got an appetite to stay and we have an appetite to keep him. We will work through that over the next month or so to get something done."

Dragons feel extra pressure after avoiding WRU cut

Wales lock Carter cleared for season start

Tiatia, who previously coached at Auckland and Moana Pasifik, as well as Toyota Verblitz and Sunwolves in Japan, had a tough first season at Dragons.

He won only once after taking the reins – at Newcastle in the Challenge Cup – and the club finished bottom of the United Rugby Championship (URC) for the first time.

Big strides were made last season with three wins and four draws in the URC, although Dragons were pipped to 14th place by Scarlets on win count.

"We finished 15th but there was progress with 19 more league points and getting to the semi-finals of the Challenge Cup," said Blumberg, who has set a target of pushing for the play-offs in the coming campaign.

"We really improved and Filo deserves real credit for how much belief he instills in people – that is his superpower.

"He is a mentor for the players and gets them to believe they are good enough to compete with anybody."

Tiatia worked without a defence coach after stepping up from that role in 2024-25.

He brought in Dale MacLeod last summer, with the experienced New Zealander effectively acting as his number two.

"Dale is an important part of it – he is the yin to Filo's yang," said Blumberg.

"You have two fantastic, technically-astute young coaches in Matt O'Brien and Sam Hobbs and other really good support staff.

"But Filo and Dale are two senior, experienced figures leading the programme, offering security and guidance."

Dragons kick off their URC campaign at Benetton on Friday, 25 September (19:45 BST), the first of six fixtures in the first block of the season.

description: Wales suffer a triple blow going into their Nations League A campaign with Harry Wilson, Nathan Broadhead and Karl Darlow all out of Craig Bellamy's squad.
fullText:
Wales have suffered a triple blow going into their Nations League A campaign with Harry Wilson, Nathan Broadhead and Karl Darlow all out of Craig Bellamy's squad.

Leeds attacking midfielder Wilson, Wales' key player in recent times, has a quad problem while Wrexham forward Broadhead has a thigh issue.

First-choice goalkeeper Darlow has also withdrawn despite making his Manchester United debut in the EFL Cup last week and being on the bench for the Premier League draw with Fulham on Sunday.

Wales have called up veteran Leicester keeper David Cornell, Huddersfield forward Joe Taylor – both of whom are uncapped – and Reading midfielder Charlie Savage as replacements.

Bellamy's team face Portugal in their Nations League opener in Lisbon on Thursday before they meet Denmark in Copenhagen next Sunday.

They then face Norway in Cardiff on Thursday, 1 October before the Danes visit the Welsh capital three days later.

Thursday, 24 September, 19:45 BST

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC One Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Wales were already without key defenders Joe Rodon and Dylan Lawlor, while Cardiff City duo Rubin Colwill and Isaak Davies are also unavailable.

Cornell, 35, joined Leicester on a one-year deal last Friday having been a free agent after leaving Preston North End in the summer.

The former Wales Under-21 international, from Swansea, has made more than 200 senior appearances having played for a string of clubs since coming through Swansea City's academy.

title: League B return, no Bradley and Kvaratskhelia test - NI talking points
description: Northern Ireland's return to Uefa Nations League B will see them face a player manager Michael O'Neill calls "one of the best in the world" but they enter the campaign without their own captain.
fullText:
The build-up to Northern Ireland's 2026 Nations League campaign has been dominated by the future of Ceadach O'Neill and the always thorny issue of eligibility.

With the Arsenal forward included in Michael O'Neill's 28-man squad for this four-game window, the 18-year-old appears set to add to his two senior caps across the next two weeks, likely ruling out any future switch of international allegiance despite an approach from the Republic of Ireland.

While one prominent storyline seems as if it will soon be put to bed, there is plenty more to look out for as Northern Ireland make their return to League B.

NI squad only picked on merit - O'Neill

O'Neill and Graham retain places in NI squad

For the first time since June 2022, Northern Ireland will face four games in the same international window.

Starting away to Georgia on 25 September and finishing at home to the same opposition on 5 October, in between Michael O'Neill's side will face Hungary at Windsor Park and Ukraine in Slovakia.

The manager has named a 28-man panel for the games, compared to bringing 23 players along for June's double-header of friendlies against Guinea and France.

O'Neill said the schedule was challenging but that his team "must deal" with the change given the four-game window will be used again this time next year in Euro 2028 qualifying.

"I think for a smaller association, it poses more challenges if I'm honest. If a player picks up a calf strain the Saturday before we meet up, he's going to miss four games. It's a window that, I believe, is more beneficial for the bigger nations.

"I'm sure within the period, players will get injured, two bookings and I think you're suspended as well. It will be challenging, but it's the way the window will be going forward."

The campaign represents a step up in quality as well as quantity, not least when facing a player O'Neill calls one of the best in the world in Georgia's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia,

While Northern Ireland have sought friendlies against Spain, France, Sweden and Denmark across the past two and a half years, as well as facing Germany in World Cup qualifying, these will be the side's first games in the second tier of the Nations League since 2020.

Topping a League C group also containing Luxembourg, Belarus and Bulgaria last time around was enough to ensure a backdoor route into the World Cup play-offs this year where Northern Ireland were beaten 2-0 by Italy in Bergamo.

Naturally, promotion ensures securing such a safety net for Euro 2028 will be tougher, but League B status does mean a top-two finish in the group would see them in the second band of seeds for December's qualifying draw.

"I do think it's a group that is quite well matched in terms of where the teams are," said O'Neill.

"Obviously some of the teams are ranked a lot higher than us, I don't think we should be frightened by that.

"I think the games will be extremely tough, but I think it's a great challenge."

Reflecting on his role with Fifa's Technical Study Group at the World Cup, O'Neill said it was noteworthy to see how many games "were decided by individual brilliance" rather that general superiority of winning teams.

Once again, however, the manager will have to do without the player in his own squad most likely to produce such moments.

While Isaac Price has been a more regular source of goals, Liverpool's Conor Bradley has a talismanic quality. Since the beginning of 2025, however, the 23-year-old has endured a luckless run to miss seven Northern Ireland's games through either injury or suspension.

Still on the sidelines after January knee surgery, Bradley is expected to be absent for the entirety of this campaign, with O'Neill telling BBC Sport NI last month that it would be a "bonus" to see his captain before the start of Euro 2028 qualifying in March.

Since a 1-0 win over Scotland in March 2024, the occasion of Bradley's first international goal, Northern Ireland have averaged 1.5 goals a game in 16 internationals with him in the side compared to just 0.7 goals per game in the seven he has missed.

Finding a different creative spark in Bradley's absence will be key to the campaign.

While there was naturally disappointment after that loss to Italy in March, there has long been a sense that this group's best chance of major tournament qualification lies in the years ahead.

Of the starting XI that featured in Bergamo, only Hull City's 31-year-old defender Paddy McNair is older than 26.

The average age of the 28-man squad named last week was just 24-years-old with a quartet of teenagers - Ceadach O'Neill, Kieran Morrison, Braiden Graham and Tom Atcheson - giving the panel an even more youthful look.

In addition to McNair, the only two other players in the squad older than 30 are central striking options Dion Charles, 30, and Josh Magennis, 36.

O'Neill, however, is expected to stick with the 21-year-old Jamie Donley up top as he continues to build for the qualification campaigns ahead.

The Tottenham Hotspur player has scored twice in 10 caps and started the past five games for Northern Ireland, but he endured a difficult 2025-26 season at club level on loan at Stoke City and Oxford United.

Despite featuring for Spurs during pre-season, he will spend this year with Luton Town, back on loan in League One where he impressed for Leyton Orient in 2024-25.

"What happened with Jamie last year was not really of Jamie's doing," said O'Neill.

"The game time at Stoke was, I think, unfair on the player, to be honest. The second loan he gets injured in his first game but the games he did play, he did well.

"I think the thing for Jamie is just to play regularly. I think he's got all the attributes of a top, young player. He's still a Tottenham player on a long-term contract and I think he's gone to a good club (in Luton)."

title: The pros and cons of being a long-distance football manager
description: The pros and cons of being a long-distance football manager. Former Stoke City manager Tony Pulis talks to BBC Sport about how he managed teams despite keeping his family home hundreds of miles away.
fullText:
Managing a football club is a tough job at the best of times.

There's the constant pressure to get results, impatience from fans and club owners, along with endless media scrutiny.

For some managers, there's the added complication of commuting from their family home - in some cases from hundreds of miles away.

Frank Lampard is one such example, with the Coventry manager choosing to split his time between the Midlands and London.

Jose Mourinho lived in a hotel during his time at Manchester United - dividing his time between a luxury five-star suite and his home - also in London.

It might come as a surprise to learn that Arne Slot chose to live in Hale, Greater Manchester while managing Liverpool - just down the road from Old Trafford, but about an hour's drive from Anfield.

Being close to Manchester airport made it easier for him to visit his wife and children, who remained in the Netherlands.

One of the longest commutes in the UK belonged to Tony Pulis. The former Stoke City manager kept his home on the south coast during his time in Staffordshire, which meant a round trip of more than 400 miles.

He travelled even further when he joined Middlesbrough in 2017, clocking up a massive 320 miles each way.

BBC Sport talked to Pulis about how he and other bosses like Lampard, Mourinho and Slot make it work.

Pulis explained how he spent most, if not all, of his working week near the clubs he managed, but drove back to his family home after games.

"My wife was absolutely adamant where we lived on the south coast was the place to bring our children up, and she was right," said the 68-year-old, who played for, and then managed, Bournemouth until 1994.

"I never felt as if I was letting the club down by having my family home away from where the club was.

"I actually felt that without having the family there, I spent more time thinking about and preparing for what I was doing.

"It's not very nice to say, but that way there's more space for you to do all those things you need to do as a manager.

"Clubs were always very good to me about my living arrangements during the week. For example, I had an apartment when I was at Stoke, which was lovely - I always stayed in nice places, which helped.

"It was always good because it meant wherever I was, my wife and children could come up and stay as well."

Pulis, who managed Stoke for 10 years in two different spells, added: "When I was at Stoke, I would drive home to the south coast after a game on the Saturday.

"It could take me three hours or more, but it was precious time because I could spend much of it on the phone and it is when I would start my preparation for our next match.

"My chairman Peter Coates would always speak to me then if we lost. If we'd won, he never bothered, knowing I wouldn't need comforting.

"Win or lose, however, I would always ring my assistants, David Kemp and Gerry Francis, and we would discuss the game in finer detail - away from the stadium to give us a different perspective.

"Then I would contact my chief scout, who would have been at our next opponent's game, for a quick run-down of what he had seen - their shape, patterns, strength, weaknesses and any injuries.

"By the time I arrived home, whatever our result, I would have my dinner on a tray in front of the TV while watching a recording of our opponent's last game, which I could get downloaded.

"Sunday was about spending all day with the family, but then either late on Sunday night or early on Monday morning I would be back up the motorway, with a clear view of what I believed was needed for our next game.

"There are so many people in football who will tell you the same - that by jumping in the car, being by yourself and then picking the people you want to speak to, with no interference and no other phones going, you can just concentrate on what you want to. Whereas if you are in your office, you have got this and that going on.

"You might be involved in a really serious debate and then your chairman says he wants to speak to you - then you have to change all of that and go and find out what he wants.

"Whereas when you are in that car and you are by yourself, you have got time to think about everything. I always valued that time and thought it was really important - so it was more beneficial to me as an individual to live away from the club."

He added: "Having my family on the south coast didn't stop me from understanding what the DNA of Stoke City Football Club was. I got to know the area and the fans, and I wanted to give them a team they could identify with.

"Wherever I worked, I never felt I wasn't doing the job I was being paid to do - I always wanted my club to feel like a family.

"I always wanted everyone to feel as though they were part of the family - and the main thing was that everyone pulled and pushed in the right direction."

Pulis, whose last job in management was in 2020 with Sheffield Wednesday, admitted: "I did spend quite a lot of time away from home - my girls would probably tell you I spent more time working away than I should have.

"But that's the way it was for me when I was a manager. You have to get the balance right and I would never have tried to do my job remotely.

"I felt as if I had to be there, taking care of training and everything else during the week. It's about knowing what you think is going to make you successful.

"I don't think any manager would do anything but the right thing to make him and the team successful."

Tony Pulis was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

title: What will 'greatest captain' bring to Bellamy's Wales?
description: The return of former captain Ashley Williams to the Wales coaching team excites boss Craig Bellamy before their Nations League fixtures.
fullText:
Wales go into their Nations League openers aiming to shut out Cristiano Ronaldo and Erling Haaland.

With that kind of challenge, Craig Bellamy's squad might need all the defensive help they can get for games against Portugal, Denmark and Norway.

Cue Ashley Williams, the centre-back described by Bellamy as Wales' "greatest captain" of the modern era.

Williams was skipper as Wales reached the semi-finals of Euro 2016 against Ronaldo and Portugal, the peak of an international career that earned him 86 caps, wearing the armband for more than half of those appearances.

Now 42, the former Everton and Swansea City defender will not be adding to those appearances.

Instead, he will form part of a new-look Bellamy backroom team that the Football Association of Wales (FAW) hopes will add a missing ingredient in the bid to reach Euro 2028.

Bellamy says Williams, and fellow new coach Alan Sheehan, will help provide "a different dynamic".

But what exactly will they bring?

Colwill's 'surreal' Ronaldo and Haaland ambition

Wilson major Wales injury concern for Nations League

With Bellamy losing two key assistants just weeks after it seemed the Wales boss himself would walk away from the job amid interest from Burnley, Williams' arrival was something of a surprise.

His coaching experience has been limited to informal roles and fans are accustomed to seeing the much-admired ex-captain in the Match of the Day studio.

Sheehan, too, was not an expected announcement, with the former Leeds, Leicester and Luton full-back out of work since November 2025 when he was sacked by Swansea City following a relatively unsuccessful seven-month stint.

They replace James Rowberry, who has opted to focus on his role with Mark Robins at Stoke City, and Piet Cremers, a man whose analytical work Bellamy said meant "everything" but left to join Belgium's Club NXT in July.

Cremers spent time under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City and worked with Bellamy and Vincent Kompany during their successful period at Burnley.

He was often the person Bellamy turned to mid-match, but Bellamy says he was already keen to take on more of the tasks that Cremers performed.

"I loved this summer interviewing people, seeing who could add to us," said the 47-year-old, who has seen former Wales midfielder and now Tottenham assistant Andrew Crofts remain part of the setup.

"It freshens you up, gives you a different eye. Different strengths coming in means a different dynamic to how you work, which leaves me quite excited."

The obvious strength Williams brings is his personality.

Past team-mates for club and country will queue up to attest to his character as a player and a person.

With Bellamy's Wales a young side, it mirrors the role the more experienced Williams played while on the field.

As senior to the likes of Gareth Bale and Aaron Ramsey, he was a leader among equals.

"I played underneath Ash as a captain, and he was a great leader in the dressing room and led by example in the way he conducted himself on and off the pitch," says Euro 2016 colleague Sam Vokes.

"He can be someone who speaks from experience and [will] go into that dressing room and immediately command respect.

"Portugal and Denmark away, he has played in those environments.

"He will be able to speak to the lads that are going out in those environments because he led by example, and led in the trenches many times."

Bellamy agrees, having retained a friendship with the former Swansea skipper after sharing a dressing room with Wales.

"In my time he's been our greatest captain," says Bellamy. "Some ex-players with a certain presence can really add something, but also his knowledge of the game is really high, his football IQ is really high."

Wales might need it at the back.

The appointments come against the backdrop of Wales' failure to reach the World Cup and the beginnings of criticism around the side's openness.

"He'll bring some unique skills, particularly when you play Nations League A games when you have to defend a lot," said FAW chief football officer Dave Adams of Williams' appointment on the Feast of Football podcast.

"Some of the dark arts of defending, he'll bring some interesting things for the players to think about."

There is the thought that Williams would also be prepared to challenge Bellamy's thinking – seen as healthy part of a management team.

But while Bellamy says he is keen to lean on Williams' defensive know-how, it will still be the former Liverpool, Manchester City and Newcastle forward's managerial message.

"With his position, sometimes it's easier coming from a player who's been in there," said Bellamy - a former Wales captain himself.

"Now, I'll lead a lot on the information, but it's nice for me to be able to ask 'What would you see with this? If you played there, how did you feel when I asked you to do that? Is that possible? Is that not possible?' I believe he'll be a huge asset to me."

Sheehan's appointment also suggested a more defensive focus.

The former Republic of Ireland Under-21 international was seen to have a pragmatic style at Swansea.

But it appears Wales will look to benefit from the 40-year-old's eye for set-piece work, something he has also been responsible for during previous coaching roles at Luton and Southampton.

"We really want someone who is in tune with restarts and set-pieces," added Adams.

"In these sorts of games they could be the factor that give us a chance to win the game, because they are going to be very hard games to play in.

"We realise the importance of attacking and defending set-pieces in these next six games, and feel Alan and [goalkeeping coach] Martyn Margetson will bring that level of detail to help the team be best prepared for these games."

title: Chiefs back in business as star QBs go down - five things from NFL week two
description: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs look back to their best but Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels suffer serious injuries. Here's what you need to know from week two in the NFL.
fullText:
After a feast of points in week one, defences hit back in week two of the NFL.

The Chicago Bears came crashing back down to earth after a flying start - and they suffered one of the two worrying injuries to two of the league's top young quarterbacks.

The Kansas City Chiefs were back doing what they do best but the Baltimore Ravens were surprisingly beaten, while two games were settled in overtime and one decided with just nine seconds on the clock.

Here's our pick from Sunday's week two action.

Allen stars as Bills open new stadium in style

The Chicago Bears scored 59 points last week but just three this time in an ugly 9-3 home loss to the Vikings, as Minnesota won their seventh straight game at Soldier Field.

The 56-point drop-off is the second most in NFL history as the Bears saw two touchdowns lost with a dropped catch and a fumble, had a field goal blocked but worst of all lost their star quarterback Caleb Williams.

The first pick of the 2024 draft was carried off the field in the fourth quarter looking in serious pain, but initial reports are that his hamstring injury may not be as serious as first feared.

Jayden Daniels was the second pick of that 2024 draft behind Williams and he left Washington's defeat at Dallas with a serious injury to the same elbow he dislocated last season.

Daniels, who seems certain to be out for some time, would still have struggled to keep up with Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott who threw four touchdowns in their 37-20 victory.

Prescott surpassed Tony Romo's team record of 248 touchdown passes by taking his tally to 249.

The Kansas City Chiefs gave another ominous sign that they were back in business with a 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Winning tight games was a hallmark of the Patrick Mahomes dynasty during three recent Super Bowl wins, so there was a familiar feeling when Harrison Butker kicked the winning field goal right at the death.

Mahomes threw three touchdowns and his 382 passing yards was his most for three years. Travis Kelce had 101 yards and a touchdown and summer signing Kenneth Walker had another huge game.

The Super Bowl MVP had 178 total yards and was crucial in overtime to help overcome a strong challenge from Daniel Jones and the Colts - who may have lost their first two games but look to have plenty to build on.

The Green Bay Packers also triumphed in overtime by erasing a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter against the New York Jets to win 20-17 - and snap a six-game losing streak.

Super Bowl champions Seattle look the real deal again after beating the Arizona Cardinals 31-7 for a 12th straight win.

Drew Lock showed he is no ordinary back-up quarterback with three touchdown passes to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, including an 82 yarder that is the longest of the talented receiver's career.

The Seahawks lost Walker to the Chiefs but have retained a remarkable 17 of 22 starters and 44 of their 53-man roster from last season's title win.

That consistency should see them go close again, but they'll face a rejuvenated San Francisco 49ers in their division, who are also 2-0 after beating the Miami Dolphins 35-15.

Showing no signs of jet leg from their victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, the Niners scored touchdowns on their first five possessions to blow Miami away - Christian McCaffrey scored twice, George Kittle also found the end zone and Brock Purdy accounted for three scores.

With the 49ers having their defensive stars back from injury Kyle Shanahan's squad look the total package once again.

The Cincinnati Bengals also look more well rounded this season after winning a 20-6 battle in Houston, thanks to an early touchdown of the season contender catch from Ja'Marr Chase.

We expect fireworks from Chase and Joe Burrow, but having a defence capable of keeping CJ Stroud out of the end zone, and sacking him four times in a road game is the biggest reason for optimism among Bengals fans.

The Philadelphia Eagles were on the ropes against the Tennessee Titans until Jalen Hurts threw the winning touchdown pass to Darius Cooper with just nine seconds left in the game.

Although not as impressive overall as other 2-0 sides, that ability to win games at the death is a familiar trait with Philly - and will make them dangerous all season again.

The New Orleans Saints just fell short after a monster comeback in Detroit last week, but went one better this week by upsetting Lamar Jackson's Baltimore Ravens 24-17 in their home opener.

Tyler Shough bundled over in a big crowd for a slightly controversial touchdown given the ball was largely unsighted, before two-time MVP Jackson then threw a late interception when trying to salvage the game.

The Saints may just surprise a few more teams this season.

Surprising everyone right now are the Las Vegas Raiders, who sit on 2-0 after winning 26-14 at the hapless Chargers.

The Chargers have lost by double digits to two of last season's biggest strugglers and with away games at Buffalo and Seattle, things look likely to get much worse.

DeShaun Watson threw a fourth quarter touchdown as the Cleveland Browns also sprung an upset win on the road in Tampa Bay, with a weather delay meaning they had to wait an extra two hours to seal the deal.

Perhaps the biggest surprise so far though is just how bad the Atlanta Falcons are. They were beaten 34-3 by the Carolina Panthers to become just the fourth team since 1978 to fail to get into an opponents red zone in their first two games.

The quarterback mess has played a part - and what summed them up nicely was undrafted rookie Jack Strand replacing a struggling Cooper Rush, and duly threw a pick six.

Atlanta could already be eyeing the first draft pick next year if this continues.

title: Edwards signs short-term deal with Red Roses
description: Shaun Edwards has started a short-term coaching consultancy role with England women.
fullText:
Shaun Edwards has started a short-term coaching consultancy role with England women.

It is understood the 59-year-old will work with current Red Roses defence coach Sarah Hunter for the rest of their WXV Global Series matches, starting with New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday.

The news comes after England's 39-Test winning streak ended with a 26-26 draw against Canada last weekend.

Englishman Edwards is one of the most decorated coaches in rugby union. He recently left his role as France men's defence coach, where he won three Six Nations titles.

He has never previously worked for England's men or women.

His playing career in rugby league saw him win 36 caps for Great Britain before coaching success with London Wasps and Wales and a six-year stint with France.

On the appointment of Edwards, England head coach John Mitchell said: "Since his time with France ended, we have had a conversation about our game, and he expressed an interest in working in an international women's set-up for the first time.

"He has a huge amount of respect for the Red Roses and what we stand for; he sees it as a privilege to join our environment.

"His coaching credentials are exceptional and his experience at the highest level of the game speaks for itself.

"Defensively, Sarah Hunter is relishing the opportunity to learn from him, alongside the rest of our coaching group, as we head into another exciting Test match against New Zealand."

Last week, Edwards expressed his desire to return to coaching and be a part of next year's men's Six Nations.

"I'm def­in­itely open to offers now, until I sort out a full-time role," he told the Daily Mail., external

"I'm a proud Englishman and everybody loves to represent their country, don't they? I'm no different."

title: Gibbs-White set to replace Palmer in England squad
description: Morgan Gibbs-White is in line for an England recall to replace Cole Palmer, who is set to withdraw from the squad because of a minor injury.
fullText:
Morgan Gibbs-White is in line for an England recall to replace Cole Palmer, who is set to withdraw from the squad because of a minor injury.

Nottingham Forest midfielder Gibbs-White missed out on selection in the initial squad for the upcoming Nations League matches, but is set to be called up.

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel admitted on Friday that Gibbs-White was close to making the cut and the 26-year-old is now expected to replace Chelsea's Palmer.

Palmer, 24, had been recalled by Tuchel after being controversially left out of England's World Cup squad.

Tuchel previously said Palmer had a "point to prove" and needed "to step up" to "keep his shirt and justify the nomination".

However, the Blues forward will now miss the extended international break in which England play four games.

The Three Lions face World Cup winners Spain at Wembley on Saturday, 26 September, then travel to the Czech Republic (29 September) and Croatia (3 October) before hosting the Czechs on 6 October.

Manchester United duo Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo are also both thought to be injury doubts for England.

They are being assessed by their club after being taken off in the closing stages of Sunday's 1-1 draw at Fulham.

If Mainoo withdraws, it is understood Everton midfielder James Garner - who made his senior England debut in March but was not selected for the World Cup - is a strong option to replace him.

Tuchel recalls Alexander-Arnold and Palmer with warning

How does the Nations League work and who is in each league?

Palmer's withdrawal comes after he played the full game for Chelsea in their 3-0 defeat at Brentford on Friday.

Following a summer off after missing out on World Cup selection, he has started six of Chelsea's seven games and played the full 90 minutes in five of them - scoring four goals and providing two assists.

Palmer, who last played for England in their 1-0 friendly defeat by Japan in March, was hampered by a recurring groin injury in 2025-26, which Chelsea had to manage.

Gibbs-White made his most recent England appearance in a 3-0 friendly win against Wales in October 2025.

He has one goal and two assists from Forest's five league games this season.

title: 'I've asked for forgiveness' - Eckert and Southampton braced for Spygate verdict
description: As Southampton manager Tonda Eckert awaits the FA hearing into his 'Spygate' misconduct conduct charge BBC sports editor Dan Roan speaks to him and club chief executive Phil Parsons on what happens next.
fullText:
More than four months since the Spygate scandal erupted, Southampton manager Tonda Eckert's wait to discover his fate for authorising an espionage campaign is almost over.

This week, a decisive Football Association hearing is set to take place, after the German coach was charged with misconduct in July.

Spying on three clubs has already cost Southampton the chance of promotion to the Premier League (worth £200m), after they were expelled from the Championship play-off final. An EFL panel also docked the club four points for this season.

As the club prepared for the latest twist in the saga, BBC Sport spoke exclusively to both Eckert and Southampton chief executive Phil Parsons, who - in his first interview on the case - insists any further punishment would be "really tough to take".

But how are the club and their coach dealing with the prospect of more turmoil? What is at stake? And why have Southampton given a permanent role to the intern who was caught spying on Middlesbrough in May?

"I would lie if I say that the summer has just been easy. Of course, if you care deeply about your profession, about the football club, there's nothing that prepares you for that. There just isn't."

Eckert speaks slowly and with an intense gaze when asked to reflect on being at the centre of one of the biggest controversies in English football history.

The 33-year-old apologised in June after an EFL independent disciplinary commission found he had orchestrated a "contrived and determined plan" to spy on Oxford United, Ipswich Town, then Middlesbrough before the play-off semi-final.

Having insisted he was unaware it breached EFL rules, and that the spying had no impact on performances, Eckert was backed by Southampton.

His team have made an encouraging start to the new season. Without the four-point deduction, they would be fourth in the table, rather than 13th.

"We've talked a lot over the summer of how we want to go through that process of addressing everything, giving everyone the chance to put questions out that are still there, to put out what they feel and have gone through, and then also close the door and move on," he says.

"Because the reality is it's a new season. We have big ambitions as a football club, and in order to reach them, we need to move on."

That is easier said than done, with Eckert in limbo while he awaits the outcome of the FA's disciplinary process.

"I've had the chance to sit down and just talk the FA through everything that happened," he says. "And now it's up to them to make a decision. I don't really have any emotions towards that."

So does he feel the FA has listened to him during its investigation?

"That was my impression," he says. "We sat for almost four hours, so it's been quite a long conversation."

When asked whether he feels the club has been punished enough, and if a suspension for him would be excessive, Eckert chooses his words carefully.

"It's been a big, big punishment," he says. "Absolutely unheard of in the history of sports.

"And it's tough for me to say that because it concerns me. I'm judging on myself, not an outside situation. But I've asked for forgiveness for what I've done. I've apologised publicly.

"I think the punishment has been very hard on the club for the last season. And to go into a new season on minus four. And the rest is not for me to decide."

Southampton owner will not sack head coach Eckert

Parsons is more forthright on whether the club has been punished enough.

"We don't know what the FA will actually hand out," he says. "It could be a long ban. It could be a short ban. It could be a suspended sentence.

"What we hope as a club is they actually recognise where we are at the moment, and what we've already been through, because I think it has to be taken into account. I really feel like we've taken enough. We've been hurt. I think it's one of the largest sanctions ever when it comes to football, or even sporting, history.

"This isn't just about the club, this is about people. We lose money not being in the Premier League, but [local] businesses lose money. We had to spend a huge amount on legal fees, and it really impacts the club even further. We don't want to be seen as a victim of this. We need to get on. We've had our cards dealt."

When it is put to Parsons that the EFL's punishments applied to the club - rather than Eckert himself - he says: "I think it's impossible to sanction the manager without the club getting hurt even more."

The most recent precedent for this case came at the 2024 Olympics women's tournament, when Fifa banned Bev Priestman - Canada's head coach - from all football for a year, after opponents New Zealand were spied on.

Parsons insists "the Canadian case is very different" but if Eckert , who is only contracted until the end of the season, is also banned, how long would it have to be for the club to look elsewhere for a new coach?

"We don't know," he says, firmly denying having approached other coaches in case Eckert has to leave. Parsons also says the club may appeal if the ruling goes against them.

"We can't worry about something we can't control at the moment," he says. "We have to deal with it when we get there but we're hoping that they look at it sensibly."

Parsons says the club's ownership "want" to back Eckert.

"We've been through an entire transfer window when it comes to recruiting players for Tonda, and that's another challenge.

"We have to be looking at all scenarios. We've always spoken about any punishment being disproportionate...You're looking for fairness in approach. And have we had that treatment to us, from a disproportionate punishment? Well, I think a lot of people will view it that way. But do we want to sit there moaning about it? No.

"But it's going to be really tough to take if we get another punishment, on top of being thrown out of the play-offs, four points this season, and potentially more. So we're really hoping that the FA, the panel, are looking as this with a balanced view to what's already happened, because it's been really heavy."

When compared to the £10m fines that both the FA and Premier League handed Chelsea this year for making £47m in secret payments related to transfers across several seasons when they were owned by Roman Abramovich, some would agree Southampton have suffered enough.

Others however, would say the FA has little choice but to sanction Eckert.

After all, according to the EFL commission, the club employed "a particularly deplorable approach" by using junior members of staff to conduct the spying "at the direction of senior personnel".

An arbitration panel then detailed how a junior analyst intern said he felt under "extreme pressure".

Southampton's initial response to the crisis also contained "inaccuracies". Middlesbrough's head of football Kieran Scott said the club's behaviour had been "disgusting"., external

Parsons shrugs off such criticism.

And when it is put to him that many expected Southampton to sack Eckert, and had they done so they would not be facing the current uncertainty, he replies: "Yeah, but Tonda also picked up the team in around 20th place in the Championship, and without him and his team we wouldn't have been in the play-off positions, and I think that deserves a bit of loyalty.

"OK, he has made a mistake and he's paid for that dearly. This has been really tough for him as a person already. I admire how strong he's been through this process because a lot of people could have cracked, the amount of pressure he was under."

For his part, Eckert says he is "very grateful for the support of the club because that could have been very different, and I think in most cases would have been very different".

The vast majority of Southampton fans that BBC Sport spoke to also seem to fully back the manager, something he says "means everything" to him.

Another to be supported is the intern involved - Will Salt - who was recently handed a permanent role as an analyst in the club's academy.

The scandal began when a photograph was published of Salt secretly filming Boro from behind a tree at their training ground before the play-off semi-final.

"He's been through a tough time," says Parsons.

"When your photo is put out to the public, that is something tough to deal with. A lot of people probably underestimated how that could have impacted a young lad so we've got a job to make sure that he's looked after in his early career. But he's a talented boy as well. I get good feedback and he's got a good role at the club."

Asked if reintegrating Salt had been challenging, given his allegations about the way he was treated, Parsons says: "I don't think Will said he felt under pressure directly from Tonda himself. He felt under pressure in the situation. And everybody knows in a job you can feel under pressure.

"But, yeah, I think Will's managed himself really well, and he'll grow from this."

So has the club learned its lessons? Parsons insists Eckert has studied the EFL's regulations, but also argues the rules could be clearer.

"They're very grey - that's something I'll continue to raise in EFL meetings," he says.

"But look, we've done something wrong, we'll get on with it."

Moving on is not easy, though. Last week, Wrexham's owners aimed a dig at Southampton by referencing the scandal in a social media advert before the two teams met. And during matches, rival fans regularly remind the club of the scandal.

"History is history and it'll be a part of our story going forwards," says Parsons. "It's about how we react now. It's given us a real togetherness and hopefully that continues through the season because we're stronger like that anyway.

"There's a bit of siege mentality as well, right - of 'everybody's against us', so we've got to embrace it."

The Championship has now paused until next month for the international break.

For now, however, his future remains uncertain.

title: 'Far from their best' to 'a joy to watch' -  ranking Premier League teams' start to season
description: Five matches into the league season, which teams in the Premier League have impressed so far and who have disappointed?
fullText:
There is now a three-week international break with no Premier League games until 10 October.

We are five matches into the league season and there is a long way to go in the campaign, but which teams have impressed so far and who have disappointed?

You can have your say in the comments at the bottom of the page.

Arsenal: Solid start to their title defence until they were ripped apart by Brighton having survived a penalty scare at Sunderland. 7

Aston Villa: Signs they are beginning to move in the right direction after losing so many key players during the transfer window. 6

Bournemouth: If games lasted 80 minutes the Cherries would be near the top of the table. Need to cut out conceding so late. 6

Brentford: Demolished Spurs and Chelsea without fuss during a highly impressive unbeaten start. Can they keep it up and challenge for Europe? 8

Brighton: Kings of entertainment after hitting 16 goals in five top-flight games, including three against champions Arsenal. A joy to watch. 9

Chelsea: After a strong start under Xabi Alonso, the Blues have lost two of their past three - and were picked apart by Brentford. Are they really moving in the right direction? 6

Coventry City: You could hear the sighs of relief in the away end at Nottingham Forest on Saturday. Will Frank Lampard's side kick on after that win? 6

Crystal Palace: Room for improvement after one win and three defeats. 5

Everton: Despite a transfer window to forget, David Moyes has made the Toffees hard to beat. 6

Fulham: Decent draws against Liverpool and Manchester United but need a win. Ipswich (away) followed by Hull (home), Coventry (away) and Crystal Palace (home) offer hope when they return from the international break. 5

Hull City: To have eight points from a tough opening five fixtures is an excellent return, including beating Manchester United and drawing with Aston Villa and Chelsea. 8

Ipswich Town: Defensively vulnerable but two late winners, against Sunderland and Crystal Palace, have earned them six points and shown their fighting spirit. 5

Leeds United: Fifth in the league, unbeaten and with the joint-best defensive record. They showed what they are capable of with a superb 4-1 win over Newcastle. 7

Liverpool: Unbeaten but have been far from their best. Three clean sheets in their past three games, but more is expected from Andoni Iraola's side. 6

Manchester City: Five league games, five victories. Managed to win at Manchester United despite going down to 10 men midway through the first half. With Erling Haaland already top scorer, City fans will expect a real push to win the league. 9

Manchester United: Disappointing performances to lose at Hull and draw at a Fulham side who were bottom of the league. Their only win so far came against Ipswich and they were denied a victory at Everton by a late equaliser. 4

Newcastle United: A mixed bag under new manager Matthias Jaissle. They impressed in a draw against Liverpool, won comfortably at Tottenham, but were also terrible in a loss at Leeds, although they responded well to beat Hull. 6

Nottingham Forest: Their best results have come away, drawing at Liverpool and winning at Aston Villa. But their home form will be a huge worry - yet to score a goal and with only one point from three matches at the City Ground. 5

Sunderland: After coming seventh in 2025-26, Sunderland fans will have wanted a better start to this season. The Black Cats gave good accounts of themselves against Arsenal and Manchester City, but lost both matches. 5

Tottenham Hotspur: After spending more than £300m in the summer, Spurs have been poor, failing to score in their opening four league matches. Supporters will be demanding an instant improvement after the international break. 2
