title: Why Cardiff is set to win race to host Fury-Joshua
description: Why Cardiff is set to beat competition from London and New York to host the long-awaited fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.
fullText:
The long-awaited heavyweight fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua is expected to take place at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Friday, 11 December.

While BBC Sport understands final details are still being hammered out between Netflix, Saudi Arabian organisers Sela and both fighters' camps, Cardiff has firmly emerged as the frontrunner, with an official announcement expected this week.

It marks another dramatic twist in a saga that, only weeks ago, appeared destined for New York. A date at Madison Square Garden was so close to completion that plans were already being drawn up for a Manhattan news conference.

Instead, after Joshua and promoter Eddie Hearn refused to budge on their contractual right to stage the fight on British soil, the Welsh capital has taken centre stage.

BBC Sport takes a look at how Cardiff became the leading candidate to host what would arguably be the biggest event in British boxing in the 21st Century.

Wembley Stadium was long assumed to be the natural home for a meeting between the two defining British heavyweights of their generation. However, the path to making the fight was complicated by Joshua and Fury having signed separate agreements with Sela rather than a joint contract.

Joshua's deal explicitly stipulated that the bout must take place in the United Kingdom, whereas Fury's contained no such restriction.

That distinction proved critical when organisers and broadcast partner Netflix began lobbying to move the show to the United States.

Hearn acknowledged that virtually every other party involved preferred New York, with Matchroom even exploring what compensation would be required to waive the UK clause.

For a moment, that stand-off threatened to scupper the entire event. Fury publicly accused Joshua of stalling and briefly floated the prospect of a trilogy fight with Oleksandr Usyk.

But once Fury relented, organisers needed to find a British venue capable of satisfying the broadcast demands without leaving fans exposed to the British winter.

Cardiff, almost by process of elimination, became the answer.

The fight had initially been discussed for November but, with negotiations over the venue dragging on, it now looks set for December.

Staging an open-air stadium fight in the UK at that time carries immense risk.

While Wembley offers unmatched prestige, exposing tens of thousands of fans and a massive international broadcast operation to potentially freezing temperatures, wind and rain was deemed unacceptable.

Moving the event indoors to an arena like London's O2 would eliminate weather risks, but at the cost of sacrificing tens of thousands of ticket sales.

The Principality Stadium's retractable roof allows organisers to capture the immense scale, atmosphere and gate revenue of a stadium show while offering full protection from the elements.

The venue's official seated capacity is just under 74,000, but boxing configurations allow for even larger crowds.

Joshua has already proven he can sell out the venue, having defended his WBA and IBF titles there against Carlos Takam in front of nearly 80,000 fans in 2017 before adding the WBO belt against Joseph Parker five months later.

We want Fury v Joshua at Wembley - London mayor

Fury says he is looking for new opponent, calls out Usyk

'Bring it on' - Cardiff businesses react to Fury vs Joshua rumours

Perhaps the most difficult hurdle has been aligning the event with Netflix's preference to broadcast during prime-time hours in the United States.

A projected UK ring walk of about 01:00 GMT - 20:00 on the US east coast - created a logistical headache for London. Wembley operates under a strict 23:00 event curfew.

While Mayor of London Sadiq Khan offered his support and Wembley officials were open to discussions, securing the necessary approvals from Brent Council and local safety advisory groups for a 01:00 start presented an administrative hurdle.

Cardiff offers a far smoother path. The Welsh Rugby Union, which owns and operates the Principality Stadium, previously indicated it would be delighted to host the fight and confirmed a late-night finish would not be a dealbreaker.

While early-hours finishes still require extensive coordination around transport, policing and crowd management in the city centre, the venue already holds a clear precedent for late-night boxing. In 2007, Joe Calzaghe's super-middleweight unification victory over Mikkel Kessler did not start until 02:00 local time to satisfy American television network Showtime.

For all the delays and frustrations that have plagued this rivalry over the past decade, Fury against Joshua remains the pinnacle of domestic boxing. Downgrading to an indoor arena would diminish the magnitude of the occasion.

Crucially, taking the fight to America would have deprived domestic fans of a generational spectacle. British supporters have driven the commercial value of this rivalry for years, filling stadiums for both fighters' respective careers and following every collapsed negotiation.

Staging the bout on home soil serves as a long-overdue reward for that loyalty, even if both men are now former world heavyweight champions.

A stadium fight of this magnitude dominates the national conversation in a way a 04:00 New York or Las Vegas broadcast simply cannot, and local amateur boxing clubs could see a surge in interest when the country's biggest stars compete on home soil.

Wales also has history of staging a huge fight between two British heavyweights: In 1993, Lennox Lewis defended his WBC title against Frank Bruno at Cardiff Arms Park - the venue that the Principality Stadium replaced.

When the demands surrounding the event are broken down, Cardiff's emergence becomes easier to understand.

fullText:
Unit1 hopes to offer lower cost version of shows such as Abba Voyage, showcasing living and dead artists in any venue

The former chief executive of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s entertainment group has obtained a near-£15m investment for his UK music tech startup that hopes to recreate classic concerts by manifesting musicians as digital avatars.

Unit1 was set up last year by Barney Wragg, an entertainment executive who ran Lord Lloyd-Webber’s Cats-to-Evita empire for five years from late 2011. It has secured the $20m in funding from a group of investors, including tech backer Balderton Capital through its partner Daniel Waterhouse, who made early investments in Spotify.

The company hopes to stage concerts fronted by the “hyper realistic” digital avatars of living artists who are no longer touring and by recreating existing performances from dead musicians. In the latter case, it will develop the avatars through a mixture of archive footage and hiring actors and musicians who either look or play like the departed star, before blending the footage together.

Unit1 has tested the technology with Scottish singer-songwriter and musician KT Tunstall, who worked with Wragg during a stint at the music company EMI. In the pilot, Tunstall was filmed in a London studio by motion capture cameras as she recreated a two-decade-old performance on Later… with Jools Holland, using the avatar to update her features to the way she looks now.

The music industry has long flirted with the idea of creating avatars of its biggest stars, such as the 2012 hologram projection of the late rapper Tupac Shakur alongside Snoop Dogg and Dr Dre at Coachella festival.

The concept found mainstream success with the 2022 launch of Abba Voyage, a lucrative virtual concert with avatars of the Swedish pop group, which runs in a purpose-built venue in east London.

Unit1 hopes to offer a lower cost to produce version of the Abba Voyage experience, by providing artists, venues, their rights holders and promoters with a route to digital shows without needing a dedicated space. The setup also means a show could in theory tour in several countries simultaneously.

The business will invest the fresh funds into research and development, as well as securing intellectual property and licensing deals with artists and their estates.

Unit1’s aim is to stage shows with real musicians playing live instruments on stage alongside digital performers. The audience will view a high-definition LED screen, which is combined with extra lights, sound and props to give them the illusion they are watching a fully human performance.

“For the audience member in the room it is seamless between the digital and the physical room, immersing them,” Wragg told the Guardian. “It’s a teleportation of an audience member to a time and place.”

However, some fans have expressed unease about dead musicians being digitally resurrected. Earlier this year, a plan to create a lifesize AI-powered avatar of the late Black Sabbath frontman Ozzy Osbourne was criticised as being disrespectful and in poor taste by some fans.

Wragg said that, in most cases, the startup was “dealing with family members of estates to create something which is well documented and understood – extremely well-known concerts or live recordings. We are mindful that you do not want to be distasteful.”

He was tight-lipped on which classic concerts Unit1 could recreate. He has previously said he wished he could have seen various well-known performances, including Queen at Live Aid, the Beatles’ performances at the Cavern Club and Jimi Hendrix at Woodstock.

Balderton – which has also backed music rights firm Kobalt and fintech Revolut – was joined in the funding round by its existing investors, including the venture capital firm Mercuri and Paul McGuinness, the Irish music executive who managed U2 from the late 1970s until 2013.

title: Nvidia boss says there is ‘0% chance’ AI destroys the world by 2030
description: Jensen Huang dismisses warnings from former Anthropic researcher and others as ‘doomsday...
fullText:
Jensen Huang dismisses warnings from former Anthropic researcher and others as ‘doomsday narratives’

The boss of the chipmaker Nvidia has said AI will not develop to a point that will lead to the extinction of the human race within a few years, rejecting such assertions as overblown “doomsday narratives”.

Jensen Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of the $5tn AI chipmaker, said the claims made on social media by the former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon that AI could become “superhuman” and kill off humanity within the decade were “irresponsible”.

“2030 is not going to be the end of the world. There is 0% chance that’s going to be the end of the world,” Huang said in an interview with CBS News. “Scaring people is unnecessary. It is irresponsible.”

Coxon’s remarks, which were backed by two other researchers at the maker of the AI system Claude, prompted an international debate about the dangers and lack of oversight of AI as companies race to develop ever more powerful models.

US lawmakers have criticised AI companies over the risks and Anthropic published a threat intelligence report detailing how criminals, state-sponsored groups, spyware vendors, scientists and propagandists have tried to use its powerful AI models to design missiles and bombs, create deadly pathogens and spy on dissidents.

Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, Sam Altman, the boss of the ChatGPT maker OpenAI, and Elon Musk have called for development of the technology to be slowed down.

However, Donald Trump has dismissed anxiety over the AI development as a “hoax” and a “conspiracy”, adding that a slowdown could give China the edge.

On Sunday, Scott Bessent, the US Treasury secretary, said the US and China had agreed to set up an AI dialogue mechanism to alert each other to help contain the technology’s potential dangers.

Huang said predictions of an extinction-level event caused by AI were “not grounded in science”.

Huang also claimed AI companies’ recent calls for national and international safety regulation aim to duck existing laws that would hold them to account.

Citing recent cases where AI companies including Anthropic and OpenAI triggered cybersecurity incidents during testing, he said there were plenty of laws to tackle the problems.

“You have cybersecurity unauthorised entry laws, you have damage liabilities … if your product does harm, if your product doesn’t perform as you promised, and if you entered into contracts with companies for service level agreements, there are plenty of laws associated with that. My point is, apply those first. And don’t let this doomsday narrative cause somebody to relieve them of the laws that currently exist.”

He continued: “Now, go and read between the lines. They’re actually not asking for more laws. They’re asking to be relieved of the laws we do have. And I think that’s a problem.”

On Monday the the Tony Blair Institute (TBI) thinktank published a paper arguing that countries risk “profound and compounding disadvantage” if they fail to embrace AI and fall behind other nations.

However, it also warned that the institutions meant to support the choices leaders would have to make were not equipped to do so.

“The previous [industrial] revolution transformed our world over generations, AI will do so within a decade,” said Tony Blair in a foreword to the paper. “New capabilities are emerging at an extraordinary pace, with profound implications for economies, education, science, labour markets, public services and national security. But the risks are equally profound and growing, and so too is public concern.

“Today’s political leaders… must make hard choices that will signficantly alter their countries’ trajectories. However, the institutions of the modern state meant to support political leaders in making these choices are simply not equipped for what is coming.”

title: More Australians will be dying than being born in 40 years as major report predicts future of lower growth
description: Seventh intergenerational report also outlines how Australia is on the brink of an uncertain age of artificial...
fullText:
Seventh intergenerational report also outlines how Australia is on the brink of an uncertain age of artificial intelligence

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

There will be more Australians dying than being born in 40 years’ time, according to the government’s latest intergenerational report, which lays bare the fundamental challenges of managing an ageing population at a time of rapid change and lower economic growth.

The country’s seventh IGR also outlines how Australia is on the brink of a new and uncertain age of artificial intelligence that will shape the economy and society over the coming four decades.

Jim Chalmers, in a speech at the Australian National University to coincide with the release of the analysis, said “this intergenerational report illuminates the road ahead”.

“No previous IGR has contended with global challenges this great, with politics this fraught, or a future less certain. The global and generational risks are serious, but Australia’s opportunities are endless,” the treasurer said.

The latest 40-year projections show the population will keep getting older as people have fewer children, to the point where falling fertility rates mean deaths are for the first time projected to outnumber births by the 2060s.

“This is a milestone that many advanced economies have already surpassed, including Japan, Germany, Italy and the Republic of Korea, with most of the rest expected to do so over coming decades,” the report says.

With the population set to grow by 0.9% for the foreseeable future, versus 1.4% historically, alongside a shrinking share of working Australians to support activity and the budget, the IGR predicts the economy has entered into a new normal of lower growth.

Living standards will still improve, but not as quickly as in the past, the IGR shows.

Real GDP on a per person basis will expand by about 1.2% over the next 40 years, down from 1.5% in the previous four decades, the IGR shows.

Even that relatively dour outlook depends on productivity picking back up from virtually zero in recent years to the historical average of 1.2% – an assumption that leans heavily on AI, or what Chalmers described as “the biggest economic transformation of our lifetime”.

“The rise and adoption of AI is likely to support the achievement of Treasury’s long-term labour productivity growth assumption over time,” the report says, while the treasurer described its role as “pivotal”.

“As a medium-sized economy, Australia’s productivity performance will depend on adopting innovation, supporting investment, developing skills and delivering regulatory reforms that improve the efficient operation of the economy,” the report says.

The forecasts underline the tightrope the government must walk between protecting Australians from the worst aspects of the new technology, and not stifling a technology that could almost single-handedly drive future prosperity.

The IGR is a five-yearly exercise, although it was most recently published in 2023 after Covid interrupted its scheduling.

Peter Costello, a former Liberal treasurer, first conceived of the IGR and formally enshrined it in the Charter of Budget Honesty Act of 1998 as a way to explain how demographic shifts affect the budget over the very long term.

First released in 2002, each report has highlighted similar challenges associated with an ageing population: pressures on delivering services to older Australians and how to pay for them – not least dealing with the growing tax burden on a shrinking share of workers.

The IGR projects an ongoing, structural budget deficit over coming decades, as it shrinks over the next 10 years before expanding again over the following 40.

Government payments as a share of GDP are anticipated to rise by 1.1 percentage points to 27.4% by the mid-2060s.

“As the scale and interaction of these structural trends intensify, maintaining a sustainable budget position will require policies and ongoing reforms that manage growing spending and revenue challenges,” the report says.

This year’s report also included a section of six “major transitions” for the next 40 years, topped by the AI “revolution” and geopolitical fragmentation.

The next four challenges were the energy transition, ageing and the care economy, the country’s “industrial transformation”, and intergenerational equity.

“The world is becoming more dangerous, more unpredictable, more unequal, and more divided. These are not just individual threads but part of a bigger fraying of that intergenerational promise, of better times,” Chalmers said.

The treasurer said responding successfully to these major challenges would be the key to defeating populist insurgencies that sought to weaponise public discontent for political ends.

The IGRs provide a robust argument in favour of the compulsory superannuation regime, which has largely offset the huge budgetary impact experienced in other countries associated with funding retirement incomes.

description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met China's Vice Premier He Lifeng [Treasury Secretary Scott...
fullText:
Top US and Chinese officials have discussed creating a new "notification mechanism" for AI incidents that could affect national security, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters on Sunday.

Bessent made the comments after what he called "successful" talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York.

The meeting came as US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are due to hold a summit in Washington later this week.

AI has come under intense scrutiny in recent days after researchers warned of the potential risks posed by the technology and some of the industry's most high profile figures called for developers to take a more cautious approach.

"We think that, just like with any cross-border activity, that moving from opaque to more transparency between the number one and the number two AI powers in the world is very important," Bessent told reporters after the talks.

He said the meeting also covered other topics, including plans to "operationalise" a process to identify potential tariff cuts on goods called the Board of Trade.

A truce in the tariffs war between the world's two biggest economies is due to expire on 10 November.

The BBC has contacted the Chinese embassy in the US for comment.

Chinese state news agency Xinhua said the two sides had "candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges on key economic and trade issues", noting that they had discussed AI.

Bessent said in a post on X on Sunday that the talks "help lay the groundwork for President Trump to advance America's economic interests and deliver results for the American people."

The US and China are locked in a race to dominate the AI and technology industries.

In recent days Washington has faced calls to slow down the development of AI over fears abouts its potential negative impact on humanity.

Trump has largely dismissed those concerns, arguing that there are sufficient policies around AI and that the US cannot lose its edge to China.

He said earlier this month "whoever wins in AI, wins."

In May, when Xi hosted Trump in Beijing, ways to collaborate on AI was one of the issues the two leaders discussed.

Those talks ended with an agreement that China would buy Boeing jets and US agricultural goods in exchange for lower tariffs.

fullText:
An ICE officer shot and seriously wounded a Venezuelan man Sunday afternoon as he was delivering food in Austin, Texas, his lawyer said.

The man was taken to a local hospital and was “in serious but stable condition” after being shot in the torso, Austin-Travis County EMS Chief Robert Luckritz said at a news conference earlier.

The White House referred NBC News to the Department of Homeland Security for comment. A spokesperson for the DHS, the federal agency to which Immigration and Customs Enforcement belongs, said in a statement late Sunday that the man was stable and was in federal custody pending removal from the U.S.

Immigration attorney Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch identified him as Wilber Rafael Garcés Perez, 28, and said he was an asylum seeker who entered the country through a parole program.

“Today at 12:30, Wilber called his wife to tell her that he had been shot,” Lincoln-Goldfinch said in an interview. “And he was yelling in agony, and the call cut off. That was all she knew.”

The DHS spokesperson said Garcés Perez entered the country illegally under the Biden administration and had a final order of removal, adding that Homeland Security Investigations, with help from the FBI, will lead an investigation into the shooting.

The shooting occurred around 1 p.m. in North Austin.

Texas Department of Public Safety spokesperson Sheridan Nolen said the agency received a request for assistance from ICE for a vehicle pursuit involving a blue Toyota Corolla.

A social media video verified by NBC News captures the sound of tires screeching followed by a person exiting a dark-colored SUV as a blue sedan is stopped next to it, both vehicles facing one another.

At least three gunshots are heard as the person approaches the sedan and runs up to it as it slowly lurches forward. The video shows the person standing next to the sedan’s driver’s side as it stops in front of an intersection. The sedan also appears to be damaged on the passenger side.

The shooting occurred before DPS troopers arrived at the scene, Nolen said.

“Once they arrived, DPS Troopers immediately began assisting partner law enforcement agencies in performing medical treatment on the driver of the Toyota Corolla,” she said in a statement.

Lincoln-Goldfinch, who is representing Garcés Perez, said lawyers for the hospital where he was treated indicated he had been released, though she wasn’t sure at the time to whom.

Lincoln-Goldfinch said she was with his wife at the hospital earlier, hoping to get information on his condition, but they were escorted from the premises.

“We not only were lied to and told that he wasn’t there, but we were thrown off the hospital grounds by several officers who treated us as trespassers,” she said.

Austin Mayor Kirk Watson showed up several hours later and had a hospital administrator call Lincoln-Goldfinch and the man’s wife, the lawyer said. The administrator confirmed he had been released to ICE, she said.

The hospital, Dell Seton Medical Center at The University of Texas, did not respond to a request for comment.

“We are deeply concerned that his wife and family have not been permitted to see him and have not received a meaningful update regarding his current condition or whereabouts,” Lincoln-Goldfinch said in a statement earlier.

Garcés Perez, who Lincoln-Goldfinch said lives in Austin, is a DoorDash driver. In an email, a company spokesperson confirmed Garcés Perez was making a delivery at the time, adding that DoorDash is investigating and would not release more information “at this time.”

Lincoln-Goldfinch said her priority, and that of Garcés Perez’s family, is to find him and verify his condition.

“No one has told me or Wilber’s wife what the treatment was or how he’s doing,” she said, “and I feel very confident he is in a lot of pain right now as we speak.”

DHS has not provided any information about whether the ICE agent involved was wearing a body camera or if the man was the target of an operation or has any criminal background other than an immigration violation.

Lincoln-Goldfinch said his wife, who has legal status, indicated her husband has no criminal history.

The shooting comes as ICE surges enforcement across the country this summer, producing more than 50,000 arrests a month for the first time in its history in July and August.

Watson, Austin’s mayor, said the city’s police department was not involved in the incident.

Police Chief Lisa Davis said a “small foot pursuit” had occurred and that Austin police investigators were on the scene. Davis added that she was in contact with Homeland Security Investigations and other state law enforcement agencies.

“A person being shot on the streets of Austin by someone purporting to be law enforcement, particularly when it’s ICE, is something that causes me to be unhappy and angry,” Watson said at the news conference. “While I’m unhappy and I’m angry about it, I’m not surprised at all.”

U.S. Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, demanded an independent investigation, the release of any body camera footage and “accountability for any ICE officer who broke the law.”

“Over and over, ICE has shot people and then lied about what happened. We can see the lies with our own eyes. We will demand truth, transparency and accountability,” he said in a post on X.

In a letter addressed to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Acting ICE Director David Venturella, Casar insisted on receiving a Congressional briefing by Sept. 28.

James Talarico, who is running as the Democratic candidate for one of Texas’ U.S. Senate seats, said he is “closely following” reports of the shooting, and requested an investigation and all available footage.

U.S. Rep. Joaquin Castro, D-Texas, demanded “full accountability.”

“Trump has allowed ICE to flood our streets and put our communities in harms way again and again,” he said in a post on X.

In reaction to the shooting, the League of United Latin American Citizens — the largest Latino civil rights organization in the U.S. — called on Congress to establish an independent oversight of immigration enforcement.

Watson said he has asked for the city of Austin to be involved in any forthcoming investigations so that the police department can “be in a position to offer clear third-party eyes and expertise”

In a statement, the Travis County District Attorney’s Office requested to be “co-equal partners in the investigation” and to receive cooperation from the federal government.

Protesters who gathered at the site of the shooting on Sunday afternoon and evening, next to an elevated stretch of Highway 183, shouted anti-ICE slogans in English and Spanish. Some carried signs that said, “Stop ICE murder,” “Moms against ICE” and “Abolish ICE.”

One woman, who said she has lived in Austin for 33 years, told NBC News earlier Sunday that she has never witnessed an incident like this and it “broke my heart.”

The protest was punctuated with the sounds of drums, and someone could be heard saying, “They don’t want you to be here,” via loudspeaker.

Late Sunday night, the gathering roiled with tension, and Texas Department of Public Safety troopers responded by deploying tear gas and, in some instances, tackling protesters.

Protesters had dispersed and troopers appeared to have exited the area by 11 p.m. local time.

The shooting comes two months after an ICE officer fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Mexican national, in Houston during an attempted traffic stop to conduct an immigration arrest. DHS has said Salgado Araujo was in the country illegally and attempted to run over agents, but it has not provided evidence of its claims.

title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico sue Trump over White House press ban
description:

fullText:
Three news organizations whose journalists were banned from the White House last week are suing President Donald Trump and three top advisers, calling the abrupt lockout a "direct assault on the First Amendment."

POLITICO, CNN and MS NOW said in a joint statement Monday that they are bringing the federal lawsuit in a bid to immediately restore access for their reporters, who were denied entry to the White House complex on Saturday and had their credentials confiscated by the Secret Service.

"This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes," the news organizations said. "Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference."

The organizations are asking a judge on the U.S. District Court in Washington. to quickly rule Trump's ban unconstitutional and prevent his aides from enforcing it.

White House and Department of Justice spokespeople did not immediately return requests seeking comment.

The White House's exclusion of the journalists followed an announcement from Trump on Truth Social Friday that he was banning reporters for the three outlets "effective immediately."

Trump's post was vague about the reasons for the ban, beyond complaining about "constant 'reporting'" of what he called "FAKE NEWS!" as well as "FICTION and LIES." During an Oval Office photo op Friday, Trump offered few specifics.

"It's really just cumulative stories over the last few years. You get sick of it," Trump said. "They're smart people, but they purposely write negative news."

The news organizations, represented by Theodore Boutros, Jr. of law firm Gibson Dunn, are filing suit against Trump, chief of staff Susie Wiles, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung and Secret Service Director Sean Curran. The news outlets argue that the president's ban violates the Constitution in multiple ways: The abrupt cancellation of White House access without notice violated the organizations' Fifth Amendment due process and property rights, and the retaliation for the content of their reporting violated their First Amendment rights.

The suit contends that the ban is already "severely impeding" the news organizations' ability to report on the Trump White House while also causing a chilling effect among other news outlets, who could find themselves similarly locked out if the president deems their coverage "insufficiently favorable."

Though longstanding legal precedents permit the White House to restrict journalists' access to the building, courts have ruled that officials can't apply those restrictions in ways that discriminate based on viewpoint or content.

Previous efforts by Trump to deny access to specific reporters or news organizations have run into resistance in the courts, although the most recent litigation led to a muddled result.

In 2018, during Trump's first term, officials suspended the White House hard pass of then CNN White House correspondent Jim Acosta, with officials contending he kept speaking and clung to the microphone after Trump made clear he was moving on to another reporter. A judge ordered Acosta's credential restored, citing a murky process surrounding the suspension.

A similar fight played out the following year, following a verbal altercation in the Rose Garden between a freelance journalist for Playboy, Brian Karem, and Trump adviser Sebastian Gorka. A federal judge ordered the White House to return Karem's credential, concluding that the rules of decorum for such events were not clear enough to provide due process.

Last year, another legal clash erupted after Trump barred the Associated Press from attending East Room events and kicked the wire service out of the White House press pool, the small group of reporters routinely given access to the Oval Office, Air Force One and other sensitive locations frequented by the president. Trump's action came after the AP refused to adopt Gulf of America, after he signed an executive order renaming the body of water long known as the Gulf of Mexico.

Though a federal district judge sided with the AP, the bulk of his ruling was temporarily put on hold by a panel of the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals, which found the most restricted areas such as the Oval Office and Air Force One were not subject to the broader First Amendment protections of the rest of the complex.

"These restricted presidential spaces are not First Amendment fora opened for private speech and discussion," the panel's majority wrote. "The White House therefore retains discretion to determine, including on the basis of viewpoint, which journalists will be admitted."

Although the appeals court's June 2025 ruling was a preliminary one, it allowed Trump to follow through with his attempt to ban the AP from the Oval Office. The AP asked the D.C. Circuit's full bench to take up the issue, but a majority of the court's judges declined to do so.

Arguments aimed at a definitive ruling on the AP's lawsuit took place before a three-judge panel last November. The court has yet to rule.

The D.C. Circuit ruled almost a half-century ago in a case involving Nation magazine reporter Robert Sherrill that journalists can't be denied access to the White House arbitrarily or based on the content of their reporting.

title: Iran and U.S. exchange fresh warnings as Saudi-Houthi conflict escalates
description:
Flames and large plume of black smoke seen rising near Riyadh airport - Reuters
As world leaders prepare to gather in New York for the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) this week, a growing number of flashpoints across the Middle East are raising concerns about a wider regional escalation, from renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen to fresh warnings exchanged between Washington and Tehran.
Why are the Houthis and Saudi Arabia back at the center of regional tensions?
A dramatic Houthi offensive in Yemen has emerged as one of the most significant developments heading into UNGA.
The Iran-backed group has seized key territory in recent weeks, including a strategically important island in the Red Sea and coastal areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a crucial maritime chokepoint linking the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. US and Gulf officials have expressed growing concern that the Houthis are seeking to establish greater control over the waterway, which is vital to global trade and energy shipments.
fullText:
As world leaders prepare to gather in New York for the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) this week, a growing number of flashpoints across the Middle East are raising concerns about a wider regional escalation, from renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen to fresh warnings exchanged between Washington and Tehran.

A dramatic Houthi offensive in Yemen has emerged as one of the most significant developments heading into UNGA.

The Iran-backed group has seized key territory in recent weeks, including a strategically important island in the Red Sea and coastal areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a crucial maritime chokepoint linking the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. US and Gulf officials have expressed growing concern that the Houthis are seeking to establish greater control over the waterway, which is vital to global trade and energy shipments.

Despite receiving increased US intelligence and targeting support, Saudi Arabia has struggled to halt the Houthi advance. CNN reported Friday that Gulf and American officials are increasingly doubtful Riyadh can reverse the Houthi gains on its own.

The fighting has intensified sharply in recent days. Saudi Arabia accused the Houthis of targeting Mecca, Islam’s holiest city, while the Houthis claimed they shot down a Saudi F‑15 fighter jet over Yemen. On Saturday, the group also claimed missile and drone attacks on “sensitive” sites in Riyadh and an Aramco oil facility in Yanbu.

The latest exchanges underscore fears that Yemen is becoming an increasingly important front in the broader regional confrontation involving Iran.

Amid the worsening security environment, the US State Department and several US diplomatic missions have urged Americans in the region to exercise increased caution.

On Saturday, the State Department warned that the conflict “has the potential to escalate rapidly” and advised heightened vigilance.

Separately, the US Embassy in Saudi Arabia issued a security alert restricting travel by US government personnel to the cities of Taif and Yanbu without special authorization.

The warnings come as officials monitor the possibility of additional attacks involving Iran, Iranian-aligned groups and US partners in the region.

Iran’s central military command said Sunday it had received information suggesting the United States, with support from regional partners, could be preparing new military action against Iran.

In a statement carried by the semi-official Tasnim News Agency, Iran warned that any new US attack would trigger sustained strikes on US bases and interests across the region. Tehran also warned that countries assisting such operations would be considered parties to the conflict.

There have been no publicly reported US strikes on Iran for more than two weeks.

US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, further raised tensions with remarks indicating major decisions on Iran may be approaching.

Speaking to Fox News, Trump said he was in “deciding mode” and that “very big things” could happen soon. According to Fox correspondent Trey Yingst, Trump outlined three possible outcomes for Iran: a deal with Washington, increased economic pressure or military action.

At the same time, Trump said his administration remains in contact with the Houthis and is still avoiding direct US military involvement in the group’s conflict with Saudi Arabia.

Regional diplomacy is expected to be dominated by discussions on Iran, Yemen, maritime security and energy markets.

Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan is leading a delegation, while Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain are all sending senior representatives.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is also expected to attend the General Assembly after the Trump administration approved travel for a core Iranian delegation.

“Consistent with our host country obligations, the core delegation from the Iranian regime will be able to attend UN General Assembly High Level Week,” a State Department spokesperson said Thursday.

With fighting intensifying in Yemen, threats escalating between Washington and Tehran, and energy markets remaining sensitive to disruptions, many diplomats arriving in New York see this year’s General Assembly as taking place under one of the most volatile Middle East security environments in recent years.

CNN’s Tim Lister contributed to this story.

title: Powerful nor’easter takes shape with days of dangerous conditions for East Coast
description: THE...
fullText:
Parts of the East Coast will be battered by gusty winds and rain through the workweek as the first nor'easter of fall develops. The storm is expected to emerge off the coast toward the end of the week and could bring high surf, strong winds, coastal flooding and severe beach erosion through the weekend.

POWERFUL MONSOON TO REIGNITE OVER THE SOUTHWEST, FOUR CORNERS FOLLOWING DAY OF INTENSE FLOODING THAT KILLED 3

The system will begin developing Monday and continue through the weekend as a sharp fall cold front pushes off the coast, bringing rain to the Ohio Valley and parts of the Mid-Atlantic while strong high pressure builds to the north.

Strong northeasterly winds will develop across the offshore and coastal waters, producing powerful wind gusts.

Seas will rise rapidly, creating heavy surf and dangerous, battering waves along exposed beaches.

7 FACTS YOU SHOULD KNOW ABOUT FLASH FLOODS

According to the FOX Forecast Center, persistent onshore winds will remain locked in through multiple high-tide cycles, allowing waves to relentlessly pound the base of coastal dunes.

Significant beach erosion and dune scarping will develop from the Outer Banks through the Mid-Atlantic and Long Island as the surface low-pressure system forms.

The FOX Forecast Center said moderate coastal flooding is expected during high tides, particularly in vulnerable back bays and low-lying coastal roadways.

The Outer Banks are forecast to see major coastal flooding, extreme surf and heavy, continuous rain. Some areas could experience wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph, with offshore waves reaching 15 to 18 feet.

The region will also see widespread rainfall, although widespread flash flooding is not currently forecast.

However, pounding waves across multiple high-tide cycles could lead to coastal flooding and severe beach erosion.

Ocean overwash onto coastal roadways, including Highway 12, is expected, potentially creating scenes similar to major coastal events seen last year.

WHAT IS COASTAL EROSION AND WHY IS IT DANGEROUS?

Water will become trapped in back bays, creating consecutive high-tide cycles and preventing water from fully draining during low tide.

Eventually, elevated tidal flooding could spread across North Carolina, Virginia, Maryland, Delaware and New Jersey, extending into southern New England.

WHAT IS A HEAT DOME AND HOW CAN IT AFFECT YOU?

The FOX Forecast Center said multiple days of continuous pounding waves will severely impact beaches. Dune washouts and damage to oceanfront boardwalks and coastal infrastructure will become increasingly likely across Mid-Atlantic and Long Island beaches.

Compounding tidal flooding and heavy wave action will also begin to impact the southern half of North Carolina.

Wind gusts along immediate coastal areas could reach 40 to 50 mph, pushing ocean water inland.

As the strengthening system tracks into or near New England, the strongest pressure gradient will impact the region, including Boston.

However, the FOX Forecast Center said there are a few scenarios that could unfold as the storm moves north.

One scenario is if the storm shifts closer to Boston. This could turn the storm into a major weather event, featuring 60 to 70 mph wind gusts, heavy rainfall, major storm surge and significant disruptions to Boston Harbor and the Massachusetts coastline.

HOW HIGH PRESSURE AND LOW PRESSURE DRIVE THE WEATHER

On the other hand, if the storm shifts closer to New Jersey or Long Island, the strongest impacts could shift farther south, potentially putting New York City on the fringe of the storm.

Finally, if the area of low pressure remains offshore, coastal New England could still experience rough surf, elevated tides and breezy conditions, while the heaviest rain and strongest winds remain displaced to the south and east over open water. The FOX Forecast Center said this scenario is appearing less likely.

What is certain, according to the FOX Forecast Center, is that wind gusts could reach over 60 mph as the peak of the storm shifts into southern New England, Massachusetts Bay and the Gulf of Maine.

Some areas could see waves reaching 15 to 18 feet along the coast.

Peak onshore winds, high astronomical tides and trapped coastal water will create the greatest risk for significant coastal inundation and structural flooding along east-facing shores, including Boston Harbor, Cape Cod and the north and south shores.

POWERFUL WAVES BATTER SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA COAST, DAMAGING HOMES AND TRIGGERING SINKHOLE

Officials said dangerous seas, extreme rip currents and massive swells will make ocean waters extremely dangerous.

title: ReBarUEFI: Resizable BAR for almost any UEFI system
description: Resizable BAR for (almost) any UEFI system. Contribute to xCuri0/ReBarUEFI development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
A UEFI DXE driver to enable Resizable BAR on systems which don't support it officially. This provides performance benefits and is even required for Intel Arc GPUs to function optimally.

Follow the wiki guide Adding FFS module and continue through the steps. It covers adding the module and the additional modifications needed if required.

Once running the modified firmware make sure that 4G decoding is enabled and CSM is off.

Next run ReBarState which can be found in Releases (if you're on Linux build with CMake) and set the Resizable BAR size. In most cases you should be able to use 32 (unlimited) without issues but you might need to use a smaller BAR size if 32 doesn't work

If Resizable BAR works for you reply to List of working motherboards so I can add it to the list. Most firmware will accept unsigned/patched modules with Secure Boot on so you won't have any problems running certain games.

If you have any issues after enabling Resizable BAR see Common Issues (and fixes)

The module is added to the UEFI firmware's DXE volume so it gets executed on every boot. The ReBarDxe module replaces the function PreprocessController of PciHostBridgeResourceAllocationProtocol with a function that checks for Resizable BAR capability and then sets it to the size from the ReBarState NVRAM variable after running the original function.

The new PreprocessController function later gets called during PCI enumeration by the PciBus module which will detect the new BAR size and allocate it accordingly.

Instructions for applying UEFIPatch not included as it isn't required for these X99 motherboards. You can follow them below.

Most UEFI firmwares have problems handling 64-bit BARs so several patches were created to fix these issues. You can use UEFIPatch to apply these patches located in the UEFIPatch folder. See wiki page Using UEFIPatch 

Use the provided buildffs.py script after cloning inside an edk2 tree to build the DXE driver. ReBarState can be built on Windows or Linux using CMake. See wiki page Building 

Previously it was thought that it won't work on PCIe Gen2 systems but one user had it work with an i5 2500k.

You can use Linux with 4G Decoding on, recent versions will automatically resize and allocate GPU BARs. If your BIOS doesn't have the 4G decoding option (make sure to check hidden) or DSDT is faulty you can then follow the Arch wiki guide for DSDT modification using modifications from DSDT Patching and boot with pci=realloc in your kernel command line. Currently there is no known method to get it on Windows without BIOS modification

Clear CMOS and Resizable BAR should be disabled. In some cases it may be necessary to remove the CMOS battery for Resizable BAR to disable.

On my system with an i5 3470 and Sapphire Nitro+ RX 580 8GB with Resizable BAR enabled in driver I get an upto 12% FPS increase with 2GB BAR size.

@dsanke, @cursemex, @dripsnek, @val3nt33n, @Mak3rde and @romulus2k4 for testing/helping develop patches

The Linux kernel especially the amdgpu driver

EDK2 for the base that all OEM UEFI follows

Ghidra which was used to patch UEFI modules to workaround artificial limitations

@vit9696 for the NVRAM whitelist patches

@ZOXZX for helping with the X79 Above 4G patches

@NikolajSchlej for developing UEFITool/UEFIPatch

QEMU/OVMF made testing hooking way easier although it didn't have any resizable BAR devices so the only way I could test it was on my actual PC.

title: The Pain Axis: LLMs Represent Self-Directed Harm and Act to Relieve It
description: Large language models sometimes behave in ways resembling human emotional responses, and recent work has identified internal representations that may explain this. We ask whether LLMs represent pain distinctly from fear, sadness, and generic negative valence, and whether this representation functions as pain would be expected to. We build a dataset describing painful situations across five categories: physical, psychological, social, moral, and cognitive. These are paired with controls for fear, negative emotion, negative world states, sadness, non-painful bodily sensation, arousal, numbness, and neutral content. Using denoised difference-in-means, we extract a linear pain direction from 25 open-weight models across five families, ranging from 2B to 72B parameters.

title: A study of sequence weighting at scale
description: TL;DR: We study the scaling laws of data weighting across in-house and open-weight LMs, finding non-monotonic behavior across scales. We vary the weight assi...
fullText:
TL;DR: We study the scaling laws of data weighting across in-house and open-weight LMs, finding non-monotonic behavior across scales.
We vary the weight assigned to sequences during training and measure how strongly the model’s loss reduction on a sequence depends on the sequence’s weight.
Taken together, our results are consistent with a general trend: as models transition from small to medium scale, they transition from learning general patterns independent of data weight to learning data-specific patterns proportional to the data weights.
As models then transition from medium to large scale they are able to learn all patterns present in the data, once again independent of data weight.

When training neural networks, we spend a lot of time thinking about precisely what we want our models to learn.
How much do we care about our models being generally intelligent across all coding tasks versus being good at OCaml specifically?
How useful is data from an older market regime compared to data collected recently?
Generally, how much do we want to upweight high-quality data versus allowing our models to learn from everything?
These questions are ultimately data mixing questions, questions about how and where to spend our models’ representational capacity and our FLOPs.

Further complicating these questions is that in practice, many of the experiments we would like to run are prohibitively expensive.
It’s intractable to run a dense multi-dimensional grid search over hyperparameters even at medium scales, let alone at the largest scales (where we may only be able to train one model for a given task).
The standard approach to this is to fit hyperparameters like data mix weights via a scaling law approach, in which we fit hyperparameters at small scales and then extrapolate those hyperparameters to larger scales (the canonical example of this being Chinchilla scaling).

A core challenge for scaling laws is that for the extrapolation to hold, large-scale models must have behaviors that are either (a) invariant with scale (e.g., MuP-style results in which many hyperparameter optima remain stable across scales) or (b) predictable via extrapolating changes in behavior at small scale (e.g., Kaplan-style results in which loss decreases predictably with scale).
Unfortunately, not all behaviors have these characteristics: some behaviors are emergent at scale and are not predictable via scaling laws.
For the rest of this post, we’ll call such non-predictable scaling behaviors aberrant.

Our internal experiments have shown that data mixing is a setting particularly prone to aberrant scaling behaviors.
This parallels findings in the MAI-Thinking-1 technical report (section 2.5.2), where the relative ordering in quality of training with a code-heavy and a STEM-heavy mix reversed as model size increased.
We therefore set out to precisely characterize the extent to which language models actually learn patterns in the data proportional to the weight accorded to that data in a data mix, and how that behavior changes across scales.

Data mix experiments can conflate the effect of the data’s weight in a corpus with other important but different considerations.
Most notably, results from data mix experiments are heavily affected by variation in data quality across different sources and by differences in the uniqueness of marginal tokens in any given data source.
To isolate the effects of mix weight alone, in this post we specifically analyze data weighting, a variant of data mixing in which each individual sequence in our training dataset receives a different weight in our loss.
We measure the extent to which a model has learned a training sequence with a given weight by first assigning random sequence weights to each sequence in the dataset, training a model on the dataset, then re-evaluating it on the same training dataset.

We then define a metric, the effective sequence weight exponent (denoted by ) that measures what power of a sequence’s weight is closest to proportional to the model’s expected loss decrease on that sequence (e.g., says that the model’s expected loss decrease on sequences is directly proportional to their weight, while says that the model’s expected loss decrease on sequences is the same for all possible sequence weights).

Previous work makes mixed predictions for how scales: (Byrd & Lipton 2019) and the general phenomenon of large-scale interpolation predict that larger models should asymptote towards , while Li et al. 2026 find that at fixed tokens-per-parameter, optimal token repetition count for valuable domains mildly increases with model size.
We ask: is the effective sequence weight exponent a smooth power law with scale, or is it aberrant?

We evaluate the effects of sequence weighting on an internal text-based benchmark.
To test across model families and scales, we evaluate two families of in-house-pretrained LLMs ranging from tens of millions to hundreds of billions of parameters and one open-weight model family (Qwen 2.5) ranging from 500M to 72B parameters.

We find a number of aberrant scaling behaviors (reasoning about data mixing across scales is complicated!) and some striking trends.
Taken together, our results are consistent with a non-monotonic rise-then-fall in the effective sequence weight exponent: small-scale models fit small effective sequence weight exponents, learning patterns across the entire dataset independent of data weight; medium-scale models fit larger effective sequence weight exponents, learning patterns in data proportional to their data weight.
Large-scale models once again fit small effective sequence weight exponents, learning all patterns present in the data regardless of weight.
Epoching shifts the effective sequence weight peak towards smaller models.

Aberrant scaling laws are inconvenient for our model training methodologies, but identifying them lets us avoid bad extrapolations.
In our science we are vigilant for such aberrant behaviors, and when we discover one, we redesign our scaling experiments and evaluations such that they become predictable.1
Our experiments suggest a number of possible remedies, from evaluating and extrapolating data-mix results only from sufficiently large models, to adjusting training weights to compensate for the observed .2
And we keep on measuring how far off our models are from our predictions to keep on catching the next place that our scaling laws break down, and to allow us to train larger, better models with even more confidence.

Dataset.
We evaluate the effects of sequence weighting on an internal text benchmark.
We weight sequences in this dataset using sequence weights drawn log-uniform between 0.01 and 10.
We train for 3 epochs and evaluate after each epoch.

Models. We evaluate three different model families on this dataset:

The JS-dense and JS-sparse models range from tens of millions to hundreds of billions of parameters.
Note that in all contexts, held-out performance is increasing with scale for these models.

Measuring the effect of sequence weighting.
We first train our model on the training dataset (with each sequence weighted corresponding to ), re-evaluate the model on its training dataset, and for each sequence measure the loss reduction on that sequence achieved from training.
We then fit a such that (appropriately normalized) the loss reduction on a given sequence with weight is best explained by .

We make this fit more precise in an attached note, but to better understand what different values mean, let’s consider a few scenarios:

Hyperparameters.
We tune hyperparameters to minimize loss against a validation set.3
Because the largest in-house models are too large to economically tune hyperparameters on, we set hyperparameters via a Chinchilla-style power law scaling law, fitting optimal hyperparameters as a function of scale.

Here are the interactive 3D surfaces for each model family:

Within a given model family and number of epochs, often increases at small scales (particularly through tens of billions of parameters) and decreases at larger scales as we near the hundreds of billions of parameters regime (for reference, the largest pictured JS-dense rung has fewer than 100B parameters).

Training for more epochs shifts the peak towards smaller model scales.
Between model families, we find little relationship between the actual values of – the smallest model in JS-sparse is substantially larger than the smallest model in JS-dense, yet has a smaller ; the largest model in JS-sparse is also substantially larger than the largest model in Qwen 2.5, yet has a larger .

Why does sometimes rise then fall?
We hypothesize that this is because models learn different patterns present in the data at different rates.
Some patterns generalize well across all sequences (for example, understanding English), while others are idiosyncratic to smaller groups of sequences.
In this dataset, there is more loss reduction possible due to idiosyncratic patterns than there is to general patterns.
We therefore hypothesize that smaller models use their limited capacity to learn general patterns and cannot represent idiosyncratic patterns, medium-sized models learn both the general and the most important idiosyncratic patterns (by sequence weight), and large models have the capacity to learn all idiosyncratic patterns with all weights.
Epoching allows the model to learn more of both the general and idiosyncratic patterns.

More broadly, we find that the behavior of sequence weighting at small scales does not cleanly predict behavior at the largest scales.
This nicely encapsulates an all-too-common result; larger models can have behaviors that differ in kind from those exhibited by smaller models.
Accordingly, our scaling research requires spending as much if not more time and care trying to understand why we’re off our predicted curves as it does fitting the curves themselves.

If this kind of thing is interesting to you, consider applying.
You’ll join a close-knit group of brilliant, supportive colleagues, harnessing tens of thousands of GPUs, petabytes of training data, and the agility and resources to invest in the best ideas.

A classic example of such a fix to an aberrant scaling law is in multiple-choice question answering: while small-scale models often hover around the noise floor with sampled responses until a discrete jump when the model learns to follow instructions, measuring continuous metrics like bits-per-byte on answers often reveals smooth, non-aberrant scaling. ↩

In particular, if effective sequence weights scale as , then achieving target loss reduction weights might require training with damped weights e.g. . We have not tested this hypothesis. ↩

We apply heavy regularization in all cases such that the resulting model approximately maximizes performance on a held-out set; while we could likely tune all but the very smallest of these architectures to memorize the entire input data in the first pass, this isn’t representative of the scenario that we care about. ↩

Alex has been a researcher at Jane Street since 2024, working on LLM
training. Previously he did a PhD in computer science at MIT.

Nitya is a machine learning researcher at Jane Street, where she has been
since 2019. She previously studied math at Stanford and MIT, and outside
of work, she particularly enjoys making meals with surprising ingredients.

title: Jevcache
description: Memoize Jev-class decisions. The same decision never runs twice: repeats are free, deterministic, and shareable.
fullText:
Fast and cheap per call isn't free at volume — or reproducible. Three things a faster model can't give you:

60–80% of an agent's decisions repeat — loops, retries, idempotent tools, heavy-tailed inputs. Every repeat is another bill. A cache hit costs $0.

Pin the exact decision — replay it in CI, offline, with no network and no model-version drift. The reproducibility real systems demand.

A cache can. Publish one and anyone recalls against it — one team's decisions become everyone's, over a file or the hosted index.

Latency? A local hit returns in ~0ms, in-process, no round-trip at all. That's the bonus. The point is you stop re-deciding what you've already decided.

Pick your volume. This is what memoization keeps off the bill.

One command bundles what you've already decided — fingerprints and answers only, never raw state. Host the file anywhere, or push to the hosted index.

Reads are open and keyless. Writes mint a free key so decisions are attributable and no one can overwrite another publisher's cache. Per-recall pricing is coming — free for now.

The same binary runs as a local cache your app talks to over HTTP. No library to install, no per-call process to spawn, and it works from any language — you just POST a schema and some state.

Prefer the command line? jevcache decide --schema … --state ticket.json --json does the same thing, and recall exits 3 on a miss for CI.

jevcache is one binary. Where you point your app at it depends on how your app is deployed.

Your own server, a container, a worker? Run jevcache serve next to it and call http://localhost:9000. Nothing leaves the box.

Vercel functions, Cloudflare, Lambda — there's no daemon to run in an ephemeral function. Host jevcache once (docker run, Fly, Railway) with a token, and your functions call it over HTTPS. Your state and model key stay on your instance.

No server at all — jevcache decide / recall read and write the local ledger. recall exits 3 on a miss, so CI can branch on it.

One static binary on your PATH — no Node, no Python, nothing to keep updated. macOS & Linux (arm64/x64); on Windows, grab jevcache-windows-x64.exe.

title: ZCode: Z.ai's coding agent harness. Powerful, intelligent, extensible
description: Z.ai's coding agent harness. Powerful, intelligent, extensible. - zai-org/ZCode
fullText:
ZCode 是 AI 编程工作台，提供桌面应用、浏览器界面和终端 Agent。本仓库包含客户端、后端服务、共享 UI，以及 Agent CLI 与运行时源码。

准备 Git、Node.js 24.14.0 和 pnpm 10.33.2，版本以 mise.toml 为准。以下开发和打包命令均在仓库根目录执行。

pnpm bootstrap 安装 workspace 依赖、准备桌面本地运行资源，再执行 build:bootstrap。

Agent CLI 与运行时源码位于 apps/zcode-cli/，作为普通目录随本仓库一起克隆，无需单独拉取或初始化 Git submodule。

默认 bootstrap 跳过远程资源准备，适合本地桌面开发。使用远程工作区或验证远程发行资源时，再运行对应准备命令。

pnpm dev:desktop 默认等同于 pnpm dev:desktop:prod，使用生产服务配置。启动脚本会准备本地运行资源、构建桌面 Agent，再启动 Electron 和源码监听。

需要独立开发数据目录时，可设置 ZCODE_DATA_BASE_DIR。例如在 macOS / Linux 中：

先执行 pnpm bootstrap:with-remote 准备远程资源（mock-cdn），再 pnpm dev:desktop；连接远程项目时资源选择「本地下载后上传」。开发态资源取自本地 packages/desktop/mock-cdn 和本地构建产物，经 SFTP 上传到远程，不访问 CDN。

该命令同时启动 Web 开发服务器（默认 http://localhost:5173）和后端（默认 http://localhost:3030）；浏览器访问前者。/ws 和一般 /api 请求代理到本地后端，/api/v1/oauth/token 单独代理到当前配置的产品服务。

Agent 源码修改后，执行 pnpm --filter @zcode/cli... build 并重启服务。需要验证完整发行包时，按下方“ZCode 命令行版”打包章节解压运行。

命令行发行包包含 TUI、Web 和 Agent，统一使用 zcode 启动：无参数进入 TUI；第一个参数为 --web 时启动 Web；其他参数交给现有 Agent CLI 处理。两种模式都在本机运行，无需 Electron。

Web 模式默认工作目录为当前目录，监听 127.0.0.1，默认不启用访问令牌，自动选择空闲端口并打开浏览器。访问终端输出的地址，按 Ctrl+C 停止服务。局域网访问可使用 --host 0.0.0.0；监听非本机地址时默认生成访问令牌，使用终端输出的带令牌链接。可通过 --token 指定令牌或 --no-token 关闭令牌认证。

直接启动通用 Web 服务的 HTTP 入口时，通过 ZCODE_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN 配置 API／WebSocket 认证；通过程序接口创建服务时，使用 authToken 选项。

构建方式见下方打包章节。pnpm build:zcode 只生成发行包，不会替换 PATH 中已有的 zcode。如果命令仍指向旧安装或其他源码目录，macOS / Linux 可用 command -v zcode 检查，Windows 可用 where.exe zcode 检查。

这个入口直接运行 Agent CLI，不经过发行包的 --web 分流。开发 Web 用 pnpm dev:web；验证统一的 zcode 命令，用下方解压后的 bin/zcode.mjs。

根目录 .env.example 提供服务地址与构建配置示例，可按需复制到 .env，本地覆盖放入 .env.local。Desktop 的开发环境通过 dev:desktop:test / dev:desktop:prod 选择。

运行时变量可在启动命令的环境中显式设置。随客户端发布的默认配置见 config/README.md。

第三方声明生成、发行校验流程及声明在发行物中的位置见 third-party/README.md。

默认目标为 macOS arm64，默认输出目录为 packages/desktop/dist/。--os 支持 mac、win、linux，--arch 支持 x64、arm64；实际打包与签名需要目标平台对应的工具和配置。

安装：双击打开产物 DMG，将 ZCode 拖入"应用程序"。本地构建未签名，首次打开若被 macOS 拦截，执行：

构建入口为 pnpm build:zcode。脚本会依次构建 CLI/TUI、后端和 Web，收集 TUI 的原生库、worker 与运行时依赖，再组装发行包；运行发行包仍需要 Node.js，版本以 mise.toml 为准。

打包前必须设置下载根地址 ZCODE_DIST_BASE_URL（可放在 .env、.env.local 或环境变量中），也可以通过 --base-url 传入。以下地址是占位示例，发布时替换为实际托管地址：

默认版本取根目录 package.json，输出目录为 dist/zcode/：

完整目录可上传到配置的下载根地址。安装脚本从该地址下载运行包，默认安装到 ~/.zcode/runtime，并在 ~/.local/bin 创建 zcode 命令。安装目录可通过 ZCODE_DIST_HOME 修改，命令目录可通过 ZCODE_DIST_BIN_DIR 修改。

旧 Lite 用户需要改用上述构建命令、环境变量和新的安装脚本。新安装不会删除旧 Lite 目录，也不会迁移或删除已有会话数据。

浏览器打开 http://127.0.0.1:3030，即可验证同一后端服务托管 Web 页面和 Agent 的完整链路。该端口需要空闲；如正在运行 pnpm dev:web，可改用其他 --port。

功能与优惠范围、维护规则、执行与数据风险，以及许可和第三方版权说明，详见 NOTICE.md。

title: Jev – System-1 Agent Architecture Radar (open-source)
description: Awesome Jev: source-backed open-source ecosystem radar, plain-language project discovery, and automatic GitHub sync - logicrw/awesome-jev-projects
fullText:
简体中文  •  English  •  日本語  •  한국어

🌐 Search and filter ↗  ｜  🤖 Install the Agent Skill  ｜  📂 Categories  ｜  🚀 Submit a project (Issue only)

[!TIP]
Project Submissions: We welcome your Jev projects! All project submissions and updates are handled exclusively via GitHub Issues. This repository does not accept Pull Requests. Simply fill out the issue template with your repository URL.

When building autonomous agents, routing every small branching decision to a heavy reasoning model (System 2) incurs seconds of latency, runaway token costs, and context drift.

TypeSafe Jev (System 1) is purpose-built for fast, typed discrete decisions:

Search and filter ↗ · 358 curated projects

A community-maintained directory and radar for Jev, highlighting open-source projects with verified code and clear decision architectures.

Entries are linked to commit-pinned source code and specific decision points for easy reference. Compatible implementations clearly identify their underlying model.

Projects follow their respective open-source licenses; unstated licenses are noted individually.

Founding partner slots are open. There are no paid sponsors yet.

Sponsorship does not change inclusion review, project descriptions, or organic ranking.

Install the skill to query projects by domain and inspect pinned source evidence directly from your terminal or agent.

title: Applesauce: Transparent Compression for Apple File System Compression (AFSC)
description: Transparent compression for Apple File System Compression (AFSC) - Dr-Emann/applesauce
fullText:
Applesauce is a command-line interface (CLI) program written in Rust that
compresses, decompresses, and prints information about compressed files for
HFS+/APFS transparent compression on macOS. It is based on
afsctool and offers several key
improvements, including better performance, improved multithreading (even for a
single file), and reduced memory usage. Applesauce supports all three compression
algorithms used by HFS+/APFS: LZFSE, LZVN, and ZLIB.

Applesauce has the following key features:

Applesauce supports three compression algorithms:

Applesauce defaults to using LZFSE compression.
Depending on the type of data being compressed and the desired balance between
compression ratio and speed, one of these algorithms may be more suitable than
the others.

Applesauce is based on afsctool, but offers several key improvements, including:

afcstool can compress multiple files in parallel, but applesauce parallelizes at
the block level, so even a single file can be compressed in parallel. Applesauce
can often be several times faster than afsctool, especially for small numbers of
large files.

afcstool will load the entire file into memory before compressing it
(although it does attempt to use mmap for large files). Applesauce will only
keep the block(s) currently being compressed in memory.

Applesauce outputs a pretty progress bar while it's working, providing a more
user-friendly experience than afsctool's sparse output.

afsctool will compress a file which fits in the xattr after compression, even
if doing so actually adds more overhead than leaving the file uncompressed.
Applesauce will not compress a file if it would result in a larger file.

afcstool overwrites files in place. Although it attempts to restore the file
if an error occurs, if it is forcefully terminated while compressing a file,
the file may be left in an invalid state.

Applesauce compresses/decompresses files to a temporary file and then atomically
renames the temporary file to the original file only when the operation is
complete: the file is never left in an invalid state, even if the program is
harshly terminated.
