title: Commanders' fans, others react to Jayden Daniels' injury vs. Cowboys
description: Here's how social media reacted to Jayden Daniels' injury vs. Cowboys.
fullText:
For nearly 30 minutes on Sunday, it looked like we were in for a heckuva game between the Washington Commanders and the Dallas Cowboys. However, just before halftime, the Commanders chose to go for a touchdown instead of a field goal with three seconds remaining. They never had a chance, as left guard Chris Paul appeared to step on quarterback Jayden Daniels' foot, causing him to break his fall with his left elbow. Unfortunately, it was the same elbow that Daniels dislocated last November.

Instead of tying the game at 17 or going down 17-13 at halftime, the Commanders faced a 17-10 deficit and the loss of their quarterback, all as a result of one play. Daniels did not return, and it's believed he suffered another dislocation of his left (non-throwing) elbow.

It was frustrating for Washington and Washington fans. Daniels was looking more like himself in the first half against the Cowboys, completing 11 of his first 14 passes and rushing for 69 yards before the injury. The Commanders appeared to have tied the game in the third quarter, when Marcus Mariota found Dyami Brown for a touchdown. Somehow, the officials did not call it a touchdown, even after the replay, shocking the game announcers, NFL rules expert Dean Blandino and all of social media.

Daniels' injury, combined with that egregious officiating error, sent the Commanders into a tailspin. Dallas cruised to a 37-20 victory, leaving the Commanders with more questions than answers moving forward.

With Daniels out for the foreseeable future, Mariota will be back under center for Washington. It was a wild game of injuries, officiating errors and bad Commanders' defense. However, online talk centered on Daniels' latest injury.

Here's how social media reacted.

Lots of doctors on this app say that the lack of surgery last time could be a factor in it happening again. 

If surgery is the way to make it more stable than it has to be done. You can't have him dislocating it every time he plants his left hand on the turf to brace himself. https://t.co/exAunVCnbj

Jayden Daniels 

How ‘bad’ is this elbow injury? ⚠️🚨 pic.twitter.com/jTY9NHCj7R

I honestly just can’t believe it. It’s week 2 and we’re already waiting for next season to start. We’re really asking if Jayden should be our QB next season and it’s a fair question. I am in such disbelief. pic.twitter.com/DyZpLMImo0

This is so brutal for Jayden. Kid has worked so hard 🙏🏻.

#Commanders Jayden Daniels - Likely elbow dislocation. Same elbow as ‘25

Didn’t have surgery in ‘25. Possible to treat w/o surgery again + return in season

But would expect high recurrence risk if so

Suspect he’d opt for surgical treatment, which would likely mean season over pic.twitter.com/iESTlApkKY

Family, 

The Guard stepped in his foot. WTF does the coach have to do with that? The offense had ALL the momentum. Right decision.

Two worst takes you can have after the Daniels injury.

1. Blaming the coaching staff 
2. Giving up on Jayden or calling him injury prone 

It was a freak accident and just bad luck, it’s football it happens. It sucks and I’m devastated but the game goes on. Jayden will be back…

Is FOX getting paid by the replay of Daniels' elbow popping out of socket? Good lord, man.

Uncle.

A lot of people said Jayden Daniels shouldn’t get surgery last season since it’s his non-throwing side.
However, this was always a concern for secondary occurrence.
I imagine they’ll recommend surgery now to tighten ligaments & ensure NO future recurrence.

Frustrating. https://t.co/YtYSVyMODx

Ruled OUT now
Scary looking injury
Re-injury is never good
But season not over
Can return more quickly than people think with a brace https://t.co/hxaVDyM3TY

https://t.co/rNe4971rOr pic.twitter.com/AchjFuvzgC

I have no idea why the Commanders didn't kick a field goal. 

Jayden Daniels appears to have injured his elbow badly again.

Three seconds left in the half, on the road, get the points and move to the second half. 

You can’t predict what happened but what a damn fluke of a play to see Daniels get hurt on. For an organization that’s seen nasty, gruesome injuries at QB to Joe Theismann, Alex Smith,…

I don’t even know what to say at this point! I’m lost for words!

This article originally appeared on Commanders Wire: Commanders' fans, others react to Jayden Daniels' injury vs. Cowboys

title: Brittany and Patrick Mahomes Share a Kiss in Sweet Moment Before Chiefs Game
description: The Chiefs hosted the Indianapolis Colts in primetime on Sunday, Sept. 20
fullText:
Patrick and Brittany Mahomes shared a pregame kiss before the Chiefs faced the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, Sept. 20

Brittany was rocking the Chiefs' signature red color as she supported her husband at Arrowhead Stadium

The Chiefs won their first game of the season on Monday, Sept. 14, defeating the Denver Broncos 31-10

Patrick Mahomes shared a sweet kiss with his wife, Brittany, before the Chiefs hosted the Indianapolis Colts in Week 2.

Just before kickoff on Sunday, Sept. 20, Brittany made her way to the sidelines to show support for her quarterback husband — who returned to the field on Monday, Sept. 14 after tearing both the ACL and LCL in his left knee last season — and wish him good luck with a kiss.

Mahomes was dressed in his Chiefs uniform and headband as he met his wife on the sidelines. Brittany, 31, made it clear she was ready to cheer on the Chiefs by wearing the team's signature red color to Arrowhead Stadium.

Mahomes, who celebrated his 31st birthday on Sept. 17, scored the first touchdown in the Chiefs' home opener against the Denver Broncos last Monday. The quarterback ran the ball into the end zone in his first game back from injury and celebrated his team's win — and his return to the field — afterwards on social media.

"Want to give all glory and thanks to God! Letting me be out there doing what i love again," Mahomes wrote in a post on X. The quarterback added, "Chiefs Kingdom this is just the start see y'all next week! 🙏🏽⏰."

Brittany, 31, also celebrated her husband's return to the field, writing, "HESSSSSS BACKKKKKKKK," over a video of Mahomes' touchdown that she filmed from her suite at Arrowhead Stadium.

The quarterback spoke about his grueling injury during a sit-down interview with ESPN's Chris Berman that aired just before kickoff on Monday. "I was banged up at the end of last year, but we're good to go now," Mahomes said.

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — 

Mahomes and Brittany started dating in high school. They got engaged in September 2020 and officially tied the knot on March 12, 2022.

The couple welcomed their daughter, Sterling Skye, in February 2021, followed by their son, Patrick "Bronze" Lavon Mahomes III, in November 2022. In January 2025, Patrick and Brittany welcomed their third child, a daughter named Golden Raye, continuing the tradition of naming their kids after different types of precious metals.

title: How Rob Pelinka Hurt Lakers Chances With Jonathan Kuminga
description: The Los Angeles Lakers missing out on Jonathan Kuminga in free agency hurt their best chance to end up with a better power forward. An active NBA offseason saw the Lakers making many moves to both add talent and lose stars. Kuminga was reportedly choosing between the Lakers and Minnesota Timberwolves in the final weeks […] The post How Rob Pelinka Hurt Lakers Chances With Jonathan Kuminga appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Lakers missing out on Jonathan Kuminga in free agency hurt their best chance to end up with a better power forward. An active NBA offseason saw the Lakers making many moves to both add talent and lose stars. Kuminga was reportedly choosing between the Lakers and Minnesota Timberwolves in the final weeks of his decision. Minnesota ultimately won out to make Kuminga their new starting power forward.

Michael Rand of the Minnesota Tribute revealed what exactly the Timberwolves did to win over Kuminga:

"Timberwolves GM Matt Lloyd talked to Kuminga's agent, Aaron Turner, so often this summer that his wife asked him to add up just how frequently they talked. The answer: 94 phone calls between the two. Anthony Edwards also actively recruited Kuminga to join the Wolves."

The biggest reason for Kuminga trusting Minnesota was the General Manager showing strong interest for quite some time. Lloyd calling Turner 94 times kept the constant communication and showed a desire to bring him in. The star power of Edwards recruiting Kuminga added a lot too to make him pick them over a team with Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves in the biggest basketball market.

Lakers General Manager Rob Pelinka is already under fire for some of his questionable moves this summer. Losing LeBron James will hurt any team, but they didn't do a sufficient job replacing his production with the new talents joining the roster.

Walker Kessler is already being questioned since the draft picks traded to acquire him and money paid to him makes him the third star on the team. A team like the Lakers clearly needs to have stronger depth, but they missed out on their best opportunity to improve the forward core.

Pelinka apparently didn't reach out nearly as much as Lloyd did to tempt Kuminga into joining them. The Lakers didn't treat Kuminga as a major priority to see him choosing the team that wanted him more. Flawed role players Jake LaRavia and Jarred Vanderbilt are expected to compete for the starting power forward role with much lower upsides than Kuminga offered.

The offseason of bold moves saw Pelinka putting together a roster that will either make him a hero or cost him his job. Banking on Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton to be top five offensive options of a contending team is quite risky for any General Manager.

Pelinka believes that the questionable moves he made were done to benefit Luka and his playing style. Some of the players joining the Lakers have similar playing styles to the Dallas Mavericks team that Doncic helped lead to the NBA Finals.

Time will tell if Pelinka's decisions were smarter than the average fan or general media consensus believes. Luka only has a few years left on his deal and could opt to leave if the Lakers struggle in the loaded West. Pelinka will get blamed and fired long before head coach JJ Redick since he put together this roster.

title: Open Radar Code Architecture
description: Open-source ice-penetrating radar for the cryosphere Learn More Read the Paper Download Open Radar Code Architecture (ORCA) is an open platform for building radar instruments to better understand Earth's coolest places
fullText:
Open Radar Code Architecture (ORCA) is an open platform for building radar instruments to better understand Earth's coolest places

ORCA is a platform for building low-cost, flexible,
and field-proven radar instruments for the cryosphere. ORCA is
the base project for Peregrine, a field-portable ice-penetrating radar UAV,
MAPPERR, a multi-frequency radar/radiometer, and EYAS, a bistatic ice-penetrating radar receiver.

This website provides documentation for the ORCA codebase, along with instructions for building each of these open-source
instruments.

We also provide general strategies for extending our code to develope radar instruments
customized to your research needs.

Our software-defined radar code works with most Ettus USRP software-defined radios.
With a few hardware components and one YAML file, you can build an
ice-penetrating radar system, customized for your research needs.

Use our guide to build Peregrine, a field-portable fixed-wing UAV equipped with a miniaturized ice-penetrating radar system.

Use our guide to build MAPPERR, a multi-frequency snowmobile-towed ice-penetrating radar-radiometer system.

ORCA is currently being developed by the University of Colorado Boulder in the Hi-SNR Laboratory. Find their website here

ORCA was originally developed by the Stanford Radio Glaciology Lab, whose cool work can be found here!

title: Baker Mayfield Taunted Immediately After Loss to Browns
description: Baker Mayfield couldn’t get to the locker room without getting called out for a loss to the Cleveland Browns. The post Baker Mayfield Taunted Immediately After Loss to Browns appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Baker Mayfield couldn't get to the locker room after Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Browns without a reminder of his hefty new contract.

"A fan somewhere in the stadium was yelling '$55 million' while Baker Mayfield and the Bucs ran into the tunnel after that loss," cleveland.com's Dan Labbe wrote on X.

After a weather delay of more than two hours, Mayfield returned with a chance to finish a game-winning touchdown drive against his former team. Instead, his fourth-down pass intended for Emeka Egbuka fell incomplete in the rain, allowing Cleveland to escape with a 23-19 victory. The Browns improved to 1-1, while Tampa Bay dropped to 0-2.

It was a disappointing finish to a matchup Mayfield had been anticipating for months. During an August appearance on the "4th and South" podcast with former teammate Jarvis Landry and Leonard Fournette, he identified Cleveland's visit as the game he had circled.

"First home game. Week 2. Cleveland," Mayfield said. "It's time to show [the Browns] which home is better."

Mayfield struck a more measured tone during game week, acknowledging how much Cleveland had changed since his departure. But he made clear that facing a former team still carried extra motivation.

Mayfield entered the season with a new three-year, $165 million extension that runs through 2029. The deal averages $55 million annually, raising the expectations for a quarterback who rebuilt his career in Tampa Bay.

Much of the scrutiny entering Sunday centered on Watson and Cleveland's $230 million investment. But Mayfield gave his own fan base reason for frustration.

He finished 20 of 34 for 182 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Tampa Bay managed just one touchdown, settling for four Chase McLaughlin field goals.

Mayfield also heard boos from the home crowd after consecutive overthrows in the third quarter. Across the field, Watson produced the response he needed with his starting job under scrutiny.

Cleveland trailed 9-6 at halftime and fell behind by 10 early in the third quarter. Watson then helped turn a stagnant offense into one capable of finishing drives, ending the afternoon 24 of 30 for 238 yards and two touchdowns without an interception.

His 55-yard touchdown connection with rookie Denzel Boston tied the game late in the third quarter. It was the longest play of the Browns season so far. Watson later found tight end Blake Whiteheart for a 17-yard touchdown with 3:51 remaining, giving Cleveland the lead it would protect through the delay.

Watson's performance should be enough to keep him in the starting lineup for next Sunday's home opener against the Carolina Panthers.

Before kickoff, Ian Rapoport reported that Cleveland viewed its first two road games as a natural point to evaluate the quarterback position. Watson gave Todd Monken a strong reason to stay with him.

The win also gives Watson a chance at a better reception when he returns to Huntington Bank Field. He was booed during Cleveland's preseason loss to Buffalo, when he completed five of 12 passes for 36 yards and an interception. Watson called the reaction "personal" and "disrespectful."

Coming home at 1-1 after leading a comeback should ease some of the pressure that would have accompanied an 0-2 start.

But Watson cannot make Sunday a one-week exception. He needs to build on the second half against Tampa Bay and give Cleveland consistent production. With Shedeur Sanders waiting behind him, another prolonged stretch of ineffective offense would put a quarterback change back in play.

title: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels out for Seahawks game after gruesome injury
description: Daniels was carted off in the final seconds of the first half of the Dallas Cowboys game and didn’t return.
fullText:
Despite missing Sam Darnold for the majority of their first two games, the Seattle Seahawks have started the season with two straight wins and they're set to take on a shorthanded Washington Commanders squad next, who's starting quarterback recently suffered an all too familiar injury.

Commanders head coach Dan Quinn announced quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered a dislocated left elbow, the same one he injured last season, in the team's 37-20 Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. He is set to undergo further testing on Monday, however the initial X-rays eliminated the possibility of a fracture.

Quinn added there's "optimism" he'll suit up again this season, although testing should help determine an exact timeline and whether the star quarterback will require surgery.

The injury occurred on 3rd and goal shortly before halftime when Daniels tried to brace himself on the turf after slipping while receiving the snap, and landed awkwardly.

Jayden Daniels is down after the Commanders last play.

📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/s6EE4exa6P

It's a crucial blow for the third-year quarterback who's coming off an injury riddled 2025 campaign where he suffered a knee sprain and hamstring injury before the disastrous dislocated elbow in Washington's 38-14 loss to the Seahawks. Daniels missed three games after the previous elbow injury.

Fast forward nearly a year later, and the Commanders are set to be without Daniels for the foreseeable future once again.

Backup Marcus Mariota recorded 111 passing yards as well as a touchdown in limited playing time against the Cowboys and he'll remain under center for Washington's Week 3 matchup against Seattle.

Seeking their first victory of the season, Mariota and the Commanders will be tasked with overcoming a dominant Seahawks defense who allowed just 151 total yards against Arizona.

title: Five Wins for USA Boxing at Melee Gala IX Against Team Canada
description: USA Boxing is rolling up wins as it looks forward to the Pan Am Games and the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games.
fullText:
USA Boxing enjoyed a successful trip to Canada for a team tournament against their Canadian counterparts this week in Winnipeg, Canada.

Six team members participated, with five coming away with victories.

Next up for USA Boxing is preparations for the upcoming Pan American Games in October in Puebla, Mexico.

USA Boxing enjoyed a successful trip to Winnipeg, Canada, for the Melee Gala XI amateur boxing tournament. Members of the United States team faced their Canadian counterparts in a six-bout international duel.

The Stars and Stripes went 5-1 in the international duel behind victories by Noelle Haro, Lorenzo Patricio, Alisha Crockett, Marcus Luther, and Naomi Graham on Saturday, September 19.

Lorenzo Patricio kicked things off for the U.S. on Saturday, earning a unanimous decision victory over Canada's Max Tomines in the 55-kilogram division (bantamweight, 121 pounds).

The Hawaii native improved his international record to 11-2 in 2026, adding a gold medal from the World Boxing Cup: China 2026, and a silver medal from the 77th International Strandja Boxing Tournament. Still just 19 years old, Patricio is a quickly rising star in international competition.

USA Boxing's two women representatives, Naomi Graham and Alisha Crockett, both scored wins that carried Team USA's momentum.

Graham secured a split decision victory over Canada's Viktoria Penney in the 75-kilogram division (middleweight, 165 pounds). The 2020 Tokyo Olympian secured her second international victory of 2026. She also earned a bronze medal at the 77th International Strandja Boxing Tournament earlier this year.

Graham, a 37-year-old native of Fayetteville, North Carolina, has an impressive resume, including a 2019 Pan Am Games gold medal. In 2025, Graham played the role of Laila Ali in the feature film "Christy" about the life of Hall of Fame boxer Christy Martin.

Crockett defeated Canada's Florence Belle Germain by a unanimous decision in the 60-kilogram division (lightweight, 132 pounds). Saturday's win was Crockett's first international win of her career. The Phoenix native, age 24, is one of the newest members on the USA Boxing Elite High Performance Team this year and is a national Golden Gloves champion.

Marcus Luther and Noelle Haro continued the USA's winning streak. Luther defeated Yacine Benaoudia by unanimous decision in the 65-kilogram division (welterweight, 145 pounds). Saturday's win marked the Washington, D.C., native's fifth international unanimous-decision victory in 2026 and improved his international record to 7-3. Luther recently won silver at the World Boxing Cup: China 2026 and is a 2025 Golden Glove winner.

Haro rounded out the day for USA Boxing in the 51-kilogram division (flyweight, 112 pounds). The Texas native improves to 4-2 on the international stage, including a bronze medal at the World Boxing Cup: Brazil 2026. Haro, age 30, fights out of Austin, Texas.

New Jersey native Tyric Trapp fell short to Umar Carcamo by a narrow split decision in the 80-kilogram division (light heavyweight, 176 pounds). Trapp has a 5-4 international record in 2026, including a bronze medal at the 2026 Copa America. He is a two-time national Golden Gloves winner with a bright future.

Team USA will now return to Colorado Springs, where the team will begin camp ahead of the 2026 Pan American Championships. The 2026 Pan American Championships will take place in Puebla, Mexico, from October 17-25.

title: Vikings’ Kevin O’Connell Has Words for Bears QB Caleb Williams After Injury
description: The Chicago Bears offense struggled to find any rhythm as the Minnesota Vikings came away with a 9-3 win in Week 2. The weather played a role, but Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores also made life difficult for Chicago, which managed just three points after putting up 59 in Week 1.Chicago also lost Caleb Williams […] The post Vikings’ Kevin O’Connell Has Words for Bears QB Caleb Williams After Injury appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Chicago Bears offense struggled to find any rhythm as the Minnesota Vikings came away with a 9-3 win in Week 2. The weather played a role, but Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores also made life difficult for Chicago, which managed just three points after putting up 59 in Week 1.

Chicago also lost Caleb Williams in the fourth quarter, adding another problem at a critical point in the game. Before exiting with his injury, Williams completed 15 of 26 passes for 138 yards, one interception, and a 56.2 passer rating.

Williams' injury came with the Bears deep in the red zone and pushing for a touchdown. Without him, the drive ended with a blocked field goal.

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell highlighted several things he liked about the team in the win over the Bears. Nonetheless, the biggest praise came when talking about the defense and containing Williams before his injury.

"I thought the tackling, a couple times in space, that surface can be tough for guys to close space, come to balance, make a tackle, and they were able to make a couple loose plays to get new first downs like that," O'Connell told reporters after the win.

"But for the most part, in between the trenches, I thought our guys answered the bell against a team we knew wanted to run it and try to get some plays off of [Williams]. Caleb is such a unique talent. Even when you think you got him, I give our guys a ton of credit for chasing him around all day, but we did keep him in there enough."

Meanwhile, despite Williams leaving the game with an injury, Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman showed a lot of respect for the Bears star.

"He has a very special, unique skill set," Cashman told reporters postgame. "The way he can make guys move, his elusiveness. We have a lot of respect for him. That's why all week, every day, we were talking about our rush plan, keeping 18 contained in the pocket, and I thought for the most part we did a really good job.

"We knew he was going to get out sometime. He's a great player. It's going to happen, but overall, I thought the guys up front did a really good job."

Nonetheless, the Vikings defense did its job and didn't let their guard down even after Williams left the game, as the contest came down to the final play and the Bears still had a chance to secure the win.

After the loss, Bears tight end Colston Loveland spoke to Marquee Sports Network to share his thoughts on the loss, as he had a quiet day, recording one reception on three targets for three receiving yards.

"Just a sloppy day," Loveland said postgame. "Penalties, turnovers. We knew coming in, whoever wins the turnover margin is probably gonna win this game, and we didn't do that. So just a lot of things we got to clean up, but [Tyson Bagent] fought and gave a lot of effort, which is good to see."

title: Good, bad and ugly coming out of Packers' Week 2 win over Jets
description: Highlighting the good, the bad and the ugly coming out of the Packers' Week 2 win over the Jets.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers overcame two horrific early injuries, a disappointing overall performance on offense, an avalanche of penalties from all three phases and a 17-7 deficit in the fourth quarter to beat the New York Jets by a 20-17 final score in overtime on Sunday.

The good coming out of the comeback win is that even the ugliest of wins still count as wins, and the Packers finally snapped their losing streak -- which dated back to last season -- by flipping the script and orchestrating an unlikely win in the fourth quarter and overtime. But the Packers played really poor football for most of Sunday at MetLife Stadium, and Matt LaFleur's team is fortunate in many ways to have survived the performance and be returning to Green Bay with a 1-1 record.

But again, is it better to control a game for 50 minutes, meltdown and lose, like in Week 1, or sleepwalk through three quarters, wake up and win, like on Sunday? That's an easy choice. But it's still fair to say the Packers have a lot of work to do moving forward.

Highlighting the good, the bad and the ugly coming out of the Packers' Week 2 win:

The final 16 minutes: After falling behind 17-7, the Packers went on a 13-0 run over the final 11 minutes of the fourth quarter and the five minutes of overtime -- finally providing the ever-elusive winning finish. It certainly wasn't a perfect final 16 minutes; the Packers had multiple opportunities to win the game outright in regulation and failed. But in the extra session, the Packers took over, pressuring the Jets into a three-and-out and then calmly moving down the field for the game-winning field goal. Credit where credit is due. In the rain and on the road, the Packers could have folded up shop after MarShawn Lloyd fumbled in the fourth quarter. But the defense got a stop to minimize the damage, the offense finally put a drive together and Skyy Moore provided a highlight special teams play to erase the deficit. Maybe the Packers can build on the final 16 minutes of Sunday and finally put together a competent 60 minutes of play come Thursday night at Lambeau Field.

Bonus: Lukas Van Ness. He was dominant. It's been a long time since we've seen a Packers edge rusher not named Micah Parsons affect the game against the run and pass as consistently as LVN did on Sunday at MetLife Stadium.

The penalties. Most weeks, committing 14 accepted penalties (and the Packers had several others declined!) for 133 yards would easily fit into "The Ugly" section of this recurring post, but not this week. Injuries take the cake coming out of Sunday. But the flag fest at MetLife Stadium nearly sent the Packers to an 0-2 start. Green Bay committed penalties on six of 12 offensive possessions, helping stall numerous drives. Five different defensive players had a penalty and three different players were penalized on special teams, so this was a three-phased failure of composure, focus and fundamentals. The Packers are fortunate the Jets were also in a penalty mood; Aaron Glenn's team had 156 penalty yards, including a 15-yarder on the final drive of overtime setting up the field goal and 61 yards of pass interference penalties drawn by Matthew Golden.

Bonus: That three-play sequence after Skyy Moore's 63-yard punt return. Inside run, inside run, pass on third down. The Packers played that series scared, despite starting the drive in the red zone with a chance to take the lead. They were lucky it didn't end up costing them the game.

The injuries. Much of the game was aesthetically ugly from a football standpoint for the Packers, but nothing comes close to watching players get carted off on back-to-back plays to start the game and finishing the contest with nearly a dozen injuries. It's scary stuff to see a player secured to a backboard after one play and then see a different player carted off with an air cast on his leg on the very next play. Jayden Reed could miss significant time, while Zach Bako-Bewele could miss the rest of the season. Brutal. Throw in another injury to Aaron Banks, plus the short week coming up before playing the Falcons on Thursday night, and the Packers are in rough shape. The hope will be that Bako-Bewele's injury isn't the fatal blow to an offensive line that could be the fatal flaw of the 2026 Packers.

This article originally appeared on Packers Wire: Good, bad and ugly coming out of Packers' Week 2 win over Jets

title: Whatever plan the Cardinals had didn't work against Jaxon Smith-Njigba
description: Would a better plan have even worked for the Cardinals against Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba?
fullText:
It wasn't just a single player who spanked the Arizona Cardinals in their home opener on Sunday, Sept. 20.

The Cardinals thought they had a game plan to contain wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but he reeled in a game-high nine catches for a game-high 155 yards and three touchdowns during the Seattle Seahawks' 31-7 romp at State Farm Stadium.

It was a dominating performance by arguably the best wideout in the NFL. He started things off with a bang by sprinting past a confused Arizona secondary and hauling in an 82-yard TD pass from Drew Lock on Seattle's second play of its opening possession.

Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told reporters it was because the defense was playing Cover Zero, meaning there were no defensive backs available downfield to help. Cardinals veteran safety Budda Baker called it what it was — a mistake.

"That play was a bad communication, a lot of guys playing something, a lot of guys playing a different thing," he said after the Cardinals fell to 1-1. "I put it on myself to communicate better so everyone understands what the call is. That's what happened on that one."

That play was the only real blemish for the Cardinals during an otherwise competitive first half, which ended with the teams tied at 7. Arizona, LaFleur said, saw some hope and a chance. Instead, the Cardinals saw more of Smith-Njigba.

The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year found the end zone just 2½ minutes into the third quarter when Lock fired over the middle, Cardinals cornerback Max Melton slipped and fell, and Smith-Njigba jumped to snare a casual 7-yard TD.

After converting a Jacoby Brisset interception into a field goal, JSN and the defending Super Bowl champions struck again when Smith-Njigba caught a 12-yard pass in the end zone, running right to left ahead of Baker's coverage.

"We had a plan," Baker said, "and the plan just wasn't good enough."

It was 24-7 with 12:40 left to play, and it was a dagger that killed any thought of a Cardinals' comeback.

"He's a dang good receiver," LaFleur said of Smith-Njigba. "The second play (early in the first quarter), that's one obviously you want back. We can be better than that just from an execution standpoint. But he's a dang good receiver. He's arguably the best one."

LaFleur said his Cardinals were focused on stopping Smith-Njigba, but added, "You don't want to sacrifice stopping the run and stuff, too, so you're mixing and matching it.

"I don't even know what his stats were. I'm not worried about it schematically in terms of what he was doing. He's going to get his at times. You've got to limit it and help our guys out, but I don't think that was the case. I thought we were playing real good defense up until probably that last 20 minutes, and they kind of just took over from there."

If Brissett (95 passing yards) and the offense (151 total yards) had performed better, Sunday's game could have been a lot closer and easier to stomach. But when the Seahawks finished their convincing win with a late, methodical 16-play, 70-yard TD drive that consumed 10 minutes and 14 seconds, it was an absolute gut punch.

"You've still got to go play defense," Cardinals outside linebacker Zaven Collins said. "I've just got to buckle down and play as much ball as necessary, whether it's three-and-out or having to go 16 plays or whatever it was."

The Cardinals better rest up and get ready because they're about to face another potential game-wrecker of a playmaker in versatile running back Christian McCaffrey when they play at the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Sept. 27.

McCaffrey has faced the Cardinals nine times in his career, scoring 13 touchdowns (seven rushing, six receiving) and logging 713 yards on 130 carries (5.5 average) and 554 yards on 59 catches (9.4 average).

In San Francisco's 35-13 win over Miami in Week 2, McCaffrey ran for two touchdowns to become the fourth-fastest player in the Super Bowl-era history to reach 100 career touchdowns and the third player ever with at least 50 TDs with two different franchises.

He's been a Cardinals' killer, and Baker, perhaps more than anyone in the Arizona locker room, knows it.

Not that he was ready to fast-forward and dive into what it'll take to slow down CMC better than the Cardinals tried to contain JSN. Baker, after all, hadn't even reached the showers when he consented to stop for a quick postgame interview.

"Yeah, yeah," he said, nodding his head about McCaffrey. "Personally, man, we just lost. I've got to watch the film and see the things we've done good, see the things we've done bad and just try to correct those details, and then we'll get onto the 49ers."

If the Cardinals let CMC do to them what JSN just did, they'll likely be SOL.

title: Cubs infielder Alex Bregman’s horse wins at Churchill Downs, then gets claimed by new owners
description: Alex Bregman and his Chicago Cubs teammates celebrated a win at Churchill Downs when Bregman's horse, Act of Parliament, won his race.
fullText:
LOUISVILLE, Ky. — Alex Bregman and his Chicago Cubs teammates celebrated the third baseman's horse winning a race at Churchill Downs.

It was short-lived, however, when the horse was claimed by new owners afterward.

Act of Parliament overcame a troubled start under jockey Axel Concepcion and rallied to win by three-quarters of a length on Thursday. The 3-year-old colt paid $8.68 to win.

"It was electric," winning trainer Will Walden said. "To have Alex and the entire team here and then have the horse come through like that made it a pretty special night."

The Cubs visited the historic Louisville track on their off day before opening a three-game set at Cincinnati on Friday.

Cubs MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong delivered a pep talk to Act of Parliament in the paddock before the race. Cubs manager Craig Counsell led the colt into the winner's circle afterward.

Several Cubs rookies dressed in racing-themed costumes, including pitcher Ryan Rolison, who donned a horse costume, and Pedro Ramirez, who dressed as a jockey.

Bregman Family Racing, the ballplayer's stable, bought Act of Parliament for $65,000.

The colt earned $27,108 for his first career victory. But Bregman lost him in the claiming race.

Act of Parliament was claimed for $20,000 afterward in a random blind draw used to break a tie when six different owners submitted bids beforehand to buy the colt. He was then transferred to a new trainer.

title: Chargers' Justin Herbert is off to a rough start under new coordinator Mike McDaniel
description: Herbert struggled for the second straight week on his home field — this time in front of a hostile crowd — as Los Angeles fell to 0-2 with its second 26-14 loss this season, this time to the Las Vegas Raiders.  Herbert was 15 of 27 for 192 yards with two interceptions and fumbled three times, although the Chargers recovered all three.
fullText:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — Two games into the season, the returns aren't promising for the Chargers and quarterback Justin Herbert under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.

Herbert struggled for the second straight week on his home field — this time in front of a hostile crowd — as Los Angeles fell to 0-2 with its second 26-14 loss this season, this time to the Las Vegas Raiders.

Herbert was 15 of 27 for 192 yards with two interceptions and fumbled three times, although the Chargers recovered all three. Los Angeles fumbled six times on the day, losing one.

In his debut with McDaniel — who spent the previous for seasons as head coach of the Miami Dolphins — calling the plays, Herbert threw for a modest 209 yards with a touchdown and a pick in a loss to Arizona.

Known as a passer who has put up big numbers in the regular season but struggled in the playoffs, Herbert doesn't even have statistics on his side so far in 2026.

"There's a room full of grown men that can handle their job and they're going to do everything they can to correct it and fix it," Herbert said. "We're going to stick together. It's tough. No one wants to lose two games but there's nothing we can do about it now."

Translating what Herbert considers to be productive practices into game success would be a step in the right direction.

"We just have to be better," Herbert said. "That's not good enough and we can't expect to win games when we're playing like that."

Herbert wasn't completely to blame. Chargers receivers dropped three passes in the first half, including a bobble by David Njoku that ended up as an interception by the Raiders' Hezekiah Masses.

Herbert's second interception came with less than three minutes remaining and Los Angeles trailing 24-14. The Raiders tacked on a safety when Chargers right tackle Joe Alt was called for holding in the end zone with 1:46 left.

That sent the pro-Raiders crowd — the franchise called Los Angeles home from 1982-94 and maintains a strong Southern California fan base — into a frenzy.

Alt was supposed to supply stability for the passing game after playing just six games last season because of an ankle injury that required surgery. He was called for four penalties Sunday.

The addition of free-agent center Tyler Biadasz was also expected to help a beleaguered offensive line, but he was lost in training camp with a knee injury.

Coach Jim Harbaugh will look to fix the offensive line and his team's other problems before next weekend game at unbeaten Buffalo.

"The 'why' is what we'll be talking about," Harbaugh said. "We'll look at the tape. We'll go back to work. That's all I know how to do. That's all we know how to do. Find the way and we'll move forward. It's a one-week league."

title: Late interception, missed field goal, punt spell doom for Jaguars
description: The Jaguars have prided themsleves on finishing off opponents, which made their second-half collapse against Denver all the more surprising.
fullText:
DENVER — So many times during their nine-game regular-season winning streak bridging the last part of 2025 and the first part of 2026, the Jacksonville Jaguars majored in pounding the figurative gas pedal to the floor and keeping it there.

Led Indianapolis 21-10 and won 36-19.

Led Denver 31-17 and won 34-20.

Led the second Indianapolis game 20-17 and won 23-17.

The Jaguars maintained maximum effort and top-flight execution and focus. They didn't give their opponents hope. They didn't get comfortable. They ran through the tape of the finish line exactly like they stormed out of the starting blocks.

All of which made their 20-13 come-from-ahead loss to the Broncos here at Mile High Stadium all the more confusing.

In a cauldron of noise and against a Broncos team that was on the cusp of reeling, the Jaguars led 13-3 with 9:02 left in the third quarter.

Was it like last November in Houston? No, that was a full-blown meltdown, blowing a 19-point lead.

Was it embarrassing? No. The Broncos are good.

Was it a collapse? The data suggests yes.

The Jaguars' offense finished interception, missed field goal and punt.

The defense finished by allowing the Broncos to go field goal, touchdown, touchdown and, in the final indignity, run out the final 4 minutes, 41 seconds.

"Very frustrating," Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison said. "We knew we left a lot of plays out there on the field. We didn't ride the momentum."

What kind of momentum did the Jaguars have? They had leads of 7-0, 10-3, 13-3 and 13-6. They didn't trail until 7:21 remained.

The Jaguars' defense had an eye-popping goal-line stand in the second quarter. The Broncos had first-and-goal from the 1 (no gain), second-and-goal from the 1 (no gain) and third-and-goal from the 1 (loss of 5 yards.). Denver was booed off the field.

But the offense lost 4 yards and punted.

Cornerback Jourdan Lewis intercepted Bo Nix in the end zone to thwart another Broncos drive. Denver was booed off the field again.

The Jaguars drove 54 yards in seven plays to take a 10-3 halftime lead on Cam Little's 44-yard field goal.

But there were warning signs all over the field that the Jaguars were messing with danger.

"We were sloppy, even in the first half; we just made some plays to make up for it," Lewis said. "But we were sloppy and not on the details."

The pass protection sprung a leak, the pass rush wasn't getting home and the Broncos rolled up 188 first-half yards.

The Jaguars captured the momentum on the two-minute drill to finish the first half and were well-positioned to seize control by opening the second half with a touchdown. They had first-and-goal from the 3. But running back Chris Rodriguez, Jr. had no room (loss of 2), quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw for no gain to running back Bhayshul Tuten and, on third down, running back LeQuint Allen, Jr., dropped a pass at the 1. Had he caught it, coach Liam Coen said he would have gone for it.

The lead was 13-3, but felt much tighter. The Jaguars had committed a major error: They had given their beleaguered opponent hope.

The Broncos answered the Jaguars' field goal with a field goal. It was 13-6.

The Broncos intercepted Lawrence and scored a touchdown. It was 13-13.

And the Broncos saw Little miss from 54 yards and scored a touchdown. It was 20-13.

Ballgame over. Gut punch administered.

"It was a little strange, but there were mental errors and just doing things we don't normally do," defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton said.

Yes, DaVon, it was a little strange because we had been spoiled 'round these parts (save for the aforementioned loss at Houston) by the Jaguars' finishing kick in the regular season.

The Jaguars didn't get passive against Denver. They didn't sit on the lead hoping the Broncos would continue to make mistake after mistake after mistake. Things … just … stopped … working.

"You need a drive, you needed a stop, you needed a catch, you needed a play," Coen said. "We just didn't do it."

And the Broncos did. During their comeback from 10 points down, the Denver offense had six completions of at least 10 yards and two 12-yard rushes. None of the Jaguars' three units had an answer.

"We didn't coach it good enough, we didn't play it good enough and we did not finish," Coen said.

Accurate, accurate and accurate.

A good thing for the Jaguars is the Texans are 0-2 (both home losses). Even the most optimistic Jaguars fan didn't have the Denver game as a win when the schedule came out. The key is to beat New England at home next week and find a way to go at least 2-1 against Cincinnati, Philadelphia and Houston. And when they're in the lead (and they will be), remember what happened against the Broncos.

title: Studs and Duds from the Browns' Week 2 win over the Bucs
description: Our stud and dud selections from the Browns' Week 2 win are out.
fullText:
In a wild, weather-impacted battle at Raymond James Stadium, the Cleveland Browns flipped the script on their season with a gritty 23-19 comeback victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

A lightning delay that halted play for two hours and 12 minutes added unexpected drama, but Cleveland's second-half surge proved decisive as they scored touchdowns on two of their final four possessions to steal a road win despite losing the overall yardage total.

Stat Line: 5 receptions, 95 yards, 1 TD

Boston was the catalyst that ignited Cleveland's dormant passing game, providing explosive, game-changing plays when the offense desperately needed a spark. Late in the third quarter, the rookie wideout evaded a Buccaneers defensive back and blew open the game with a electric 55-yard touchdown catch-and-run that tied the contest at 16–16.

Denzel Boston is the fifth @NFL receiver since 2003 w/ 50+ receiving yards & a receiving TD in EACH of their first two career games:

• DENZEL BOSTON (2026)
• Jordan Addison (2023)
• Ja’Marr Chase (2021)
• Terry McLaurin (2019)
• Calvin Johnson (2007) pic.twitter.com/dExeEimvt6

Boston consistently separated against Tampa Bay's perimeter cornerbacks, finishing as the game's leading receiver and solidifying his role as the centerpiece of this receiving core.

Stat Line: 24/30 passing, 238 yards, 2 TDs, 0 INTs, 121.9 passer rating

Shaking off a miserable first half, Watson engineered the most efficient performance he's had in a Browns uniform. He distributed the ball with surgical precision down the stretch, completing 80 percent of his passes and orchestrating a 12-play, 68-yard go-ahead drive in the fourth quarter where he converted four high-pressure third downs before throwing the game-winning 17-yard touchdown pass to Blake Whiteheart.

We'll see if this game ever starts again but as of now, it's pacing to be Deshaun Watson's best game by EPA per dropback in his time with the Cleveland Browns.

The Bucs defense has been really underwhelming through two weeks, especially the linebackers and underneath coverage. pic.twitter.com/8lWKmY2mDw

Stat Line: 3 total tackles, 1.0 sack, 2 tackles for loss

Graham continues to prove that his disruptive rookie campaign was no fluke, anchoring an interior defensive front that held firm when the game was on the line.

He blew up multiple interior run schemes, brought down Baker Mayfield for a crucial third-down sack in the third quarter, and routinely reset the line of scrimmage against Tampa Bay's interior guards. Graham's penetration forced Mayfield into hurried throws and helped limit Tampa Bay to field goals on multiple red-zone trips.

Stat Line: 3/3 field goals (long of 50 yards), 2/2 extra points, 11 total points

When the offense was completely bogged down in the first half, Szmyt single-handedly kept Cleveland within striking distance by drilling field goals from 50 and 48 yards out. He later knocked through a 34-yard attempt in the third quarter to cap off a drive, executing with flawless mechanics under dynamic crosswinds and eventual downpours in Tampa. On an afternoon where points were hard to come by, Szmyt provided a reliable security net.

Stat Line: 12 carries, 21 rushing yards (1.75 YPC), 5 receptions, 27 receiving yards

Judkins found almost no running room against Vita Vea and a stout Tampa Bay front, repeatedly getting contacted at or behind the line of scrimmage.

Outside of contributing five checkdown catches, he failed to gain leverage in the run game, averaging under two yards per carry and leaving Cleveland stuck behind the chains.

Stat Line: 1 total tackle, 0 sacks, 0 QB hits

Verse delivered another quiet performance off the edge, failing to make an impact against Tampa Bay's offensive tackles. He was routinely sealed out on stretch runs, enabling Bucky Irving to rip off key explosive gains on the perimeter, and failed to record a single quarterback hit on Mayfield. For a high-profile pass rusher expected to generate dynamic disruption, floating through back-to-back games without a signature play is a growing concern.

title: NFL intends to proceed with Ravens-Cowboys in Brazil, despite field concerns
description: When it comes to the NFL's obsession with expanding pro football's footprint, nothing will get in the way.
fullText:
When it comes to the NFL's obsession with expanding pro football's footprint, nothing will get in the way.

Concerns exist regarding the quality of the playing surface in Rio de Janeiro for next Sunday's game between the Ravens and Cowboys. The league, however, is undeterred.

Via Mark Maske of Front Office Sports, a league spokesperson said Sunday that (quoting Maske not the spokesperson) "the league is looking forward to the game in Rio and, as with all international games, it has a plan in place to ensure a high-quality playing surface."

Separately, the NFL Players Association told Maske that it's aware of the situation, and that it has been in touch with the league office about it.

Eight years ago, the NFL moved a Chiefs-Rams game from Mexico City to L.A. due to field concerns. However, the league has seemingly adopted a "damn the torpedoes" approach wen it comes to globalizing the game — and it doesn't seem to be inclined to let something like a less-than-ideal field get in the way.

title: Defense clamps down after Week 1 tackling woes, fueling Broncos' 20-13 comeback win over Jaguars
description: The Denver Broncos ' defense went back to the basics after a disastrous opener in Kansas City.  The defense limited Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville offense to three points in the second half — and none over the final 24 minutes — allowing Bo Nix to stage a comeback as the Broncos rallied for a 20-13 win Sunday.  “Look, our job is to play the game and give the ball to the offense,” linebacker Alex Singleton said after his defense's rebound.
fullText:
DENVER (AP) — The Denver Broncos ' defense went back to the basics after a disastrous opener in Kansas City. It focused on the most fundamental part of football there is — tackling.

The defense limited Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville offense to three points in the second half — and none over the final 24 minutes — allowing Bo Nix to stage a comeback as the Broncos rallied for a 20-13 win Sunday.

"Look, our job is to play the game and give the ball to the offense," linebacker Alex Singleton said after his defense's rebound.

A job made easier by simply wrapping up.

The Broncos re-emphasized fundamentals all week after missing a whopping 28 tackles in a 31-10 loss to Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. They held the Jaguars under 100 yards rushing Sunday and kept Lawrence out of the end zone after he threw for three TDs and ran for another in a 34-20 win in Denver last December.

"It was being better this week and being one step better, having that short-term memory," Pat Surtain II explained. "Erase that week and just focus on this week ahead."

The Broncos (1-1) were one of the top defenses in the league last season, but it wasn't on display in Week 1. That could possibly be chalked up to not playing all that many snaps in the preseason.

One thing's for sure — the team's confidence never wavered.

"It's funny how everyone was freaking out after one game," defensive lineman Zach Allen said. "We got back on track today."

Trailing 13-3 in the third quarter, the defense dug in as Nix and the offense found their groove in reeling off 17 straight points to snap the Jaguars' nine-game regular-season winning streak.

The Jaguars finished the game by going interception, missed field goal and punt. The Broncos' last four drives looked like this: field goal, TD, TD and victory formation.

"It was a good day for the team to bounce back," said cornerback Riley Moss, who picked off Lawrence's pass late in the third quarter. "There's still things that we've got to work on. It wasn't a perfect game, but we got the 'W.'"

Last December, Lawrence threw for 279 yards and three TDs with no interceptions. This time, it was a different story. Lawrence threw for 138 yards in the first half but only 51 more the rest of the way. What's more, the Broncos held the Jaguars to 2 of 6 on third-down conversions in the second half.

"As as far what they did, it wasn't anything that surprised us," Lawrence said. "They played really good up front. They got after us a little bit and I thought we played on our heels a little bit."

In constant pursuit was pass rusher Nik Bonitto, who had three QB hits. He led a group that kept constant pressure on Lawrence.

"They're a great offense," Bonitto said. "But at the same time, we look at last year's game and we see it was really just missed tackles that gave them a lot of points and even this year making sure that we're playing to our standard."

One of the biggest sequences of the game was in the third quarter and the Jaguars facing a first-and-goal at the 9. Denver held them to a field goal to make it 13-3 and keep the game in range.

"We made game-changing plays," said Surtain, whose team hosts the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday night. "That's what we did — just finding ways to get them off the field, finding ways to win third down. That was huge."

title: Monique Billings steals spotlight with eye-catching pregame outfit before Fever game
description: Monique Billings brought plenty of color and personality to Gainbridge Fieldhouse with her coordinated pregame outfit before Sunday’s game against the Washington Mystics.
fullText:
Monique Billings steals spotlight with eye-catching pregame outfit before Fever game originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Monique Billings delivered one of the most colorful WNBA pregame looks of the weekend. The Indiana Fever forward arrived at Gainbridge Fieldhouse before Sunday's game against the Washington Mystics wearing a coordinated blue-and-red plaid ensemble featuring a sleeveless cropped vest and matching skirt.

Billings added a silver chain belt, rose-tinted glasses, several bracelets and white knee-high boots to complete the vibrant look.

Athlete Vanity shared a photo of Billings' pregame outfit on X.

Billings appeared to enjoy every second of the arrival. She smiled as she walked through the arena with her arms extended, bringing the same unmistakable energy to the tunnel that she routinely gives the Fever on the court.

It was confident, colorful and full of personality.

WNBA tunnel fashion gives players an opportunity to show a different side of themselves before the competition begins.

Monique Billings 📸 https://t.co/yYujvLUs9kpic.twitter.com/1StIZRZtpj

Billings took full advantage Sunday.

The matching plaid pieces provided the foundation of her outfit, but the accessories turned it into one of the day's most noticeable looks. The chain belt added another layer to the coordinated set, while the tinted glasses and white boots prevented the ensemble from feeling too traditional.

Even the way Billings entered the arena helped sell the outfit. Rather than stopping for a formal pose, the veteran forward looked as though she were dancing her way through the tunnel.

That joy has become an important part of what Billings provides Indiana.

The 6-foot-4 forward joined the Fever in free agency in April after spending the 2025 season with the Golden State Valkyries. She signed a multiyear contract with Indiana and brought another experienced frontcourt option to a roster built to compete for a championship.

Billings previously spent six seasons with the Atlanta Dream before playing for the Dallas Wings, Phoenix Mercury and Valkyries. She also competed for Hive BC during the 2026 Unrivaled season and represented the United States during the FIBA Women's World Cup qualifying tournament.

Her career has required adaptability, and that versatility has helped her establish a meaningful role with the Fever.

Billings can rebound, defend multiple frontcourt positions and provide energy without needing the offense designed around her. Her willingness to do the less glamorous work has made her a useful piece alongside Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston.

There was nothing understated about her Sunday outfit, however.

MORE: Sophie Cunningham's sharp pregame outfit turns heads before Fever-Mystics game

Billings' pregame arrival came before a pivotal matchup in the WNBA playoff race. Indiana entered Sunday with a 27-14 record and an opportunity to create more separation from Washington in the standings. The Mystics instead took control early and earned a 93-77 victory.

Washington improved to 26-16 while Indiana fell to 27-15, tightening the race for postseason positioning. The Mystics shot 57 percent from the field and received dominant performances from their frontcourt. Kiki Iriafen finished with 21 points and 14 rebounds, while Shakira Austin recorded 20 points and 10 rebounds.

Caitlin Clark led the Fever with 25 points, but Indiana could not overcome a first half in which Washington built a 20-point advantage. The loss also gave the Mystics the head-to-head tiebreaker after the teams split their first two meetings of the season.

Indiana still has an opportunity to improve its position before the playoffs begin, but Sunday represented a missed chance for the Fever. Billings, meanwhile, provided one of the afternoon's brightest moments before the game even started.

Between her coordinated plaid set, distinctive accessories and energetic entrance, the Fever forward made certain her latest tunnel appearance would not go unnoticed.

title: Panthers produce stunning 56-point turnaround after historic embarrassment
description: Carolina allowed a franchise-record 59 points in Week 1, then delivered one of Sunday’s most dominant victories.
fullText:
Panthers produce stunning 56-point turnaround after historic embarrassment originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Seven days completely changed the conversation surrounding the Carolina Panthers. Carolina surrendered a franchise-record 59 points in its season-opening loss to the Chicago Bears. The defensive performance created immediate questions about the team's toughness, preparation and ability to compete in the NFC South.

The Panthers answered every one of them Sunday. Carolina demolished the Atlanta Falcons 34-3 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, producing a 56-point improvement in scoring margin from one week to the next.

Bryce Young threw for 287 yards and three touchdowns. Devin Lloyd intercepted two passes, returned one for a touchdown and helped the Panthers force five Atlanta turnovers.

The result was not merely a bounce-back victory.

Young has thrown six touchdown passes through Carolina's first two games and added another score on the ground. His three-touchdown performance against Atlanta pushed his passer rating for the season to 113.3. Young found veteran tight end Darren Waller for two touchdowns. Waller's production carried additional meaning because the game marked his first appearance in his hometown of Atlanta in six years.

Tetairoa McMillan added five receptions for 101 yards, giving Young a dynamic downfield option. Xavier Legette produced a 55-yard reception that helped Carolina establish control early.

The Panthers led 20-3 at halftime and never allowed Atlanta to threaten.

That represented a dramatic change from Week 1, when Carolina's defense appeared incapable of generating a stop.

MORE: Caleb Williams injury overshadows Bears' brutal loss to Vikings

Lloyd was involved in nearly every important defensive moment. The linebacker forced a fumble from Cooper Rush and recorded two interceptions. His second pick came on rookie Jack Strand's first NFL pass, which Lloyd returned for a touchdown.

Atlanta committed turnovers with both quarterbacks and failed to reach the red zone for the second consecutive game.

Rush completed passes for only 86 yards before being replaced. Strand's introduction produced an immediate defensive touchdown for Carolina. The Falcons fell to 0-2 and left the afternoon with major questions about their quarterback situation and offensive structure.

Carolina faced an entirely different reality.

The Panthers became only the fifth team in franchise history to score at least 30 points in a road victory. More importantly, they demonstrated that their disastrous opener did not have to define their season.

Young looked decisive. Waller looked healthy. McMillan looked capable of becoming a featured receiver. The defense played with the aggression and discipline missing against Chicago.

One dominant afternoon does not erase every concern created by allowing 59 points. It does prove the Panthers were capable of responding rather than unraveling. Carolina's scoring margin moved from minus-22 in Week 1 to plus-31 in Week 2.

A 56-point swing in seven days might be the most unexpected statistic of the NFL weekend.

title: Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase join exclusive NFL club in Bengals’ win vs. Texans
description: One of the greatest QB-WR duos in NFL history.
fullText:
Joe Burrow has started slowly in nearly every season of his career. He hasn't been prolific through two games this season, but he's been successful.

In addition, he's joined some elite company alongside his running mate, Ja'Marr Chase.

For only the second time in his career, Burrow has thrown for 200+ yards in each of his first two games of the season. Sunday in Houston, Burrow threw for 207 yards and two touchdowns on 20/31 passing with no interceptions.

Both touchdowns went to Chase, giving the duo 50 touchdown connections for their career. According to NFL researcher Arye Pulli, only four QB-WR duos in NFL history have hit that mark before reaching the age of 30, and the Burrow-Chase duo just joined the club.

Chase finished the game with seven catches for 75 yards and those two scores.

QB-WR duos in NFL history to reach 50 touchdown connections while both players were under 30:

🏈 Dan Marino — Mark Clayton
🏈 John Hadl — Lance Alworth
🏈 Daunte Culpepper — Randy Moss
🏈 Joe Burrow — Ja’Marr Chase

That’s the entire list.

Again, Burrow hasn't been prolific yet. But he's been productive and successful.

On Sunday, Burrow also showed his toughness as he dealt with back tightness during the week leading up to Sunday. Not ideal going up against the Texans' defense. But Burrow wasn't mincing words or backing down earlier this week when he said he was good to go.

On Sunday in Houston, Burrow went out and withstood five sacks, delivering a performance that helped the Bengals to a massive road win.

We've seen Burrow deliver performances like this while banged up and taking several hits in a game. Houston's defense is ferocious, and they sacked Burrow five times on Sunday. Yet Burrow extended plays, including the second touchdown to Chase and a 16-yard third-down pass to Samaje Perine.

Despite back tightness and Houston's defense, Burrow overcame it all, and the Bengals are now 2-0. Just wait till he starts posting prolific numbers.

Coach Pete Golding's Ole Miss football team scored perhaps the biggest win of Week 3 in college football, beating LSU 32-24 on a day when QB Trinidad Chambliss looked like a Heisman favorite. Ole Miss has a big target on its back after ascending to the fourth spot in the latest rankings. title: Former Steelers HC Mike Tomlin offers excellent analysis of offensive struggles
description: Sunday's performance by the Steelers offense reminded of the team under Mike Tomlin and he talked about what he saw after the loss.
fullText:
Sunday's offensive performance by the Pittsburgh Steelers was forgettable to say the least. There was nothing about what the Steelers did on offense against the New England Patriots to take away as a positive. Pittsburgh failed to score a touchdown and finished with just 235 total yards of offense.

Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin, who is now an analyst for NBC, was asked for his thoughts on the game and he was very honest in his evaluation, even though the game reminded us a great deal of the offense from many games in the Tomlin era.

"From my perspective, they don't have a place to hang their hat," Tomlin said. "They haven't established the run. They're not performing well enough on third-down or possession-down circumstances. And to make matters worse, they're not getting yards in chunks. They can't solve all their problems, but they better solve at least one of these problems, and really soon."

All of the problems with the Steelers center on two factors. One, they have invested heavily in the offensive line and it hasn't paid off and two, the skill position players on the team lack any level of explosion, which just congests the offense at the line of scrimmage or in coverage. These aren't coaching fixes; they are roster fixes, and right now there aren't any players available short of pulling off some big trades to correct these problems during the season.

On the bright side, Michael Penix Jr. is expected to return next week. However, we will have to wait and see what Kevin Stefanski says on Monday morning.

title: Iga Swiatek’s former coach knows exactly why she lost in the fourth round of the US Open
description: Iga Swiatek came into the US Open with newfound confidence, but that didn’t translate to results. The Pole had ended her title drought at the...
fullText:
Iga Swiatek came into the US Open with newfound confidence, but that didn't translate to results.

The Pole had ended her title drought at the Canadian Open with a resurgent run before reaching the semifinals of the Cincinnati Open.

Swiatek then started well in New York, winning her first three matches without dropping a set.

But she ended up losing to Qinwen Zheng in the fourth round, falling 7-5, 6-3 to the Chinese player.

Two weeks after her exit, Swiatek's old coach, Katerina Urbanova, provided an explanation for the defeat.

As per sport.pl, Urbanova was asked if she saw the loss to Zheng coming.

She replied: "I had noticed it before. It was different in the third-round US Open match against Marie Bouzková.

"The Czech player played well. Poles thought that she played at a very high level, though in my opinion, it was just her normal.

"However, the situation favoured Iga in that match because Bouzkov hits shorter balls, so Iga could capitalise on those with the power of her own shots.

"If we go back to the match with Zheng, you could see that the Chinese player began hitting high balls that landed deep near the baseline, whereas she had previously played shorter balls and mixed up her style.

"This variation threw Iga off. At the same time, while she had been returning very well leading up to the match against Zheng, that return game was missing in this last match."

"She has reverted to the issues she's been dealing with all season. She did have a better run in recent weeks, winning the tournament in Toronto and reaching the semifinals in Cincinnati.

"However, she still lacks self-confidence. We also have to remember that her rivals now know how to play against her. It only takes a few slower balls to make Iga start committing errors. She struggles most with so-called "dead balls"- shots where she has to generate her own pace.

"That's when she starts missing often. Her opponents know this and force her into committing errors, particularly on the forehand side."

Asked how Swiatek can deal with her ongoing issues, Urbanova responded: "The problem is that tennis is constantly evolving, and her power no longer makes quite the same impression. An important technical challenge is still her forehand grip; it is unconventional and requires work.

"Perhaps her Spanish coach can manage to make changes? I see him trying to get Iga to stay lower on her legs.

"She has stopped jumping into her shots and is now more grounded; this will allow for greater stability over time. Iga is having a really poor season, but things have started moving in the right direction since Wimbledon.

"Even before the US Open, her serving has improved and she was returning well. However, when those elements falter, she reverts to old habits, playing too cautiously.

"She is afraid to pull the trigger at certain moments and slows down her swing. What worries me – as a coach who has known her since childhood – is that Iga sometimes lacks courage on the court; she retreats during rallies or at specific stages of a match."

Swiatek's results this year have seen her fall to ninth in the WTA rankings.

title: Cubs’ Alex Bregman shares selfie showing damage from foul ball to face
description: A foul ball left Alex Bregman with significant facial injuries.
fullText:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman shared a graphic selfie Sunday after suffering a frightening facial injury from a foul ball during an MLB game.

Bregman was struck during the fourth inning of Chicago's 9-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Teammate Michael Busch fouled a pitch from Luis Mey, and the ball bounced into Bregman while he stood near the on-deck circle.

Bregman immediately left the game with blood visible on his face. He later underwent hospital testing after the ball struck him near his cheekbone.

MORE: Tarik Skubal leaves Dodgers temporarily for personal reasons 1 day after start against Giants

The selfie, which he shared on his Instagram, showed significant swelling around Bregman's eye, along with facial cuts and a nosebleed. Especially the area below his eye had turned slightly black. He also included a message for supporters: "Thanks for all the messages, y'all. I'll be back 🙏."

Cubs manager Craig Counsell described the incident as a "terrible, terrible accident." He said the team's priority was getting positive medical results after Bregman was taken to the hospital.

The injury came during an important stretch for Chicago. The Cubs entered Sunday chasing a postseason berth and remained positioned for a National League wild-card spot.

Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman (3) walks off the field after getting hit by a foul ball in the fourth inning in the game against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Bregman had already contributed during Sunday's game before leaving. He delivered an RBI single in the first inning, helping Chicago build an early lead.

After Bregman exited, Matt Shaw replaced him as a pinch-hitter. Pedro Ramirez shifted to third base while Shaw moved to second.

The Cubs continued producing offensively without their veteran third baseman. Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 45th home run, while Michael Conforto and Seiya Suzuki also homered.

MORE: Yankees make sudden change to lineup, remove breakout star

Chicago now faces a balance between its postseason push and Bregman's recovery. His defensive stability and veteran experience remain valuable during the final week.

Counsell said Bregman's general well-being came before baseball considerations. "I want to get a good report first," the manager said.

Bregman's message offered some optimism, but his return timeline remains unclear. The Cubs will need to await further medical updates before determining his availability.

title: Croatia Forward Boris Tisma No Longer Part of Washington Basketball
description: One of the Washington Huskies' incoming international signings is no longer set to play for Danny Sprinkle.
fullText:
Despite appearing in practice footage over the past couple of months, incoming Croatian forward Boris Tisma is no longer set to play for the Washington Huskies in the 2026-27 season.

Tisma, one of several reported international signings for UW coach Danny Sprinkle this offseason, has now signed a two-year contract with Movistar Estudiantes, a professional team based in Madrid, Spain. He previously played for Real Madrid in 2020-21 and was then loaned out to another Liga ACB team in 2021.

Prior to the 6-foot-9 power forward's move to America, he played for two teams in Croatia—Split (2022-25) and Zadar (2025-26)—and one SC Derby in Montenegro, proving to be a rising international prospect that attracted the attention of several schools, including UW.

📝 OFICIAL 

Boris Tisma, nuevo jugador de Movistar Estudiantes.

El ala-pívot croata (2,04 m, 2002) se incorpora al equipo para las dos próximas temporadas. 🇭🇷

¡Bienvenido, Boris! 💙

👇https://t.co/pTOdmOqkig pic.twitter.com/KS3dzh0ECT

The departure of Tisma isn't surprising in the wake of the NCAA changing eligibility requirements for international players coming to the United States back in May. Any player who has signed a professional contract prior to coming to the States now loses their eligibility, though it's unclear if that's the specific reason why UW and Tisma parted.

In the past two months, the Huskies have added a pair of transfers, former Rutgers guard Harun Zrno and ex-Nevada guard Tayshawn Comer, but still have a void to fill in the post with the loss of Tisma. UW has not released its 2026-27 roster on the school's website with less than one month until Sprinkle's team hits the road to face Boise State in a preseason exhibition on October 17 at Idaho Central Arena.

As of now, UW has five bigs going into year three under Sprinkle: second-year forwards Jasir Rencher and Nikola Dzepina, third-year center Lathan Somerville, fourth-year forward Mady Traore, and incoming fourth-year transfer LeJuan Watts.

title: Zach Johnson wins at Pebble Beach for 2nd straight Champions victory and 6th of the season
description: Zach Johnson won the Pure Insurance Championship on Sunday at foggy Pebble Beach for his second straight PGA Tour Champions victory and the sixth in his first season on the 50-and-over circuit.
fullText:
PEBBLE BEACH, Calif. — Zach Johnson won the Pure Insurance Championship on Sunday at foggy Pebble Beach for his second straight PGA Tour Champions victory and the sixth in his first season on the 50-and-over circuit.

Johnson broke a tie with Stewart Cink for the tour victory lead, closing with a 7-under 65 for a two-stroke victory over former LIV player Henrik Stenson, Steven Alker and early starter Rory Sabbatini. Johnson, the Sanford International winner last week in South Dakota, had a 14-under 202 total.

Johnson won the six titles in only 15 starts. The Iowa native won 12 times on the PGA Tour, highlighted by major titles at the 2007 Masters and 2015 British Open.

Sabbatini shot a 63 — the best round of the week — to post at 12 under. He parred the final two holes, finishing as the other leaders were playing the first few holes on the back nine.

Johnson — who eagled the par-4 second — birdied the par-4 11th to join Sabbatini at 12 under, and took the lead with a birdie on the par-4 13th.

Johnson played an aggressive line off the tee on the par-5 18th and reached the green in two. He two-putted from 35 feet for birdie — holing a 3-footer.

Stenson closed with a 68 playing alongside Johnson.

Alker had a 67. He was coming off three straight victories, one of them on the Legends Tour in Europe.

The players were paired with juniors of The First Tee program from chapters across the country.

title: Troy Melton injury update as Tigers RHP says 'twinges' chased him
description: Detroit Tigers righty Troy Melton exited Sunday in the fourth inning in Chicago, but he said he doesn't think it's a serious arm injury.
fullText:
CHICAGO – Detroit Tigers starting pitcher Troy Melton experienced forearm tightness and soreness in his throwing arm while pitching in the fourth inning against the Chicago White Sox on Sunday, Sept. 20.

He was taken out of the game and will undergo tests on Monday.

"It's just general tightness and soreness," Melton said after the Tigers lost 8-1 at Rate Field, ending any hopes of the postseason. "There are days where you get twinges like that, and it goes away. You don't think about it again. Then you do some work on it, and it's gone. It just never went away."

SUNDAY'S ACTION: Detroit Tigers playoff hopes end with soggy spanking in Chicago

Any issues with Melton's throwing arm raise instant concerns because he had issues earlier this season. Melton, 25, was diagnosed in late February with right elbow inflammation. He went on the 60-day injured list and returned to action May 24.

"It's hard without knowing exactly for sure what's going on, but I don't think they're related," Melton said. "As of what I know right now, I wouldn't say they're similar. I mean, obviously similar body part, I guess, but I don't think it's the same thing."

Melton was not sharp in this game. He threw just 47 of his 83 pitches for strikes. He said he started to feel the forearm issue while warming up before the fourth inning. "I kind of felt a little bit of tightness just in my forearm and kind of expected it to go away," he said. "It kind of just never did. It got achy and tight on me pretty quick and never got any better as the inning progressed. So just kind of stayed tight."

He tried to stretch out his arm on the mound. "Without raising super alarm flags," he said. "There was no individual pitch that set it off or anything like that."

Tigers catcher Eduardo Valencia noticed something wrong and went to the mound.

"I was good enough to go for the next hitter," Melton said. "I was just trying to get it to a place where it felt better, and just never did."

Tigers pitching coach Chris Fetter went out to the mound. As soon as Fetter heard about the arm issue, he motioned for Tigers manager A.J. Hinch and a trainer to come to the mound.

"Fett went out to just calm down the inning in the moment," Hinch said. "Then when Fett turned around, that's when I went out. So Troy just said he didn't feel great, so we're gonna get him checked out."

He will undergo tests on Monday.

"He reported some achiness and some issue with his arm, so I we're gonna get him checked out [Monday], kind of full examination," Hinch said. "As soon as he started saying he was uncomfortable, we took him out of the game. So I haven't seen him since, and we'll hope for the best tomorrow. But we'll see how the how the tests come back.

Melton was taken out with the White Sox holding a 3-0 lead. He threw 3⅔ innings, giving up four hits and four runs. He struck out four while walking three.

"I saw the non-command, but there was no issue until Fett motioned me out," Hinch said.

The game started after a 3-hour, 50-minute rain delay. With just a week left in the regular season and no shared open dates, they had to get this game in because the White Sox are fighting for the playoffs. So, they started in a rainstorm. It looked like it was raining sideways, as fans sat in the stands wearing ponchos and trash bags with holes cut out for the arms and head, and puddles formed around the edges of the field.

Melton did not feel the conditions played any role in his arm issue.

"I've pitched in the cold and the rain before," Melton said. "It's not like it was something that super affected me. But yeah, honestly, the mound held up pretty well. It wasn't too bad."

Melton, in his second big-league season, had something of a coming-out party, entering Sunday with a 2.52 ERA over 110⅔ innings with 90 strikeouts and 34 walks.
